e.en: He was arrested for {impersonating} a police officer online.
e.zh: 他因在网上冒充警察而被捕。

e.en: My nephew loves {impersonating} cartoon characters at parties.
e.zh: 我侄子喜欢在聚会上模仿卡通人物。

e.en: Her {impersonation} of the prime minister went viral overnight.
e.zh: 她对总理的模仿一夜之间走红网络。

e.en: Email {impersonation} attacks have doubled this year.
e.zh: 邮件冒充攻击今年翻了一番。

impersonations.t: n. 冒充；模仿表演（复数）

e.en: His {impersonations} of famous actors had the audience laughing.
e.zh: 他对著名演员的模仿让观众笑个不停。

e.en: AI voice {impersonations} are becoming alarmingly convincing.
e.zh: 人工智能语音模仿已经逼真到令人警觉的程度。

e.en: The Vegas show featured an Elvis {impersonator} in full costume.
e.zh: 这场拉斯维加斯表演有一位身着全套服装的猫王模仿者。

e.en: Police arrested an {impersonator} pretending to be a tax officer.
e.zh: 警方逮捕了一名假冒税务官员的人。

impersonators.t: n. 模仿者；冒充者（复数）

e.en: Beware of {impersonators} sending DMs that look like support staff.
e.zh: 小心那些发送私信冒充客服人员的骗子。

e.en: Several {impersonators} performed at the celebrity look-alike contest.
e.zh: 几位模仿者参加了明星模仿大赛。

e.en: The intern's {impertinence} surprised the senior partners.
e.zh: 实习生的无礼让高级合伙人们感到吃惊。

e.en: She apologized for the {impertinence} of her earlier question.
e.zh: 她为自己之前那个无礼的问题道歉。

e.en: It's {impertinent} to ask about a colleague's salary directly.
e.zh: 直接打听同事的薪水是很失礼的。

e.en: The reporter asked an {impertinent} question about her divorce.
e.zh: 记者就她的离婚提了一个无礼的问题。

imperturbable.t: adj. 沉着冷静的；不易激动的

e.en: The pilot remained {imperturbable} during the turbulence.
e.zh: 飞行员在颠簸中始终镇定自若。

e.en: Her {imperturbable} demeanor reassured the nervous clients.
e.zh: 她处变不惊的神态让紧张的客户安心了下来。

e.en: He answered the hostile questions {imperturbably} and smiled.
e.zh: 他从容不迫地回答着敌意的问题,还面带微笑。

e.en: The cat sat {imperturbably} as the puppy barked nearby.
e.zh: 小狗在旁边狂吠,猫却安然不动地坐着。

impervious.t: adj. 不受影响的；不可渗透的

e.en: The new coating is {impervious} to scratches and stains.
e.zh: 这种新涂层不会刮花也不会沾染污渍。

e.en: He seemed {impervious} to criticism from his rivals.
e.zh: 他似乎对对手的批评毫不在意。

impetigo.t: n. 脓疱病（一种皮肤病）

e.en: The doctor diagnosed the rash as {impetigo} and prescribed antibiotics.
e.zh: 医生诊断出这种皮疹是脓疱病,并开了抗生素。

e.en: {Impetigo} spreads quickly among children in daycare centers.
e.zh: 脓疱病在托儿所的孩子中传播得很快。

e.en: His {impetuosity} cost the team an important contract.
e.zh: 他的鲁莽冲动让团队失去了一份重要合同。

e.en: Youthful {impetuosity} sometimes leads to brilliant breakthroughs.
e.zh: 年轻时的冲动有时会带来惊人的突破。

e.en: Don't make {impetuous} decisions about quitting your job.
e.zh: 不要冲动地决定辞职。

e.en: Her {impetuous} reply got her into trouble with the client.
e.zh: 她冲动的回复让她和客户之间出了问题。

e.en: He {impetuously} bought the house without inspecting it first.
e.zh: 他没事先看房就冲动地买下了那栋房子。

e.en: She {impetuously} agreed to the deal before reading the terms.
e.zh: 她还没看条款就冲动地答应了这笔交易。

e.en: The new study gave fresh {impetus} to climate research.
e.zh: 这项新研究为气候研究注入了新的动力。

e.en: Customer complaints provided the {impetus} for redesigning the app.
e.zh: 客户的投诉成了重新设计这款应用的推动力。

e.en: The bishop accused the writer of {impiety} and blasphemy.
e.zh: 主教指责那位作家不敬神且亵渎神明。

e.en: His {impiety} toward family traditions shocked his grandmother.
e.zh: 他对家族传统的不敬让祖母大为震惊。

imping.t: v. 接羽（修补鸟类折断的羽毛）

e.en: Falconers practice {imping} to repair a hawk's broken feathers.
e.zh: 驯鹰人通过接羽术来修复鹰受损的羽毛。

e.en: The handler is {imping} new feathers onto the injured falcon's wing.
e.zh: 驯养员正在为受伤的猎鹰接上新羽毛。

e.en: New regulations may {impinge} on small business owners' freedoms.
e.zh: 新法规可能会侵犯小企业主的自由。

e.en: Bright sunlight began to {impinge} on the dim gallery space.
e.zh: 明亮的阳光开始照进昏暗的画廊空间。

e.en: The lawsuit alleges an {impingement} on free speech rights.
e.zh: 该诉讼指控此举侵犯了言论自由权。

e.en: Shoulder {impingement} causes pain when you lift your arm.
e.zh: 肩峰撞击综合征会在抬臂时引起疼痛。

e.en: The villagers considered his jokes about the temple {impious}.
e.zh: 村民认为他拿寺庙开的玩笑是不敬神的。

e.en: She gave an {impious} smirk during the solemn ceremony.
e.zh: 在庄严的仪式上她露出一抹不敬的冷笑。

e.en: The toddler flashed an {impish} grin before hiding the keys.
e.zh: 那个小孩调皮地一笑,然后把钥匙藏了起来。

e.en: Her {impish} sense of humor kept the whole office laughing.
e.zh: 她那顽皮的幽默感让整个办公室笑个不停。

e.en: He grinned {impishly} as he swapped the salt for sugar.
e.zh: 他调皮地咧嘴一笑,把盐换成了糖。

e.en: She winked {impishly} at her brother across the dinner table.
e.zh: 她隔着餐桌淘气地朝弟弟眨了眨眼。

e.en: The general was known for his {implacability} toward deserters.
e.zh: 这位将军以对逃兵毫不留情而闻名。

e.en: Her {implacability} in negotiations frustrated even seasoned diplomats.
e.zh: 她在谈判中的毫不妥协连资深外交官都感到无奈。

implacable.t: adj. 难以平息的；不可缓和的

e.en: He faces {implacable} opposition from every faction in parliament.
e.zh: 他在议会中遭到各派系毫不妥协的反对。

e.en: The judge has an {implacable} stance against drunk drivers.
e.zh: 法官对酒驾者持有毫不留情的立场。

implacably.t: adv. 执拗地；不可缓和地

e.en: She remained {implacably} opposed to selling the family home.
e.zh: 她坚决反对出售家族祖宅,毫不让步。

e.en: The critics were {implacably} hostile to his new film.
e.zh: 评论家们对他的新片抱有不可调和的敌意。

implant.t:
v. 植入；灌输
n. 植入物

e.en: Doctors will {implant} a small device to regulate her heartbeat.
e.zh: 医生将植入一个小装置来调节她的心跳。

e.en: The dental {implant} looks just like a real tooth.
e.zh: 这颗牙齿种植体看起来和真牙一模一样。

implantable.t: adj. 可植入的（医疗器械）

e.en: Researchers developed an {implantable} sensor that monitors blood sugar continuously.
e.zh: 研究人员开发出一种可植入传感器,能持续监测血糖。

e.en: The startup makes tiny {implantable} chips for medical tracking.
e.zh: 这家初创公司生产用于医疗追踪的微型可植入芯片。

e.en: Recovery after the {implantation} took just a few weeks.
e.zh: 植入手术后的恢复期只需要几周时间。

e.en: Successful {implantation} of the embryo marks the start of pregnancy.
e.zh: 胚胎成功着床标志着怀孕的开始。

implanted.t: v. 已植入（implant 的过去式）

e.en: The surgeon {implanted} a pacemaker to steady his heart rhythm.
e.zh: 外科医生植入了一台起搏器来稳定他的心律。

e.en: Childhood lessons {implanted} a deep love of reading in her.
e.zh: 童年的教导在她心中植入了对阅读的深爱。

implausibility.t: n. 难以置信；不合情理

e.en: Critics pointed out the {implausibility} of the movie's ending.
e.zh: 评论家们指出这部电影结局的不合理之处。

e.en: The {implausibility} of his alibi led detectives to dig deeper.
e.zh: 他不在场证明的不可信使侦探们深入调查。

implausible.t: adj. 难以置信的；不合情理的

e.en: His excuse for being late sounded completely {implausible}.
e.zh: 他迟到的借口听起来完全不可信。

e.en: The novel's plot is exciting but somewhat {implausible}.
e.zh: 这部小说情节精彩,但有些难以让人信服。

e.en: The hero {implausibly} survives a fall from the cliff.
e.zh: 主角难以置信地从悬崖坠落后竟然生还。

e.en: She {implausibly} claimed never to have seen the email.
e.zh: 她声称从未看过那封邮件,实在难以让人相信。

implement.t:
v. 实施；执行
n. 工具；器具

e.en: The team will {implement} the new payment system next month.
e.zh: 团队下个月将上线新的支付系统。

e.en: A hammer is the right {implement} for this job.
e.zh: 锤子是这项工作合适的工具。

implementation.t: n. 实施；执行；（代码）实现

e.en: The {implementation} of the new policy starts in January.
e.zh: 新政策将于一月开始实施。

e.en: This library offers a fast {implementation} of the sorting algorithm.
e.zh: 这个库提供了该排序算法的高效实现。

implementations.t: n. 实施；（代码）实现（复数）

e.en: Different {implementations} of the protocol can have varying performance characteristics.
e.zh: 该协议的不同实现可能具有不同的性能表现。

e.en: We compared three {implementations} before choosing the most efficient one.
e.zh: 我们比较了三种实现方案,最后选择了最高效的那个。

impassioned.t: adj. 充满激情的；慷慨激昂的

e.en: She gave an {impassioned} speech about climate justice.
e.zh: 她就气候正义发表了一场充满激情的演讲。

e.en: His {impassioned} plea convinced the jury to reconsider.
e.zh: 他充满激情的恳求让陪审团重新考虑。

impassive.t: adj. 面无表情的；无动于衷的

e.en: The guard's face stayed {impassive} as tourists shouted.
e.zh: 游客们大喊大叫时,卫兵的脸依然毫无表情。

e.en: She listened to the bad news with an {impassive} stare.
e.zh: 她以面无表情的眼神听完了那则坏消息。

impassively.t: adv. 面无表情地；无动于衷地

e.en: He stared {impassively} at the screen during the layoff call.
e.zh: 在裁员通话中,他面无表情地盯着屏幕。

e.en: The CEO answered the tough questions {impassively}.
e.zh: 首席执行官面不改色地回答了那些尖锐的问题。

impassivity.t: n. 无动于衷；面无表情

e.en: His {impassivity} during the argument frustrated his partner.
e.zh: 他在争吵中无动于衷的态度让伴侣很沮丧。

e.en: The dealer's {impassivity} made it impossible to read him.
e.zh: 那位发牌员毫无表情,让人完全猜不透他。

impasto.t: n. (绘画) 厚涂颜料技法

e.en: Van Gogh used thick {impasto} to give his skies texture.
e.zh: 梵高用厚涂法让天空充满了肌理感。

e.en: She built up the petals with bold strokes of {impasto}.
e.zh: 她用大胆的厚涂笔触堆塑出花瓣。

e.en: His {impatience} with slow loading times is hurting the product.
e.zh: 他对加载缓慢的不耐烦正在伤害这款产品。

e.en: You could hear the {impatience} in her voice on the call.
e.zh: 你能从她通话的语气中听出焦躁。

e.en: She planted bright pink {impatiens} along the shady walkway.
e.zh: 她在阴凉的小路边种上了鲜艳的粉色凤仙花。

e.en: {Impatiens} thrive in pots that get morning sun only.
e.zh: 凤仙花在只见晨光的花盆里长得很好。

e.en: Customers grow {impatient} when checkout takes more than a minute.
e.zh: 如果结账超过一分钟,顾客就会变得不耐烦。

e.en: He was {impatient} to start his new job in Tokyo.
e.zh: 他迫不及待地想去东京开始新工作。

e.en: She tapped her foot {impatiently} while waiting for the bus.
e.zh: 她一边等公交车,一边不耐烦地用脚打着拍子。

e.en: The dog scratched the door {impatiently} to be let out.
e.zh: 狗不耐烦地抓挠着门,想要出去。

e.en: Congress voted to {impeach} the president for abuse of power.
e.zh: 国会投票弹劾总统,指控其滥用职权。

e.en: The defense tried to {impeach} the witness's credibility.
e.zh: 辩方试图质疑这名证人的可信度。

impeachable.t: adj. 可被弹劾的；应受控告的

e.en: Lying under oath is clearly an {impeachable} offense.
e.zh: 宣誓后作伪证显然属于可被弹劾的罪行。

e.en: Legal experts debated whether the conduct was {impeachable}.
e.zh: 法律专家就该行为是否可被弹劾展开了辩论。

impeached.t: v. 被弹劾（impeach 的过去式）

e.en: The governor was {impeached} but later acquitted by the senate.
e.zh: 州长遭到弹劾,但后来被参议院判无罪。

e.en: Only three U.S. presidents have ever been {impeached}.
e.zh: 美国历史上仅有三位总统曾被弹劾。

e.en: The {impeachment} hearings were broadcast live on every channel.
e.zh: 弹劾听证会在各大电视台进行了直播。

e.en: Cable news covered the {impeachment} vote for hours.
e.zh: 有线新闻台对那场弹劾投票进行了数小时的报道。

impeccable.t: adj. 完美无瑕的；无可挑剔的

e.en: Her English is {impeccable} after just two years abroad.
e.zh: 她出国才两年,英语就已无可挑剔。

e.en: The hotel offered {impeccable} service from check-in to checkout.
e.zh: 酒店从入住到退房都提供了无可挑剔的服务。

impeccably.t: adv. 无可挑剔地；完美无缺地

e.en: He was always {impeccably} dressed for client meetings.
e.zh: 他每次见客户时穿着都无可挑剔。

e.en: The waiter handled the spilled wine {impeccably}.
e.zh: 服务员处理那杯洒落的红酒处理得无懈可击。

impecunious.t: adj. 身无分文的；贫困的

e.en: As an {impecunious} student, she lived on instant noodles.
e.zh: 作为一名穷学生,她靠方便面度日。

e.en: The {impecunious} writer slept on a friend's couch for months.
e.zh: 那位身无分文的作家在朋友的沙发上睡了好几个月。

e.en: Match the speaker's {impedance} to the amplifier for clean sound.
e.zh: 将音箱的阻抗与功放匹配,才能获得干净的音质。

e.en: The engineer measured the cable's {impedance} at one ohm.
e.zh: 工程师测得那根电缆的阻抗为一欧姆。

e.en: Heavy regulation can {impede} innovation in early-stage startups.
e.zh: 过多的监管会阻碍初创企业早期阶段的创新。

e.en: Don't let perfectionism {impede} shipping the first version.
e.zh: 别让完美主义阻碍你发布第一个版本。

impeded.t: v. 被阻碍（impede 的过去式）

e.en: Construction noise {impeded} the team's focus all morning.
e.zh: 施工的噪音整个上午都干扰着团队的专注。

e.en: Bad weather seriously {impeded} the rescue operation in the mountains.
e.zh: 恶劣天气严重阻碍了山区的救援行动。

impedes.t: v. 阻碍（impede 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A cluttered interface {impedes} the user from finding key features.
e.zh: 杂乱的界面会妨碍用户找到关键功能。

e.en: Fear of failure often {impedes} creative risk-taking.
e.zh: 对失败的恐惧常常阻碍人们去做有创意的冒险。

impediment.t:
n. 障碍；妨碍
n. 口吃等生理缺陷

e.en: Her speech {impediment} disappeared after a year of therapy.
e.zh: 经过一年的治疗,她的语言障碍消失了。

e.en: Slow internet was the biggest {impediment} to remote work.
e.zh: 网速慢是远程办公最大的障碍。

impedimenta.t: n. 累赘的行李；随军辎重

e.en: The hikers ditched their heavy {impedimenta} before the final climb.
e.zh: 在最后的攀登前,徒步者们丢下了沉重的随身行李。

e.en: Travel light and leave the {impedimenta} of daily life behind.
e.zh: 轻装出行,把日常生活的累赘抛在身后。

e.en: The team listed the technical {impediments} blocking the launch.
e.zh: 团队列出了阻碍发布的各项技术障碍。

e.en: There are no legal {impediments} to signing the contract today.
e.zh: 今天签订合同没有任何法律障碍。

impeding.t:
adj. 妨碍的
v. 阻碍（现在分词）

e.en: Old company policies are {impeding} the move to remote work.
e.zh: 陈旧的公司制度正在阻碍向远程办公的转型。

e.en: Stop {impeding} traffic and pull your car over to the side.
e.zh: 别再阻碍交通了,把车靠边停。

e.en: Curiosity should {impel} you to ask one more question.
e.zh: 好奇心应该促使你再多问一个问题。

e.en: Rising costs may {impel} the company to raise prices.
e.zh: 成本上涨可能迫使公司提高价格。

impelled.t: v. 驱使（impel 的过去式）

e.en: A sense of duty {impelled} her to report the data leak.
e.zh: 一种责任感驱使她举报了那起数据泄露。

e.en: He felt {impelled} to apologize after watching the video.
e.zh: 看完那段视频后,他觉得不得不道歉。

e.en: A worn pump {impeller} is causing the low water pressure.
e.zh: 水泵叶轮磨损是水压不足的原因。

e.en: The mechanic replaced the cracked {impeller} in the boat engine.
e.zh: 机修工更换了船用发动机里破裂的叶轮。

e.en: Storm clouds {impend} over the valley as we set up camp.
e.zh: 我们扎营时,乌云正笼罩在山谷上方。

e.en: Major layoffs seem to {impend} at the struggling startup.
e.zh: 这家陷入困境的初创公司似乎即将进行大规模裁员。

impending.t: adj. 即将来临的；迫在眉睫的

e.en: Everyone felt the weight of the {impending} deadline.
e.zh: 每个人都感受到了即将到来的截止日期带来的压力。

e.en: Dark clouds warned of an {impending} thunderstorm.
e.zh: 乌云预示着一场即将到来的雷暴。

impenetrability.t: n. 不可穿透性；难以理解

e.en: The {impenetrability} of the code frustrated even senior developers.
e.zh: 这段代码的晦涩难懂连资深开发者都感到沮丧。

e.en: Scientists tested the {impenetrability} of the new armor material.
e.zh: 科学家测试了这种新型装甲材料的不可穿透性。

impenetrable.t: adj. 无法穿透的；难以理解的

e.en: The forest was dark and {impenetrable} after sunset.
e.zh: 日落后这片森林漆黑一片,无法穿越。

e.en: His legal contracts are {impenetrable} to ordinary readers.
e.zh: 他的法律合同对普通读者来说晦涩难懂。

impenetrably.t: adv. 无法穿透地；费解地

e.en: The fog hung {impenetrably} over the harbor all morning.
e.zh: 整个上午,浓雾密不透风地笼罩着港口。

e.en: The manual was {impenetrably} written in dense jargon.
e.zh: 这本手册写得满是术语,令人完全看不懂。

impenitent.t: adj. 不知悔改的；顽固的

e.en: The {impenitent} thief showed no remorse during sentencing.
e.zh: 这名毫无悔意的小偷在宣判时没有表现出任何悔过。

e.en: She remained {impenitent} despite the public backlash.
e.zh: 尽管受到公众强烈反对,她依然毫无悔意。

imperative.t:
adj. 必要的；紧迫的
n. 必要的事；命令

e.en: It's {imperative} that we back up the database before deployment.
e.zh: 在部署前备份数据库是绝对必要的。

e.en: Use the {imperative} mood when writing button labels.
e.zh: 撰写按钮文案时要使用祈使语气。

imperatives.t: n. 必要的事；命令（复数）

e.en: Climate change creates new {imperatives} for global cooperation.
e.zh: 气候变化为全球合作带来了新的迫切要求。

e.en: Business {imperatives} sometimes conflict with employee well-being.
e.zh: 商业上的迫切需求有时会与员工福祉产生冲突。

imperceptible.t: adj. 难以察觉的；细微的

e.en: The temperature drop was {imperceptible} until I checked the thermostat.
e.zh: 温度的下降几乎察觉不到,直到我看了恒温器才发现。

e.en: She gave an almost {imperceptible} nod of approval.
e.zh: 她几乎不易察觉地点了点头表示同意。

imperceptibly.t: adv. 难以察觉地；细微地

e.en: The shoreline is shifting {imperceptibly} year after year.
e.zh: 海岸线正以人眼难以察觉的速度逐年变化。

e.en: His mood changed {imperceptibly} as the meeting wore on.
e.zh: 会议持续进行,他的情绪在不知不觉中发生了变化。

imperfect.t: adj. 有缺陷的；不完善的

e.en: The app launched with an {imperfect} but usable interface.
e.zh: 这款应用上线时界面虽不完美但可以使用。

e.en: Spanish has a separate {imperfect} tense for past habits.
e.zh: 西班牙语有一种专门表示过去习惯的未完成时态。

e.en: Every handmade ceramic has some small {imperfection}.
e.zh: 每一件手工陶器都有一些小瑕疵。

e.en: He learned to embrace {imperfection} in his creative work.
e.zh: 他学会了在创作中接受不完美。

imperfectly.t: adv. 不完美地；有缺陷地

e.en: The translation captured the joke only {imperfectly}.
e.zh: 这个翻译只是不完整地传达了笑话的笑点。

e.en: The door closed {imperfectly}, leaving a small gap.
e.zh: 门没关严,留下了一道小缝。

e.en: The museum displays artifacts from China's {imperial} era.
e.zh: 博物馆展出中国帝制时期的文物。

e.en: Americans still measure distance in {imperial} units like miles.
e.zh: 美国人仍然用英里这样的英制单位来测量距离。

e.en: The course covers European {imperialism} in nineteenth-century Africa.
e.zh: 这门课程讲述十九世纪欧洲在非洲的帝国主义扩张。

e.en: Critics accused the tech giant of cultural {imperialism}.
e.zh: 批评人士指责这家科技巨头推行文化帝国主义。

imperialist.t:
n. 帝国主义者
adj. 帝国主义的

e.en: The novel critiques the {imperialist} mindset of its era.
e.zh: 这部小说批判了那个时代的帝国主义心态。

e.en: She studied {imperialist} expansion across Southeast Asia.
e.zh: 她研究了帝国主义在东南亚的扩张。

e.en: The country's {imperialistic} ambitions worried its neighbors.
e.zh: 这个国家的帝国主义野心令周边国家感到担忧。

e.en: He criticized the company's {imperialistic} approach to new markets.
e.zh: 他批评这家公司进入新市场时采取的帝国主义式做法。

e.en: She waved {imperially} at the waiter from across the room.
e.zh: 她从房间另一头以居高临下的姿态向服务员招手。

e.en: The CEO gestured {imperially} for everyone to sit down.
e.zh: CEO 摆出威严的姿态示意大家坐下。

e.en: Skipping security updates can {imperil} user data.
e.zh: 不安装安全更新可能会危及用户数据。

e.en: Reckless spending could {imperil} the entire startup.
e.zh: 鲁莽的支出可能会危及整家初创公司。

imperiled.t: v. 危及（imperil 的过去式）

e.en: Conservation laws protect {imperiled} species from extinction.
e.zh: 保护法保护濒危物种免于灭绝。

e.en: The leak {imperiled} the company's upcoming product launch.
e.zh: 这次泄露危及了公司即将到来的产品发布。

e.en: The manager spoke in an {imperious} tone that annoyed everyone.
e.zh: 经理说话语气专横,惹恼了所有人。

e.en: She gave him an {imperious} look and walked away.
e.zh: 她傲慢地瞥了他一眼便走开了。

e.en: He pointed {imperiously} at the door and demanded silence.
e.zh: 他傲慢地指向门口,要求大家安静。

e.en: The director addressed the interns {imperiously} during the meeting.
e.zh: 会议期间,主管以居高临下的口吻对实习生讲话。

e.en: His {imperiousness} alienated half the engineering team.
e.zh: 他的专横态度让工程团队的一半人都疏远了他。

e.en: There was an {imperiousness} in her voice that silenced critics.
e.zh: 她声音中的威严气势让批评者们都沉默了。

e.en: Heavy {impost} duties discouraged merchants from trading there.
e.zh: 沉重的关税让商人不愿在那里交易。

e.en: The horse carried a heavy {impost} in yesterday's race.
e.zh: 那匹马在昨天的比赛中负重很大。

e.en: The {imposter} pretended to be a doctor for years.
e.zh: 那个冒名顶替者多年来一直假扮医生。

e.en: Many new engineers struggle with {imposter} syndrome at work.
e.zh: 许多新工程师在工作中受冒名顶替综合症困扰。

e.en: The {impostor} fooled investors out of millions of dollars.
e.zh: 那个骗子骗取了投资者数百万美元。

e.en: She often feels like an {impostor} despite her achievements.
e.zh: 尽管成就斐然,她仍常觉得自己是个冒牌货。

imposture.t: n. 冒名顶替；欺诈行为

e.en: His elaborate {imposture} as a prince was finally exposed.
e.zh: 他精心伪装成王子的骗局终于被揭穿。

e.en: The journalist uncovered an {imposture} at the charity organization.
e.zh: 那位记者揭露了慈善机构的一场冒名顶替。

e.en: He felt deep {impotence} watching the disaster unfold on TV.
e.zh: 看着电视里灾难发生,他感到深深的无力。

e.en: The senator criticized the committee's {impotence} on climate issues.
e.zh: 参议员批评委员会在气候问题上的无能为力。

e.en: The general's {impotency} in battle cost the kingdom dearly.
e.zh: 将军在战场上的无能让王国付出了惨重代价。

e.en: She wrote about the {impotency} of words in moments of grief.
e.zh: 她写下了悲痛时刻言语的无力。

e.en: Local police felt {impotent} against the powerful criminal gang.
e.zh: 当地警方在强大的犯罪团伙面前感到无能为力。

e.en: The old laws are {impotent} in the age of the internet.
e.zh: 在互联网时代,旧法律已无能为力。

e.en: He watched {impotently} as the flames consumed his home.
e.zh: 他无助地看着火焰吞噬了自己的家。

e.en: The minister gestured {impotently} at the angry crowd.
e.zh: 部长无力地朝愤怒的人群挥了挥手。

impound.t: v. 扣押；没收（车辆、财物）

e.en: Police can {impound} your car if you park illegally.
e.zh: 如果违规停车,警察可以扣押你的车。

e.en: Customs officers may {impound} undeclared goods at the border.
e.zh: 海关可在边境扣押未申报的货物。

impounded.t: v. 被扣押（impound 的过去式）

e.en: My car was {impounded} after I missed three parking tickets.
e.zh: 我漏交了三张停车罚单,车被扣了。

e.en: The court {impounded} the evidence pending further investigation.
e.zh: 法院扣押了证据,等待进一步调查。

e.en: You'll pay a fee to release your car from {impoundment}.
e.zh: 你需要交一笔费用才能把车从扣押场领回。

e.en: The {impoundment} of the funds delayed the housing project.
e.zh: 资金被冻结导致住房项目延期。

e.en: Long wars tend to {impoverish} entire generations of citizens.
e.zh: 长期战争往往会使几代人陷入贫困。

e.en: Cutting arts education would {impoverish} our children's future.
e.zh: 削减艺术教育会让孩子们的未来变得贫乏。

e.en: The charity supports {impoverished} families in rural areas.
e.zh: 该慈善机构帮助农村地区的贫困家庭。

e.en: Years of drought {impoverished} the farming community.
e.zh: 多年的干旱使这个农业社区陷入贫困。

e.en: The crisis led to widespread {impoverishment} across the region.
e.zh: 那场危机导致整个地区普遍陷入贫困。

e.en: Censorship causes a real {impoverishment} of public discourse.
e.zh: 审查制度使公共讨论真正变得贫乏。

e.en: Engineers pointed out the {impracticability} of the original design.
e.zh: 工程师指出了原始设计的不可行性。

e.en: The plan was abandoned due to its sheer {impracticability}.
e.zh: 该计划因完全不可行而被放弃。

impracticable.t: adj. 行不通的；难实施的

e.en: Building a tunnel here would be financially {impracticable}.
e.zh: 在这里修隧道在经济上是行不通的。

e.en: Their proposal sounds nice but is largely {impracticable}.
e.zh: 他们的提议听起来不错,但基本上行不通。

impractical.t: adj. 不切实际的；不实用的

e.en: High heels are {impractical} for hiking up muddy trails.
e.zh: 穿高跟鞋走泥泞的山路很不实用。

e.en: His ideas are creative but often {impractical} in real projects.
e.zh: 他的点子很有创意,但在实际项目中往往不切实际。

e.en: The {impracticality} of the schedule became obvious within a week.
e.zh: 这个时间表的不切实际一周内就显而易见。

e.en: Critics pointed out the {impracticality} of remote-only teams.
e.zh: 批评者指出了完全远程团队的不切实际。

e.en: The angry villagers began to {imprecate} curses upon the thief.
e.zh: 愤怒的村民们开始诅咒那个小偷。

e.en: She would often {imprecate} bad luck on her rivals.
e.zh: 她常常诅咒对手倒霉。

e.en: He muttered an {imprecation} when his code wouldn't compile.
e.zh: 代码编译不过时,他咒骂了一句。

e.en: The old wizard hurled an {imprecation} at the invading army.
e.zh: 老巫师对入侵的军队下了一道诅咒。

imprecise.t: adj. 不精确的；不准确的

e.en: The instructions were too {imprecise} for me to follow.
e.zh: 说明太不精确,我没法照着做。

e.en: His memory of that night is {imprecise} after so many years.
e.zh: 过了这么多年,他对那晚的记忆已经模糊。

e.en: The term "AI" is often used {imprecisely} in marketing.
e.zh: "人工智能"这个词在营销中常被不严谨地使用。

e.en: He {imprecisely} estimated the distance at about ten miles.
e.zh: 他大致估计距离约为十英里。

e.en: The {imprecision} of the data made our analysis unreliable.
e.zh: 数据的不精确使我们的分析不可靠。

e.en: Legal documents leave little room for {imprecision}.
e.zh: 法律文件几乎不允许有任何不精确之处。

impregnable.t: adj. 坚不可摧的；无懈可击的

e.en: The medieval fortress was considered {impregnable} for centuries.
e.zh: 那座中世纪要塞数百年来被视为坚不可摧。

e.en: No system is truly {impregnable} to a determined hacker.
e.zh: 没有任何系统能真正抵挡住执着的黑客。

e.en: You can {impregnate} the wood with oil to waterproof it.
e.zh: 你可以用油浸渍木头使其防水。

e.en: Scientists managed to {impregnate} the panda through artificial means.
e.zh: 科学家通过人工方式让那只熊猫成功怀孕。

e.en: The cloth was {impregnated} with a special insect repellent.
e.zh: 这块布浸渍了一种特殊的驱虫剂。

e.en: The cake was {impregnated} with rum and orange syrup.
e.zh: 这块蛋糕浸透了朗姆酒和橙汁糖浆。

e.en: The {impregnation} of the fabric makes it fully waterproof.
e.zh: 这种浸渍处理让布料完全防水。

e.en: Successful {impregnation} of pandas in captivity remains rare.
e.zh: 圈养熊猫成功受孕的情况仍然罕见。

impresario.t: n. 剧团经理；演出策划人

e.en: The famous {impresario} brought the ballet company to New York.
e.zh: 那位著名的演出经理人把这家芭蕾舞团带到了纽约。

e.en: She became a leading {impresario} in the indie music scene.
e.zh: 她成为独立音乐界举足轻重的演出经纪人。

e.en: Several {impresarioes} competed to sign the rising opera star.
e.zh: 几位演出经纪人争相签下那位崭露头角的歌剧明星。

e.en: The festival attracts {impresarioes} from across Europe each summer.
e.zh: 这个艺术节每年夏天都吸引来自欧洲各地的演出经纪人。

impress.t: v. 给…留下深刻印象；使铭记

e.en: She wore her best suit to {impress} the interviewer.
e.zh: 她穿上最好的西装,想给面试官留下好印象。

e.en: The kid's piano skills really {impress} everyone at the party.
e.zh: 这孩子的钢琴技巧让聚会上的每个人都惊叹。

impressed.t: adj. 印象深刻的；钦佩的

e.en: I was {impressed} by her quick thinking during the meeting.
e.zh: 她在会议上反应敏捷，让我印象深刻。

e.en: The teacher {impressed} the importance of practice on her students.
e.zh: 老师向学生强调了练习的重要性。

impresses.t: v. impress 的第三人称单数

e.en: His latest album {impresses} both critics and fans alike.
e.zh: 他的最新专辑让乐评人和粉丝都赞不绝口。

e.en: Nothing {impresses} my grandfather more than honest hard work.
e.zh: 没有什么比踏实肯干更让我爷爷欣赏了。

e.en: She kept {impressing} the deadline on the whole team.
e.zh: 她不断向整个团队强调截止日期的重要性。

e.en: He spent the whole evening {impressing} his date with magic tricks.
e.zh: 他整晚都用魔术来打动他的约会对象。

impression.t:
n. 印象；感想
n. 压痕；模仿

e.en: My first {impression} of the city was overwhelmingly positive.
e.zh: 我对这座城市的第一印象非常好。

e.en: His comedian friend does a hilarious {impression} of the president.
e.zh: 他那位喜剧演员朋友模仿总统模仿得超搞笑。

impressionable.t: adj. 易受影响的；敏感的

e.en: Social media has a strong effect on {impressionable} young teens.
e.zh: 社交媒体对易受影响的青少年有很大作用。

e.en: At that {impressionable} age, every book felt life-changing.
e.zh: 在那个易受感染的年纪，每本书都像能改变人生。

e.en: Monet is widely regarded as the father of {impressionism}.
e.zh: 莫奈被普遍认为是印象派之父。

e.en: The museum's new wing focuses entirely on French {impressionism}.
e.zh: 博物馆的新展厅完全聚焦于法国印象派。

e.en: The exhibit compares European and Japanese {impressionisms} side by side.
e.zh: 展览将欧洲和日本的印象派艺术并列对比。

e.en: Different {impressionisms} emerged across regions in the late nineteenth century.
e.zh: 十九世纪末各地涌现出不同流派的印象主义。

impressionist.t: n. 印象派画家；模仿艺人

e.en: She bought a small {impressionist} painting at the auction.
e.zh: 她在拍卖会上买下一幅小幅印象派画作。

e.en: The {impressionist} on TV does a perfect Obama voice.
e.zh: 电视上那位模仿者把奥巴马的声音学得惟妙惟肖。

impressionistic.t: adj. 印象派的；凭印象的

e.en: His review was {impressionistic} rather than based on hard data.
e.zh: 他的评论偏印象式，而不是基于硬数据。

e.en: The film uses {impressionistic} lighting to evoke childhood memories.
e.zh: 这部电影用印象派式的光影唤起童年回忆。

impressionistically.t: adv. 凭印象地；印象派式地

e.en: The novelist describes Tokyo {impressionistically}, focusing on mood over detail.
e.zh: 小说家以印象式笔法描绘东京，重氛围而非细节。

e.en: She painted the harbor {impressionistically}, capturing only the light.
e.zh: 她以印象派手法画港口，只捕捉光影。

e.en: The {impressionists} broke away from academic painting traditions in Paris.
e.zh: 印象派画家们打破了巴黎学院派的绘画传统。

e.en: Stand-up {impressionists} can imitate dozens of celebrity voices on demand.
e.zh: 模仿秀演员能随时模仿数十位名人的声音。

e.en: The ad got over a million {impressions} in a single day.
e.zh: 这则广告一天内获得了超过一百万次曝光。

e.en: First {impressions} matter a lot in job interviews.
e.zh: 在求职面试中，第一印象非常重要。

impressive.t: adj. 令人印象深刻的；出色的

e.en: That's an {impressive} score for your first attempt.
e.zh: 对于第一次尝试来说，这个分数相当出色。

e.en: The skyline of Shanghai is genuinely {impressive} at night.
e.zh: 上海的夜景天际线确实令人叹为观止。

impressively.t: adv. 令人印象深刻地；出色地

e.en: She handled the difficult question {impressively} during the press conference.
e.zh: 她在新闻发布会上处理那个棘手问题处理得令人佩服。

e.en: The startup grew {impressively} fast in its first two years.
e.zh: 这家初创公司前两年增长得惊人地快。

impressment.t: n. 强征入伍；强行征用

e.en: British {impressment} of American sailors helped trigger the War of 1812.
e.zh: 英国强征美国水手是1812年战争爆发的导火索之一。

e.en: Naval {impressment} was a brutal practice common in the 1700s.
e.zh: 海军强征兵役是十八世纪常见的残酷做法。

imprimatur.t: n. 出版许可；官方认可

e.en: The proposal needs the CEO's {imprimatur} before it can move forward.
e.zh: 这项提案需要CEO的认可才能推进。

e.en: Getting Oprah's {imprimatur} can turn any book into a bestseller.
e.zh: 得到奥普拉的背书能让任何一本书成为畅销书。

e.en: The artist applied a warm {imprimatura} before sketching the figure.
e.zh: 画家在勾勒人物前先涂了一层暖色底层。

e.en: A thin {imprimatura} unifies the underpainting and gives depth.
e.zh: 薄薄一层底色能统一底稿并增加层次感。

imprint.t:
n. 印记；烙印
v. 铭刻；压印

e.en: The book was published under a small literary {imprint}.
e.zh: 这本书是由一家小型文学出版品牌发行的。

e.en: Childhood experiences {imprint} themselves on our memory forever.
e.zh: 童年经历会永远烙印在我们的记忆里。

e.en: Her father's words are {imprinted} on her memory.
e.zh: 父亲的那些话深深刻在她的记忆中。

e.en: The duckling {imprinted} on the first human it saw.
e.zh: 那只小鸭子把它见到的第一个人当成了妈妈。

imprinting.t:
n. 印刻效应；铭印
v. 铭刻

e.en: Newborn ducklings undergo {imprinting} within hours of hatching.
e.zh: 刚孵化的小鸭子在几小时内就会形成印随行为。

e.en: The factory is {imprinting} serial numbers on every component.
e.zh: 工厂正在每个零件上压印序列号。

implemented.t: v. 实现；执行（implement 的过去式）

e.en: The company {implemented} a four-day workweek last quarter.
e.zh: 公司上个季度实施了每周四天工作制。

e.en: She {implemented} the login feature in just two days.
e.zh: 她仅用两天就实现了登录功能。

e.en: As the lead {implementer}, she rewrote half the codebase.
e.zh: 作为首席实施者,她重写了一半的代码库。

e.en: The framework's original {implementer} answered our questions on GitHub.
e.zh: 该框架的最初开发者在 GitHub 上回答了我们的问题。

implementing.t: v. 正在实施、执行（implement 的现在分词）

e.en: We are {implementing} dark mode across all our mobile apps.
e.zh: 我们正在所有移动应用中实现深色模式。

e.en: The school is {implementing} stricter rules around phone use.
e.zh: 学校正在执行更严格的手机使用规定。

implements.t:
v. 实现；执行
n. 工具；器具

e.en: This class {implements} the standard Iterator interface in Java.
e.zh: 这个类实现了 Java 中标准的迭代器接口。

e.en: The chef arranged her cooking {implements} neatly on the counter.
e.zh: 厨师把她的烹饪器具整齐地摆在台面上。

e.en: The new evidence may {implicate} two more senior executives.
e.zh: 新证据可能会牵连另外两名高层管理人员。

e.en: He refused to {implicate} his colleagues in the scheme.
e.zh: 他拒绝把同事牵扯进这起阴谋中。

e.en: Three officials were {implicated} in the corruption scandal.
e.zh: 三名官员被卷入了这起腐败丑闻。

e.en: Stress is often {implicated} in many chronic health problems.
e.zh: 压力常被认为与许多慢性健康问题有关。

implicates.t: v. 牵连；暗示（第三人称单数）

e.en: The leaked email {implicates} the CEO in the cover-up.
e.zh: 这封泄露的邮件将首席执行官牵连进了掩盖事件。

e.en: This study {implicates} sugar in rising obesity rates.
e.zh: 这项研究指出糖与肥胖率上升有关。

e.en: Witnesses gave testimony {implicating} the manager in the fraud.
e.zh: 证人提供了将经理卷入诈骗案的证词。

e.en: The report stops short of {implicating} any specific officer.
e.zh: 报告没有具体牵连任何一位警官。

implication.t: n. 暗示；（可能的）影响、后果

e.en: The {implication} of his comment was that we were lying.
e.zh: 他话中的意思是我们在撒谎。

e.en: This decision has serious {implication} for the entire industry.
e.zh: 这个决定对整个行业有重大影响。

e.en: The privacy {implications} of this app worry many users.
e.zh: 这款应用的隐私影响让许多用户感到担忧。

e.en: We need to consider the legal {implications} before signing.
e.zh: 我们需要在签字前考虑法律层面的影响。

e.en: Linguists study how {implicature} lets speakers mean more than they say.
e.zh: 语言学家研究会话含义如何让说话者的意思超出字面。

e.en: Her response carried an {implicature} that she disapproved.
e.zh: 她的回答暗含着她并不赞同的意思。

implicit.t: adj. 隐含的；隐式的（编程）

e.en: There was an {implicit} agreement that no one would speak publicly.
e.zh: 大家心照不宣地达成共识,谁也不会公开发言。

e.en: She has {implicit} trust in her doctor's judgment.
e.zh: 她对医生的判断有着绝对的信任。

e.en: By staying silent, the manager {implicitly} approved the plan.
e.zh: 经理保持沉默,等于默许了这项计划。

e.en: Children {implicitly} learn grammar long before they study it formally.
e.zh: 孩子们在正式学习语法之前,就已潜移默化地掌握了它。

implied.t:
adj. 暗示的；含蓄的
v. 暗示（imply 的过去式）

e.en: Her tone {implied} that she didn't believe a word.
e.zh: 她的语气暗示她一个字也不相信。

e.en: There is an {implied} warranty on every appliance we sell.
e.zh: 我们出售的每件电器都附带默示保修。

e.en: The contract {impliedly} obligates both parties to act in good faith.
e.zh: 该合同默示双方都有诚信履约的义务。

e.en: By accepting the gift, he {impliedly} agreed to the terms.
e.zh: 接受礼物的行为意味着他默示同意了条款。

implies.t: v. 暗示；意味着（第三人称单数）

e.en: His silence {implies} that he agrees with the proposal.
e.zh: 他的沉默意味着他同意这项提议。

e.en: The data {implies} a strong link between sleep and memory.
e.zh: 数据表明睡眠与记忆之间存在密切联系。

e.en: The startup began to {implode} after losing its main investor.
e.zh: 这家初创公司在失去主要投资人后开始崩溃。

e.en: Engineers used charges to {implode} the old stadium safely.
e.zh: 工程师使用炸药安全地内爆拆除了旧体育场。

e.en: His career is {imploding} after the scandal broke last week.
e.zh: 丑闻上周曝光后,他的事业正在土崩瓦解。

e.en: The submarine risked {imploding} under the immense ocean pressure.
e.zh: 在巨大的海洋压力下,潜艇有内爆的危险。

e.en: I {implore} you to reconsider before making this decision.
e.zh: 我恳求你在做出这个决定之前再考虑一下。

e.en: The villagers {implore} the government for clean drinking water.
e.zh: 村民们恳求政府提供干净的饮用水。

imploring.t:
adj. 恳求的
v. 正在恳求

e.en: She gave him an {imploring} look across the crowded room.
e.zh: 她隔着拥挤的房间向他投去恳求的目光。

e.en: He kept {imploring} his boss to extend the deadline.
e.zh: 他不停地恳求老板延长截止日期。

e.en: The dog gazed {imploringly} at the leftover pizza.
e.zh: 那只狗用恳求的眼神盯着剩下的披萨。

e.en: She looked {imploringly} at her father, hoping he would relent.
e.zh: 她哀求地望着父亲,希望他能心软。

e.en: The team's sudden {implosion} cost them the championship.
e.zh: 球队的突然崩盘让他们失去了冠军。

e.en: Engineers triggered a controlled {implosion} of the abandoned tower.
e.zh: 工程师对那座废弃高塔进行了受控内爆拆除。

e.en: I didn't mean to {imply} that your work was sloppy.
e.zh: 我并不是想暗示你的工作很草率。

e.en: These results {imply} that the drug works as expected.
e.zh: 这些结果表明该药物的效果符合预期。

e.en: Are you {implying} that I cheated on the exam?
e.zh: 你是在暗示我考试作弊吗?

e.en: The headline is {implying} a connection that doesn't actually exist.
e.zh: 这个标题暗示了一种实际上并不存在的关联。

e.en: It's considered {impolite} to check your phone during dinner.
e.zh: 在晚餐时看手机被认为是不礼貌的行为。

e.en: He apologized for his {impolite} remarks at the meeting.
e.zh: 他为自己在会上不礼貌的言论道了歉。

e.en: She {impolitely} interrupted the speaker mid-sentence.
e.zh: 她不礼貌地打断了发言人的话。

e.en: He yawned {impolitely} during his colleague's presentation.
e.zh: 他在同事做报告时不礼貌地打了个哈欠。

e.en: It would be {impolitic} to criticize the boss in public.
e.zh: 在公开场合批评老板是不明智的。

e.en: His {impolitic} tweet cost the campaign several key donors.
e.zh: 他那条欠考虑的推文让竞选团队失去了几位重要捐款人。

imponderable.t:
adj. 难以估量的
n. 难以估量的事物

e.en: The long-term effects of the new policy remain {imponderable}.
e.zh: 新政策的长期影响仍然难以估量。

e.en: There are too many {imponderable} factors in this forecast.
e.zh: 这份预测中有太多无法衡量的因素。

import.t:
v. 导入（模块、文件）；进口
n. 进口商品

e.en: You can {import} contacts directly from your Gmail account.
e.zh: 你可以直接从 Gmail 账户中导入联系人。

e.en: China is the world's largest {import} market for soybeans.
e.zh: 中国是世界最大的大豆进口市场。

e.en: Doctors stress the {importance} of regular exercise for heart health.
e.zh: 医生强调定期锻炼对心脏健康的重要性。

e.en: She finally understood the {importance} of saving money early.
e.zh: 她终于明白了尽早存钱的重要性。

e.en: It's {important} to back up your files regularly.
e.zh: 定期备份文件很重要。

e.en: She made an {important} discovery in the lab last week.
e.zh: 她上周在实验室有了一项重要发现。

e.en: More {importantly}, the new policy protects user privacy.
e.zh: 更重要的是,新政策保护了用户隐私。

e.en: He spoke {importantly} about his role in the project.
e.zh: 他煞有介事地谈论自己在项目中的角色。

e.en: The {importation} of foreign cars has increased sharply.
e.zh: 外国汽车的进口量大幅上升。

e.en: New rules restrict the {importation} of certain plants.
e.zh: 新规定限制某些植物的进口。

imported.t:
v. 已导入；进口的
adj. 进口的

e.en: This cheese is {imported} directly from France.
e.zh: 这种奶酪直接从法国进口。

e.en: I {imported} the contacts from my old phone.
e.zh: 我从旧手机导入了联系人。

e.en: China is the world's largest {importer} of soybeans.
e.zh: 中国是全球最大的大豆进口国。

e.en: The {importer} faced new tariffs on electronics this year.
e.zh: 这家进口商今年面临电子产品的新关税。

e.en: The app is {importing} your photos from the cloud.
e.zh: 应用正在从云端导入你的照片。

e.en: The country stopped {importing} oil from that region.
e.zh: 该国停止从那个地区进口石油。

imports.t:
n. 进口商品；导入项
v. 导入（第三人称单数）

e.en: The script {imports} data from a CSV file.
e.zh: 该脚本从 CSV 文件导入数据。

e.en: Steel {imports} dropped by twenty percent last quarter.
e.zh: 上季度钢材进口下降了百分之二十。

importunate.t: adj. 强求的；纠缠不休的

e.en: The {importunate} salesman called her three times today.
e.zh: 那个纠缠不休的推销员今天给她打了三次电话。

e.en: She ignored the {importunate} demands of the reporters.
e.zh: 她无视记者们死缠烂打的要求。

e.en: Beggars often {importune} tourists outside the train station.
e.zh: 乞丐常在火车站外纠缠游客。

e.en: He continued to {importune} his boss for a raise.
e.zh: 他不断地纠缠老板要求加薪。

e.en: She gave in to his {importunity} and agreed to help.
e.zh: 她屈服于他的死缠烂打,答应帮忙。

e.en: The charity's {importunity} eventually wore down many donors.
e.zh: 该慈善机构的反复请求最终让许多捐赠者妥协。

e.en: The government plans to {impose} a tax on sugary drinks.
e.zh: 政府计划对含糖饮料征税。

e.en: I don't want to {impose}, but could I stay tonight?
e.zh: 我不想打扰你,但今晚能借住吗?

e.en: The judge {imposed} a hefty fine on the company.
e.zh: 法官对该公司处以高额罚款。

e.en: Strict curfews were {imposed} during the emergency.
e.zh: 紧急状态期间实施了严格的宵禁。

imposes.t: v. 强加；征收（第三人称单数）

e.en: The new law {imposes} stricter limits on data collection.
e.zh: 新法律对数据收集施加了更严格的限制。

e.en: Working from home {imposes} its own kind of discipline.
e.zh: 在家办公本身就需要一种自律。

imposing.t:
adj. 壮观的；气势宏伟的
v. 正在强加

e.en: The cathedral is an {imposing} stone building near the river.
e.zh: 那座大教堂是河边一座宏伟的石头建筑。

e.en: They are {imposing} new restrictions on social media ads.
e.zh: 他们正在对社交媒体广告施加新的限制。

e.en: Sorry for the {imposition}, but could you watch my dog?
e.zh: 抱歉给你添麻烦,你能帮我看一下狗吗?

e.en: The {imposition} of sanctions hurt the local economy.
e.zh: 制裁的实施损害了当地经济。

e.en: Citizens protested the new tax {impositions} from the government.
e.zh: 民众抗议政府新征收的税款。

e.en: She apologized for the {impositions} she had placed on her friends.
e.zh: 她为给朋友们添的麻烦道歉。

e.en: The startup achieves {impossibilities} that bigger companies can't.
e.zh: 这家初创公司做到了大公司做不到的事。

e.en: His list of demands was full of {impossibilities}.
e.zh: 他的要求清单充满了不可能办到的事。

impossibility.t: n. 不可能；不可能的事

e.en: Finishing this project in one day is a near {impossibility}.
e.zh: 一天内完成这个项目几乎是不可能的。

e.en: The engineer proved the {impossibility} of perpetual motion.
e.zh: 工程师证明了永动机的不可能性。

impossible.t: adj. 不可能的；做不到的

e.en: It's {impossible} to please everyone on the team.
e.zh: 要让团队里每个人都满意是不可能的。

e.en: My toddler has been {impossible} to deal with today.
e.zh: 我家小孩今天简直让人无法招架。

impossibly.t: adv. 不可能地；极其（难以置信地）

e.en: The deadline was {impossibly} tight for such a big task.
e.zh: 对于这么大的任务,期限紧得离谱。

e.en: The mountain road was {impossibly} steep and narrow.
e.zh: 那条山路陡峭狭窄得令人难以置信。

e.en: The dictator threatened to {imprison} anyone who criticized him.
e.zh: 那位独裁者扬言要监禁任何批评他的人。

e.en: Don't let fear {imprison} you in a job you hate.
e.zh: 别让恐惧把你困在一份你讨厌的工作里。

imprisoned.t:
adj. 被监禁的
v. imprison 的过去式

e.en: He was wrongfully {imprisoned} for nearly a decade.
e.zh: 他被冤枉关押了将近十年。

e.en: The journalist was {imprisoned} for reporting on government corruption.
e.zh: 那位记者因报道政府腐败而遭到监禁。

imprisoning.t: v. imprison 的现在分词；囚禁

e.en: The regime is {imprisoning} dissidents at an alarming rate.
e.zh: 该政权正以惊人的速度监禁异见人士。

e.en: Perfectionism can be {imprisoning} if you let it run your life.
e.zh: 如果任由完美主义主导生活，它会成为一种囚笼。

e.en: He faces up to ten years' {imprisonment} for the fraud.
e.zh: 他因诈骗最高可被判处十年监禁。

e.en: Solitary {imprisonment} can cause severe psychological damage.
e.zh: 单独囚禁会造成严重的心理创伤。

imprisonments.t: n. imprisonment 的复数；多次监禁

e.en: The activist's repeated {imprisonments} only strengthened her resolve.
e.zh: 这位活动人士屡次被监禁反而坚定了她的决心。

e.en: Historians documented thousands of unjust {imprisonments} during that era.
e.zh: 历史学家记录了那个时代数千起冤狱。

imprisons.t: v. imprison 的第三人称单数

e.en: The state {imprisons} far more people than any other country.
e.zh: 该国监禁的人数远远超过任何其他国家。

e.en: Shame often {imprisons} people more tightly than any cell.
e.zh: 羞耻感对人的禁锢往往比任何牢房都更紧。

improbability.t: n. 不大可能；不可能的事

e.en: The sheer {improbability} of winning the lottery doesn't stop people buying tickets.
e.zh: 中彩票的概率极低，但这并不能阻止人们买彩票。

e.en: Despite the {improbability}, the underdog team won the championship.
e.zh: 尽管希望渺茫，那支不被看好的队伍还是赢得了冠军。

improbable.t: adj. 不大可能的；未必会发生的

e.en: It seems {improbable} that we'll finish before midnight.
e.zh: 我们能在午夜前完成似乎不太可能。

e.en: The movie's plot is entertaining but highly {improbable}.
e.zh: 这部电影的情节很有趣，但非常不切实际。

improbably.t: adv. 出乎意料地；难以置信地

e.en: {Improbably}, the old laptop still boots up after ten years.
e.zh: 难以置信的是，这台旧笔记本电脑用了十年还能开机。

e.en: She {improbably} survived the crash without a single scratch.
e.zh: 令人难以置信，她在那场车祸中竟毫发无损。

impromptu.t:
adj. 即兴的
adv. 即兴地；临时地

e.en: They held an {impromptu} meeting in the hallway.
e.zh: 他们在走廊里临时开了个会。

e.en: She gave an {impromptu} speech that moved the entire audience.
e.zh: 她即兴发表了一段演讲，感动了在场所有人。

improper.t: adj. 不恰当的；不合适的

e.en: Using company funds for personal travel is clearly {improper}.
e.zh: 动用公司资金去私人旅行显然是不当行为。

e.en: The audit found several cases of {improper} accounting.
e.zh: 审计发现了几起会计处理不当的情况。

improperly.t: adv. 不恰当地；不合宜地

e.en: The chemicals were stored {improperly} and contaminated the soil.
e.zh: 这些化学品存放不当，污染了土壤。

e.en: He was fired for handling client data {improperly}.
e.zh: 他因处理客户数据不当而被解雇。

e.en: The senator denied any {impropriety} regarding the campaign donations.
e.zh: 那位参议员否认在竞选捐款方面有任何不当行为。

e.en: Even the appearance of {impropriety} can ruin a politician's career.
e.zh: 哪怕只是看起来有不当行为，也能毁掉政客的前途。

improv.t: n. 即兴表演（improvisation 的缩写）

e.en: She takes weekly {improv} classes to boost her confidence.
e.zh: 她每周上即兴喜剧课来增强自信。

e.en: Good {improv} comedy looks effortless but takes years to master.
e.zh: 优秀的即兴喜剧看似轻松，实则要练多年才能上手。

e.en: Reading every day will {improve} your vocabulary fast.
e.zh: 每天阅读会让你的词汇量进步飞快。

e.en: The new manager promised to {improve} working conditions.
e.zh: 新经理承诺会改善工作环境。

improved.t:
adj. 改良的
v. improve 的过去式

e.en: Her English has {improved} dramatically since she moved to London.
e.zh: 自从搬到伦敦后，她的英语进步神速。

e.en: The {improved} version of the app loads twice as fast.
e.zh: 改进后的应用版本加载速度快了一倍。

improvement.t: n. 改进；提升；改善之处

e.en: There's been a noticeable {improvement} in air quality this year.
e.zh: 今年空气质量有了明显的改善。

e.en: This draft is a huge {improvement} over the last one.
e.zh: 这一稿比上一稿有了巨大的进步。

improvements.t: n. improvement 的复数；多项改进

e.en: The latest update brings several performance {improvements}.
e.zh: 最新版本带来了多项性能优化。

e.en: We've made major {improvements} to the kitchen this summer.
e.zh: 今年夏天我们对厨房做了大幅改造。

e.en: Bakers often add a dough {improver} to make bread fluffier.
e.zh: 烘焙师常加面团改良剂让面包更松软。

e.en: He's a slow but steady {improver} on the tennis court.
e.zh: 他在网球场上进步缓慢但很稳定。

improves.t: v. improve 的第三人称单数

e.en: Regular exercise {improves} both mood and sleep quality.
e.zh: 规律运动能改善情绪和睡眠质量。

e.en: This wine actually {improves} with a few years in the cellar.
e.zh: 这款葡萄酒在地窖里放上几年反而更好喝。

improvidence.t: n. 没有远见；不知节省

e.en: His {improvidence} with money left the family in debt.
e.zh: 他在用钱方面毫无远见，让家里陷入债务。

e.en: The report blamed years of governmental {improvidence} for the crisis.
e.zh: 报告将这场危机归咎于政府多年来的短视。

e.en: It would be {improvident} to spend your savings on a single trip.
e.zh: 把全部积蓄花在一次旅行上未免太没远见了。

e.en: His {improvident} habits caught up with him after retirement.
e.zh: 他不善规划的习惯在退休后终于自食其果。

improving.t:
v. improve 的现在分词
adj. 有益的

e.en: The patient's condition is slowly {improving}.
e.zh: 病人的病情正在慢慢好转。

e.en: She's focused on {improving} her public speaking skills.
e.zh: 她正专注于提升自己的演讲能力。

improvisation.t: n. 即兴创作；即兴表演

e.en: Jazz relies heavily on {improvisation} rather than written scores.
e.zh: 爵士乐很大程度上依靠即兴演奏，而非乐谱。

e.en: With no recipe, dinner became a fun exercise in {improvisation}.
e.zh: 没有食谱，做晚饭就成了一场有趣的即兴发挥。

improvisational.t: adj. 即兴的；临场发挥的

e.en: The actors took an {improvisational} approach to every scene.
e.zh: 演员们对每一场戏都采用即兴的方式处理。

e.en: Her teaching style is highly {improvisational} and energetic.
e.zh: 她的教学风格非常即兴且充满活力。

e.en: The pianist's {improvisatory} flourishes delighted the audience.
e.zh: 钢琴家即兴的华彩段落让观众听得入迷。

e.en: He has an {improvisatory} flair that makes every solo unique.
e.zh: 他有种即兴天赋，让每段独奏都独一无二。

improvise.t: v. 即兴创作；临时凑合

e.en: When the projector failed, she had to {improvise} the whole presentation.
e.zh: 投影仪坏了，她只好临时发挥把整个演讲做完。

e.en: Good chefs can {improvise} a meal from whatever's in the fridge.
e.zh: 好厨师能用冰箱里现有的东西即兴做出一顿饭。

improvised.t: adj. 即兴的；临时凑成的

e.en: He {improvised} a quick speech when the keynote speaker didn't show.
e.zh: 主讲嘉宾没来，他临时即兴讲了几句。

e.en: They built an {improvised} shelter using branches and a tarp.
e.zh: 他们用树枝和防水布临时搭了个简易棚子。

improviser.t: n. 即兴创作者；即兴表演者

e.en: She's a brilliant {improviser} on stage and never freezes up.
e.zh: 她是位出色的即兴表演者，在台上从不怯场。

e.en: Every great jazz {improviser} has a distinctive musical voice.
e.zh: 每位伟大的爵士即兴演奏家都有独特的音乐个性。

improvising.t: v. improvise 的现在分词；即兴创作

e.en: The saxophonist spent ten minutes {improvising} over the chord changes.
e.zh: 那位萨克斯手在和弦上即兴吹了十分钟。

e.en: Without a script, the comedian started {improvising} with the audience.
e.zh: 没有剧本，那位喜剧演员就开始和观众即兴互动。

e.en: His {imprudence} with credit cards led to serious debt.
e.zh: 他用信用卡时的轻率让他陷入严重债务。

e.en: The report criticized the {imprudence} of the investment strategy.
e.zh: 报告批评了该投资策略的轻率。

e.en: It would be {imprudent} to quit your job without savings.
e.zh: 没有存款就辞职是不明智的。

e.en: Sharing passwords online is an {imprudent} habit.
e.zh: 在网上分享密码是个轻率的习惯。

e.en: She {imprudently} invested all her savings in one stock.
e.zh: 她轻率地把所有积蓄都投到一只股票上。

e.en: He spoke {imprudently} about the company's secret plans.
e.zh: 他不慎地谈到了公司的秘密计划。

imps.t: n. imp 的复数；小恶魔；淘气鬼

e.en: The little {imps} ran around the playground laughing.
e.zh: 几个小调皮鬼在操场上跑来跑去地笑着。

e.en: In the story, mischievous {imps} stole the farmer's apples.
e.zh: 故事里,顽皮的小妖精偷走了农夫的苹果。

e.en: The student's {impudence} shocked the entire classroom.
e.zh: 那个学生的无礼震惊了整个教室。

e.en: She had the {impudence} to interrupt the CEO mid-sentence.
e.zh: 她竟然厚颜无耻地打断了CEO的话。

impudent.t: adj. 厚颜无耻的；放肆的

e.en: The waiter gave an {impudent} reply to the customer's complaint.
e.zh: 服务员对顾客的投诉给出无礼的回应。

e.en: His {impudent} smile annoyed everyone at the meeting.
e.zh: 他那放肆的笑容惹恼了会议上的每个人。

e.en: The teenager {impudently} rolled his eyes at his mother.
e.zh: 那个少年放肆地对母亲翻了个白眼。

e.en: She {impudently} questioned the manager's authority in front of clients.
e.zh: 她在客户面前无礼地质疑经理的权威。

e.en: The lawyer tried to {impugn} the witness's credibility.
e.zh: 律师试图质疑证人的可信度。

e.en: Critics {impugn} the motives behind the new policy.
e.zh: 批评者质疑新政策背后的动机。

e.en: The general's {impuissance} became obvious after the failed attack.
e.zh: 将军的无能在那次失败的进攻后变得显而易见。

e.en: Voters expressed frustration at the government's {impuissance} during the crisis.
e.zh: 选民对政府在危机中的无力深表失望。

impulse.t: n. 冲动；一时兴起；脉冲

e.en: I bought this jacket on a sudden {impulse}.
e.zh: 我一时冲动买下了这件夹克。

e.en: The nerve sends an electrical {impulse} to the muscle.
e.zh: 神经将电脉冲传送到肌肉。

impulses.t: n. impulse 的复数；冲动；脉冲

e.en: Try to control your shopping {impulses} during the holiday sales.
e.zh: 假日促销期间尽量控制你的购物冲动。

e.en: The brain processes thousands of nerve {impulses} every second.
e.zh: 大脑每秒处理成千上万的神经冲动。

e.en: His {impulsive} decision to move abroad surprised his family.
e.zh: 他冲动地决定出国让家人很意外。

e.en: Teenagers often make {impulsive} choices they later regret.
e.zh: 青少年常常做出事后后悔的冲动选择。

e.en: She {impulsively} booked a flight to Tokyo last night.
e.zh: 她昨晚一冲动就订了去东京的机票。

e.en: He {impulsively} quit his job after the argument.
e.zh: 那场争吵后他冲动地辞了职。

impulsiveness.t: n. 冲动；易冲动的性格

e.en: Her {impulsiveness} sometimes gets her into trouble at work.
e.zh: 她的冲动有时会让她在工作中惹上麻烦。

e.en: Therapy helped him manage his {impulsiveness} and anger.
e.zh: 治疗帮助他控制冲动和愤怒。

impunity.t: n. 免受惩罚；逍遥法外

e.en: Hackers operated with {impunity} due to weak online laws.
e.zh: 由于网络法律薄弱,黑客肆无忌惮地行事。

e.en: No one should break the rules with {impunity}.
e.zh: 没人能违反规则而不受惩罚。

e.en: The lab rejected the sample because it was {impure}.
e.zh: 实验室因样品不纯而拒收。

e.en: Drinking {impure} water can cause serious illness.
e.zh: 饮用不洁的水会导致严重疾病。

e.en: Even a tiny {impurity} can ruin the chip's performance.
e.zh: 哪怕极小的杂质也会毁掉芯片的性能。

e.en: The filter removes any {impurity} from the drinking water.
e.zh: 过滤器去除饮用水中的任何杂质。

e.en: He strongly denied the {imputation} of dishonesty.
e.zh: 他强烈否认对他不诚实的指控。

e.en: Statisticians use {imputation} to handle missing data values.
e.zh: 统计学家用插补法处理缺失的数据值。

e.en: Don't {impute} bad motives to people you barely know.
e.zh: 不要把恶意归咎于你根本不了解的人。

e.en: Critics {impute} the company's success to government subsidies.
e.zh: 批评者将该公司的成功归因于政府补贴。

imputed.t:
adj. 推定的
v. impute 的过去式

e.en: The journalist {imputed} the scandal to poor management.
e.zh: 记者将这起丑闻归咎于管理不善。

e.en: Economists use {imputed} rent when calculating homeowner income.
e.zh: 经济学家在计算房主收入时使用估算租金。

inauspicious.t: adj. 不吉利的，预兆不好的

e.en: The startup had an {inauspicious} start with no funding.
e.zh: 那家初创公司开局不利,毫无资金支持。

e.en: Rain on the wedding day felt {inauspicious}.
e.zh: 婚礼当天下雨让人感觉不吉利。

inauthentic.t: adj. 不真实的；非原创的

e.en: Her apology felt {inauthentic} and rehearsed.
e.zh: 她的道歉听起来很不真诚,像是排练过的。

e.en: Tourists complained the restaurant served {inauthentic} Italian food.
e.zh: 游客抱怨那家餐厅做的不是正宗意大利菜。

e.en: Viewers quickly noticed the {inauthenticity} of his on-camera persona.
e.zh: 观众很快察觉到他镜头前的形象并不真实。

e.en: The brand suffered from years of perceived {inauthenticity}.
e.zh: 该品牌多年来一直被认为不够真诚。

inbetween.t:
adj. 介于中间的
n. 中间状态

e.en: There's no {inbetween} option — you either join or leave.
e.zh: 没有中间选项,要么加入要么离开。

e.en: She's stuck in an {inbetween} stage of her career.
e.zh: 她正处于职业生涯的过渡阶段。

inboard.t:
adj. 内侧的；船内的
adv. 向内

e.en: The boat has a powerful {inboard} engine for speed.
e.zh: 这艘船配备了强劲的内置发动机以提升速度。

e.en: Move the cargo {inboard} to balance the vessel.
e.zh: 把货物移向船内中央以保持船只平衡。

inborn.t: adj. 天生的，与生俱来的

e.en: She has an {inborn} talent for solving puzzles.
e.zh: 她天生擅长解谜。

e.en: Curiosity seems to be {inborn} in young children.
e.zh: 好奇心似乎是幼儿与生俱来的。

inbound.t: adj. 入站的；返程的（流量、航班）

e.en: The {inbound} flight from Tokyo arrives at midnight.
e.zh: 从东京飞来的航班将于午夜抵达。

e.en: Our team handles all {inbound} customer support calls.
e.zh: 我们团队负责处理所有来电的客户支持。

inbred.t: adj. 近亲繁殖的；天生的

e.en: The royal family suffered from generations of being {inbred}.
e.zh: 那个王室因世代近亲通婚而饱受困扰。

e.en: He has an {inbred} love of the outdoors.
e.zh: 他对户外活动有种与生俱来的热爱。

e.en: {Inbreeding} can cause serious genetic problems in animals.
e.zh: 近亲繁殖会导致动物出现严重的遗传问题。

e.en: Conservationists worry about {inbreeding} in small panda populations.
e.zh: 保育人员担心小种群熊猫的近亲繁殖问题。

e.en: This phone has an {inbuilt} GPS and compass.
e.zh: 这款手机内置了GPS和指南针。

e.en: Humans have an {inbuilt} fear of falling.
e.zh: 人类天生对坠落感到恐惧。

inc.t: abbr. 股份有限公司（Incorporated 的缩写）

e.en: She works at Apple {Inc}. as a software engineer.
e.zh: 她在苹果公司担任软件工程师。

e.en: The company registered as Bright Solutions {Inc}. last year.
e.zh: 该公司去年注册为Bright Solutions公司。

inca.t: n. 印加人；印加帝国的

e.en: The {Inca} empire once stretched across the Andes mountains.
e.zh: 印加帝国曾横跨整个安第斯山脉。

e.en: Tourists hike to ancient {Inca} ruins in Peru.
e.zh: 游客前往秘鲁徒步参观古老的印加遗址。

incalculable.t: adj. 难以估量的；无法计算的

e.en: The damage from the flood was {incalculable}.
e.zh: 这次洪水造成的损失无法估量。

e.en: Her contribution to the team was of {incalculable} value.
e.zh: 她对团队的贡献价值难以估量。

e.en: The discovery is {incalculably} important to modern medicine.
e.zh: 这一发现对现代医学的重要性难以估量。

e.en: Losing her would set the project back {incalculably}.
e.zh: 失去她会让项目遭受难以估量的倒退。

incan.t: adj. 印加人的；印加帝国的

e.en: The museum displays beautiful {Incan} gold artifacts.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了精美的印加黄金文物。

e.en: Machu Picchu is the most famous {Incan} site.
e.zh: 马丘比丘是最著名的印加遗址。

e.en: The {incandescence} of the molten metal lit the workshop.
e.zh: 熔化金属的炽热光芒照亮了整个车间。

e.en: Her face glowed with the {incandescence} of pure joy.
e.zh: 她的脸上焕发着纯粹喜悦的光彩。

e.en: Most homes have replaced {incandescent} bulbs with LEDs.
e.zh: 大多数家庭已将白炽灯泡换成LED灯。

e.en: She was {incandescent} with rage after reading the email.
e.zh: 读完那封邮件后,她怒火中烧。

e.en: The wizard chanted an ancient {incantation} to break the curse.
e.zh: 巫师吟诵古老的咒语来破除诅咒。

e.en: He repeated the phrase like a magical {incantation}.
e.zh: 他像念咒语般反复念叨着那句话。

e.en: The poem has an {incantatory} rhythm that mesmerizes listeners.
e.zh: 这首诗有种咒语般的节奏,令听者着迷。

e.en: His speech took on an almost {incantatory} quality.
e.zh: 他的演讲带上了一种近乎咒语般的特质。

incapable.t: adj. 无能力的，做不到的

e.en: He seems {incapable} of telling the truth.
e.zh: 他似乎根本说不出真话。

e.en: The old laptop is {incapable} of running modern software.
e.zh: 这台旧笔记本无法运行现代软件。

incapacitate.t: v. 使丧失能力；使不能胜任

e.en: A single sting can {incapacitate} a small animal.
e.zh: 一次蜇咬就能让小动物失去活动能力。

e.en: The injury could {incapacitate} him for several months.
e.zh: 这次受伤可能让他数月无法行动。

e.en: She was {incapacitated} by a back injury for weeks.
e.zh: 她因背部受伤而卧床数周无法行动。

e.en: The driver was {incapacitated} after the accident.
e.zh: 那位司机在事故后失去了行动能力。

e.en: She suffers from {incapacitating} migraines every month.
e.zh: 她每月都饱受让人无法工作的偏头痛折磨。

e.en: The fear became {incapacitating} whenever she boarded a plane.
e.zh: 每次登机时她都会被恐惧彻底困住。

e.en: The drug causes temporary {incapacitation} of the muscles.
e.zh: 该药物会导致肌肉暂时失去功能。

e.en: His {incapacitation} forced the company to find a replacement.
e.zh: 他的丧失行动能力迫使公司另寻替代人选。

e.en: The CEO resigned due to {incapacity} caused by illness.
e.zh: 那位CEO因病丧失行为能力而辞职。

e.en: His {incapacity} for empathy made him a poor leader.
e.zh: 他缺乏共情能力,使他难以胜任领导岗位。

e.en: The state will {incarcerate} repeat offenders for longer terms.
e.zh: 州政府会对惯犯处以更长的监禁。

e.en: They voted to {incarcerate} him for twenty years.
e.zh: 他们投票决定将他监禁二十年。

e.en: He was {incarcerated} for three years on fraud charges.
e.zh: 他因欺诈罪被监禁三年。

e.en: Many {incarcerated} people struggle to find jobs after release.
e.zh: 许多被监禁过的人出狱后难以找到工作。

e.en: Mass {incarceration} has become a major social issue.
e.zh: 大规模监禁已成为一个重大的社会问题。

e.en: Her {incarceration} lasted nearly a decade.
e.zh: 她的监禁持续了将近十年。

incarnate.t:
adj. 化身的，具体化的
v. 使具体化

e.en: To his fans, he was rock and roll {incarnate}.
e.zh: 对粉丝来说,他就是摇滚乐的化身。

e.en: The villain seemed like evil {incarnate} on screen.
e.zh: 屏幕上那个反派简直就是邪恶的化身。

e.en: This phone is the latest {incarnation} of the iPhone.
e.zh: 这款手机是iPhone的最新版本。

e.en: She seemed like the {incarnation} of kindness itself.
e.zh: 她仿佛就是善良的化身。

incarnational.t: adj. 道成肉身的；化身的

e.en: The theology emphasizes the {incarnational} presence of God.
e.zh: 该神学强调上帝的道成肉身式临在。

e.en: His ministry takes an {incarnational} approach to community service.
e.zh: 他的事工以道成肉身的方式参与社区服务。

e.en: One {incautious} remark cost her the promotion.
e.zh: 一句不慎的话让她失去了晋升机会。

e.en: Hikers who are {incautious} on icy trails often fall.
e.zh: 在冰雪山路上不小心的徒步者常常摔倒。

e.en: He {incautiously} shared his password with a stranger.
e.zh: 他不慎将密码告诉了一个陌生人。

e.en: She spoke {incautiously} and offended several colleagues.
e.zh: 她说话不谨慎,得罪了几位同事。

incendiary.t:
n. 燃烧弹
adj. 煽动性的；纵火的

e.en: His {incendiary} speech sparked riots across the city.
e.zh: 他煽动性的演讲在全城引发了骚乱。

e.en: Police found {incendiary} devices hidden in the warehouse.
e.zh: 警方在仓库里发现了隐藏的燃烧装置。

incense.t:
n. 熏香
v. 激怒

e.en: She lit some {incense} to relax before meditation.
e.zh: 她点了些香，准备冥想前放松一下。

e.en: The temple was filled with the smell of {incense}.
e.zh: 寺庙里弥漫着香的味道。

incensed.t: adj. 激怒的，非常生气的

e.en: Fans were {incensed} by the referee's controversial decision.
e.zh: 球迷对裁判有争议的判罚感到非常愤怒。

e.en: She was {incensed} when the airline lost her luggage.
e.zh: 航空公司弄丢了她的行李，她气坏了。

incenses.t:
n. 熏香（复数）
v. 激怒（第三人称单数）

e.en: Nothing {incenses} him more than people being late.
e.zh: 没有什么比别人迟到更让他光火了。

e.en: The shop sells various {incenses} from across Asia.
e.zh: 这家店出售来自亚洲各地的各种香。

e.en: The company offered a cash {incentive} for early signups.
e.zh: 公司为提前注册的用户提供了现金奖励。

e.en: Tax breaks are a strong {incentive} for businesses to invest.
e.zh: 税收优惠是企业投资的有力激励。

e.en: The government introduced new {incentives} for clean energy.
e.zh: 政府推出了新的清洁能源激励措施。

e.en: Sales staff get {incentives} for hitting monthly targets.
e.zh: 销售人员达到月度目标可获得奖金。

e.en: The startup has grown rapidly since its {inception} in 2020.
e.zh: 这家初创公司自2020年成立以来发展迅速。

e.en: From {inception}, the project faced funding challenges.
e.zh: 该项目从一开始就面临资金问题。

e.en: The election result left the markets in {incertitude}.
e.zh: 选举结果让市场陷入了不确定之中。

e.en: Her voice betrayed a deep {incertitude} about the plan.
e.zh: 她的声音透露出对计划深深的疑虑。

e.en: The {incessant} noise from construction kept me awake.
e.zh: 施工持续不断的噪音让我无法入睡。

e.en: I'm tired of his {incessant} complaints about work.
e.zh: 我受够了他对工作没完没了的抱怨。

e.en: It rained {incessantly} for three days straight.
e.zh: 接连三天下个不停地下雨。

e.en: The baby cried {incessantly} all through the night.
e.zh: 宝宝整夜哭个不停。

e.en: Most cultures consider {incest} a serious taboo.
e.zh: 大多数文化都将乱伦视为严重的禁忌。

e.en: The novel explores themes of {incest} and family secrets.
e.zh: 这部小说探讨了乱伦和家庭秘密的主题。

incestuous.t: adj. 乱伦的；关系过密的

e.en: The tech industry can feel {incestuous} with everyone connected.
e.zh: 科技圈人人相识，感觉关系错综复杂。

e.en: The Greek myths are full of {incestuous} relationships.
e.zh: 希腊神话中充满了乱伦关系。

inch.t:
n. 英寸
v. 缓慢移动

e.en: The snow was about an {inch} deep this morning.
e.zh: 今天早上的雪大约有一英寸厚。

e.en: Move the picture an {inch} to the left, please.
e.zh: 请把那幅画往左移一英寸。

e.en: The {Inchcape} Rock is famous in maritime poetry.
e.zh: 印齐角礁在航海诗歌中很有名。

e.en: Sailors long feared the dangerous reef called {Inchcape}.
e.zh: 水手们长期害怕那座叫印齐角的危险礁石。

inched.t: v. 缓慢移动（inch 的过去式）

e.en: Traffic {inched} forward during the morning rush hour.
e.zh: 早高峰时段，车流缓慢地向前挪动。

e.en: She {inched} closer to read the small print.
e.zh: 她一点点凑近，想看清小字。

inches.t:
n. 英寸（复数）
v. 缓慢移动（第三人称单数）

e.en: The new monitor measures 27 {inches} diagonally.
e.zh: 新显示器对角线长27英寸。

e.en: He missed the catch by just a few {inches}.
e.zh: 他差几英寸就接到球了。

inching.t: v. 缓慢移动；一点点挪动

e.en: Stock prices are slowly {inching} upward this week.
e.zh: 本周股价正在缓慢地小幅上涨。

e.en: The cat kept {inching} toward the bird outside.
e.zh: 那只猫一点点朝外面的鸟挪过去。

inchoate.t: adj. 刚开始的；未成形的

e.en: She had only an {inchoate} idea for her novel.
e.zh: 她对自己的小说只有一个尚未成形的构想。

e.en: The movement remains {inchoate} without clear leadership.
e.zh: 由于缺乏明确领导，这场运动仍处于初始阶段。

e.en: He {inchoately} sensed something was wrong at home.
e.zh: 他隐约感觉到家里出了什么问题。

e.en: The plan was {inchoately} formed and needed more thought.
e.zh: 这个计划还很不成熟，需要再斟酌。

e.en: The {incidence} of diabetes has risen sharply in cities.
e.zh: 城市里糖尿病的发病率急剧上升。

e.en: Researchers tracked the {incidence} of flu cases this winter.
e.zh: 研究人员追踪了今年冬天的流感发病情况。

incidences.t: n. 发生率（incidence 的复数）

e.en: Several {incidences} of fraud were reported last quarter.
e.zh: 上个季度报告了多起欺诈事件。

e.en: The report lists all {incidences} of safety violations.
e.zh: 报告列出了所有违反安全规定的情况。

e.en: Police are investigating the {incident} that happened last night.
e.zh: 警方正在调查昨晚发生的事件。

e.en: It was an embarrassing {incident} we'd rather forget.
e.zh: 那是一件令人尴尬、我们宁愿忘掉的事。

e.en: The cost of parking is {incidental} compared to the ticket price.
e.zh: 与票价相比，停车费只是次要的开销。

e.en: Her success was {incidental} to the team's overall victory.
e.zh: 她的成功对团队的整体胜利来说只是顺带的。

incidentally.t: adv. 顺便说一句；附带地

e.en: {Incidentally}, did you hear that Sarah got promoted?
e.zh: 顺便说一句，你听说Sarah升职了吗？

e.en: He mentioned, quite {incidentally}, that he was leaving.
e.zh: 他相当随意地提到自己要走了。

incidentals.t: n. 杂项费用；零星开支

e.en: Budget extra cash for {incidentals} during your trip.
e.zh: 旅行时多准备些零花钱应付杂项开支。

e.en: The hotel charges separately for {incidentals} like minibar items.
e.zh: 酒店对迷你吧之类的杂项另行收费。

e.en: Several {incidents} of vandalism occurred in the park.
e.zh: 公园里发生了几起破坏公物的事件。

e.en: The pilot reported no {incidents} during the long flight.
e.zh: 飞行员报告这次长途飞行没有发生任何意外。

e.en: The hospital must {incinerate} all medical waste safely.
e.zh: 医院必须安全地焚烧所有医疗废物。

e.en: Don't {incinerate} plastics in your backyard fire pit.
e.zh: 不要在你的后院火坑里焚烧塑料。

e.en: All confidential documents were {incinerated} after the audit.
e.zh: 审计结束后，所有机密文件都被焚毁了。

e.en: The wildfire {incinerated} thousands of acres of forest.
e.zh: 野火烧毁了数千英亩的森林。

e.en: {Incineration} is one method of dealing with hazardous waste.
e.zh: 焚烧是处理危险废物的方法之一。

e.en: The city is building a new waste {incineration} plant.
e.zh: 该市正在建造一座新的垃圾焚烧厂。

e.en: Old medical records are burned in the hospital {incinerator}.
e.zh: 旧的医疗记录在医院的焚化炉中被烧毁。

e.en: The factory's {incinerator} runs around the clock.
e.zh: 工厂的焚化炉昼夜不停地运转。

e.en: Doctors detected an {incipient} tumor during the routine scan.
e.zh: 医生在例行扫描中发现了一个初期肿瘤。

e.en: There are signs of an {incipient} economic recovery.
e.zh: 有迹象显示经济正在初步复苏。

e.en: The surgeon will {incise} the skin to remove the cyst.
e.zh: 外科医生将切开皮肤以摘除囊肿。

e.en: Craftsmen {incise} delicate patterns into the silver bowl.
e.zh: 工匠们在银碗上雕刻精致的图案。

incised.t:
v. 切开（过去式）
adj. 刻入的

e.en: The artist {incised} her initials into the wooden frame.
e.zh: 艺术家把自己的姓名首字母刻在了木框上。

e.en: Ancient names were {incised} on the stone monument.
e.zh: 古老的名字被刻在石碑上。

incises.t: v. 切开（第三人称单数）

e.en: The dentist carefully {incises} the gum to access the tooth.
e.zh: 牙医小心地切开牙龈以接触到牙齿。

e.en: He {incises} elegant designs into each leather wallet.
e.zh: 他在每个皮夹上刻出优雅的图案。

e.en: The jeweler spent hours {incising} patterns on the bracelet.
e.zh: 珠宝匠花了好几个小时在手镯上雕刻花纹。

e.en: {Incising} the bark too deeply can harm the tree.
e.zh: 在树皮上刻得太深会伤害树木。

e.en: The surgeon made a small {incision} below the ribs.
e.zh: 外科医生在肋骨下方做了一个小切口。

e.en: Keep the {incision} clean to prevent infection.
e.zh: 保持切口清洁以防感染。

e.en: He developed an {incisional} hernia after the surgery.
e.zh: 手术后他得了切口疝。

e.en: The doctor checked for any {incisional} bleeding overnight.
e.zh: 医生检查了夜间是否有切口出血。

e.en: Modern surgery often uses tiny {incisions} for faster recovery.
e.zh: 现代手术常用微小切口以加快恢复。

e.en: The chef made shallow {incisions} on the fish before grilling.
e.zh: 厨师在烤鱼前在鱼身上划了几道浅口。

incisive.t: adj. 犀利的；一针见血的

e.en: Her {incisive} questions exposed flaws in the proposal.
e.zh: 她敏锐的提问暴露了提案中的缺陷。

e.en: The reporter is known for her {incisive} analysis of politics.
e.zh: 这位记者以对政治的犀利分析著称。

e.en: The professor {incisively} dismantled the student's argument.
e.zh: 教授一针见血地驳倒了学生的论点。

e.en: She writes {incisively} about social inequality.
e.zh: 她对社会不平等问题的写作鞭辟入里。

e.en: The lawyer's {incisiveness} impressed everyone in the courtroom.
e.zh: 那位律师的犀利让法庭上每个人都印象深刻。

e.en: I admire the {incisiveness} of her opinion columns.
e.zh: 我钦佩她评论专栏的尖锐深刻。

e.en: The dentist filled a small cavity in my front {incisor}.
e.zh: 牙医在我前门牙的一个小蛀洞上补了牙。

e.en: He chipped his upper {incisor} during the soccer game.
e.zh: 他在足球比赛中把上门牙磕掉了一块。

e.en: Humans have eight {incisors} in total, four on each jaw.
e.zh: 人类总共有八颗门牙，上下颌各四颗。

e.en: Rabbits' {incisors} keep growing throughout their lives.
e.zh: 兔子的门牙会终生不断生长。

e.en: The post was removed for trying to {incite} violence.
e.zh: 该帖子因煽动暴力而被删除。

e.en: His speech was meant to {incite} the crowd to action.
e.zh: 他的演讲意在煽动人群采取行动。

e.en: He was charged with {incitement} to commit a crime.
e.zh: 他被指控煽动他人犯罪。

e.en: The video was flagged as {incitement} to hatred.
e.zh: 该视频被标记为煽动仇恨内容。

e.en: Online {incivility} has become a major problem on social media.
e.zh: 网络上的不文明行为已成为社交媒体的一大问题。

e.en: She was shocked by the {incivility} of the customer.
e.zh: 那位顾客的无礼让她感到震惊。

incl.t: 缩. 包含（including 的缩写）

e.en: The price is $50, {incl} shipping and tax.
e.zh: 价格为50美元，含运费和税。

e.en: All meals are provided, {incl} breakfast and dinner.
e.zh: 所有餐食均提供，包括早餐和晚餐。

e.en: The flight was delayed due to {inclement} weather.
e.zh: 航班因恶劣天气而延误。

e.en: Schools closed early because of the {inclement} conditions.
e.zh: 由于天气恶劣，学校提前停课。

inclination.t:
n. 倾向；爱好
n. 倾斜度

e.en: I have no {inclination} to go out tonight.
e.zh: 我今晚没什么兴致出门。

e.en: She has a natural {inclination} toward music and art.
e.zh: 她对音乐和艺术有天然的爱好。

incline.t:
v. 倾向于；使倾斜
n. 斜坡

e.en: The bike struggled up the steep {incline}.
e.zh: 自行车吃力地爬上陡坡。

e.en: I {incline} toward the cheaper option for now.
e.zh: 我目前倾向于选择较便宜的方案。

inclined.t: adj. 倾向于的；有意愿的

e.en: I'm {inclined} to agree with her on this issue.
e.zh: 在这个问题上我倾向于同意她的看法。

e.en: The roof is gently {inclined} to let rain run off.
e.zh: 屋顶略微倾斜以便雨水流走。

e.en: The pilot checked the {inclinometer} before banking the plane.
e.zh: 飞行员在飞机倾斜前检查了倾角仪。

e.en: Engineers used an {inclinometer} to measure the slope's angle.
e.zh: 工程师用倾角仪测量了斜坡的角度。

e.en: Please {include} your phone number on the form.
e.zh: 请在表格上填上你的电话号码。

e.en: The package will {include} a charger and a manual.
e.zh: 包装内将附带充电器和说明书。

included.t:
v. 包含（过去式）
adj. 包含在内的

e.en: Tax is already {included} in the listed price.
e.zh: 标价已经包含了税费。

e.en: Everyone, kids {included}, enjoyed the show.
e.zh: 所有人,包括孩子在内,都很喜欢这场表演。

includes.t: v. 包含（第三人称单数）

e.en: The plan {includes} unlimited data and free calls.
e.zh: 该套餐包含无限流量和免费通话。

e.en: Her résumé {includes} five years at Google.
e.zh: 她的简历里包括在谷歌工作的五年经历。

e.en: Many countries, {including} Japan, signed the agreement.
e.zh: 许多国家,包括日本,都签署了该协议。

e.en: The fee is twenty dollars, {including} shipping.
e.zh: 费用是二十美元,含运费。

e.en: The company promotes diversity and {inclusion} at work.
e.zh: 公司在职场推动多元与共融。

e.en: Her {inclusion} on the team surprised everyone.
e.zh: 她被纳入团队让大家都很意外。

e.en: The city passed an {inclusionary} housing policy for low-income families.
e.zh: 市政府通过了面向低收入家庭的包容性住房政策。

e.en: They adopted {inclusionary} hiring practices to widen the talent pool.
e.zh: 他们采取包容性招聘做法以扩大人才库。

e.en: Check the policy for {inclusions} and exclusions before signing.
e.zh: 签约前请查看保单的承保范围与除外项目。

e.en: The diamond had tiny {inclusions} visible under a microscope.
e.zh: 这颗钻石在显微镜下能看到细小的内含物。

inclusive.t: adj. 包容的；包含在内的

e.en: We want to build an {inclusive} community for all backgrounds.
e.zh: 我们希望打造一个面向各种背景的包容社区。

e.en: The conference runs from May 3 to 7 {inclusive}.
e.zh: 会议从5月3日开到5月7日,首尾日均含。

e.en: The team designs products {inclusively}, considering users with disabilities.
e.zh: 团队以包容的方式设计产品,会考虑残障用户。

e.en: She speaks {inclusively}, making sure everyone feels heard.
e.zh: 她说话很包容,让每个人都觉得被倾听。

e.en: The school is praised for its {inclusiveness} and warm culture.
e.zh: 这所学校以其包容性和温暖氛围受到称赞。

e.en: True {inclusiveness} means more than just inviting people in.
e.zh: 真正的包容不只是把人请进来这么简单。

e.en: His {incogitant} reply showed he hadn't thought it through.
e.zh: 他那不假思索的回答显示他根本没想清楚。

e.en: Don't be so {incogitant} about other people's feelings.
e.zh: 别这么不顾他人感受。

incognito.t:
adj. 匿名的；隐姓埋名的
adv. 匿名地

e.en: The actor traveled {incognito} to avoid the paparazzi.
e.zh: 那位演员隐姓埋名出行以躲避狗仔队。

e.en: Open an {incognito} window to browse without saving history.
e.zh: 打开无痕窗口,浏览时就不会保存历史记录。

e.en: The {incoherence} of his speech worried the doctors.
e.zh: 他讲话语无伦次,让医生们很担心。

e.en: Critics pointed out the {incoherence} of the policy proposal.
e.zh: 评论人士指出该政策建议前后矛盾。

incoherent.t: adj. 不连贯的；语无伦次的

e.en: After the accident he was confused and {incoherent}.
e.zh: 事故后他神志不清,语无伦次。

e.en: The essay was rambling and largely {incoherent}.
e.zh: 这篇文章东拉西扯,基本不知所云。

ims.t: n. 即时通讯系统（Instant Messaging System 缩写）

e.en: Modern phones support multiple {ims} for chatting with friends.
e.zh: 现代手机支持多种即时通讯应用与朋友聊天。

e.en: Corporate {ims} like Slack have replaced most internal emails.
e.zh: 像Slack这样的企业即时通讯工具已取代大多数内部邮件。

inabilities.t: n. 无能；无力（inability 的复数）

e.en: The report listed several {inabilities} that limited the team's progress.
e.zh: 报告列出了限制团队进展的几项无能之处。

e.en: His learning {inabilities} were addressed with special tutoring.
e.zh: 通过特别辅导解决了他的学习障碍。

e.en: Her {inability} to focus made remote work difficult.
e.zh: 她无法专注,使远程工作变得困难。

e.en: The app's {inability} to sync data frustrated many users.
e.zh: 该应用无法同步数据让许多用户感到沮丧。

inaccessibility.t: n. 难以到达；无法访问

e.en: The website's {inaccessibility} excludes users with disabilities.
e.zh: 该网站的不便访问性将残障用户排除在外。

e.en: Mountain villages suffer from the {inaccessibility} of medical care.
e.zh: 山区村庄因医疗服务难以获取而苦恼。

inaccessible.t: adj. 无法进入的；难以访问的

e.en: The server is currently {inaccessible} due to maintenance.
e.zh: 由于维护,该服务器目前无法访问。

e.en: Many old buildings remain {inaccessible} to wheelchair users.
e.zh: 许多老建筑仍然不便轮椅使用者进入。

e.en: The article contained one minor factual {inaccuracy}.
e.zh: 这篇文章包含一处轻微的事实错误。

e.en: GPS {inaccuracy} can be a problem in dense cities.
e.zh: 在密集的城市里,GPS不准确可能是个问题。

e.en: The weather forecast turned out to be completely {inaccurate}.
e.zh: 天气预报结果完全不准确。

e.en: Please correct any {inaccurate} information on your profile.
e.zh: 请更正你个人资料上任何不准确的信息。

e.en: The news site {inaccurately} reported the death toll.
e.zh: 该新闻网站不准确地报道了死亡人数。

e.en: He {inaccurately} described the meeting to his colleagues.
e.zh: 他向同事不准确地描述了那次会议。

e.en: Government {inaction} on climate change angered young voters.
e.zh: 政府在气候变化上的不作为激怒了年轻选民。

e.en: His {inaction} during the emergency cost the company millions.
e.zh: 他在紧急情况下的不作为让公司损失了数百万。

e.en: Heat can {inactivate} the virus within minutes.
e.zh: 高温可以在几分钟内使病毒失活。

e.en: You can {inactivate} the account from the settings page.
e.zh: 你可以从设置页面停用该账户。

inactivated.t: adj. 已灭活的；已停用的

e.en: The vaccine uses {inactivated} virus particles to trigger immunity.
e.zh: 该疫苗使用灭活的病毒颗粒来激发免疫力。

e.en: His old account was {inactivated} after years of disuse.
e.zh: 他的旧账户因多年未用而被停用。

e.en: Heat treatment ensures complete {inactivation} of harmful bacteria.
e.zh: 热处理确保有害细菌的彻底灭活。

e.en: Gene {inactivation} helps researchers study cellular functions.
e.zh: 基因失活有助于研究人员研究细胞功能。

e.en: Your account has been {inactive} for over six months.
e.zh: 你的账户已超过六个月未使用。

e.en: He's been physically {inactive} since breaking his leg.
e.zh: 自从摔断腿后,他一直缺乏运动。

e.en: Long periods of {inactivity} can harm your cardiovascular health.
e.zh: 长时间不活动会损害你的心血管健康。

e.en: The account was closed due to two years of {inactivity}.
e.zh: 该账户因两年无活动而被关闭。

e.en: He often felt a deep sense of {inadequacy} at work.
e.zh: 他在工作中常感到深深的自卑。

e.en: The report exposed the {inadequacy} of current safety measures.
e.zh: 报告揭露了现行安全措施的不足。

e.en: The lighting in this room is completely {inadequate} for reading.
e.zh: 这个房间的照明完全不适合阅读。

e.en: Many schools still have {inadequate} funding for arts programs.
e.zh: 许多学校的艺术项目资金仍然不足。

e.en: The bridge was {inadequately} maintained for years before collapsing.
e.zh: 那座桥多年维护不善后倒塌。

e.en: Workers were {inadequately} trained to handle the new equipment.
e.zh: 工人接受的新设备操作培训不够。

inadmissible.t: adj. 不可采纳的；不允许的

e.en: The judge ruled the recorded conversation {inadmissible} as evidence.
e.zh: 法官裁定那段录音不可作为证据。

e.en: Hearsay is generally {inadmissible} in most criminal trials.
e.zh: 传闻在大多数刑事审判中通常不可采纳。

e.en: The data leak resulted from sheer {inadvertence}, not malice.
e.zh: 这次数据泄露纯属疏忽,并非恶意。

e.en: His {inadvertence} in signing the contract proved costly.
e.zh: 他签合同时的疏忽代价惨重。

inadvertent.t: adj. 无意的；疏忽造成的

e.en: The email contained an {inadvertent} disclosure of customer data.
e.zh: 那封邮件无意中泄露了客户数据。

e.en: His {inadvertent} comment offended several team members.
e.zh: 他无心的评论冒犯了几名团队成员。

e.en: I {inadvertently} deleted the file while cleaning up folders.
e.zh: 我在整理文件夹时不小心删除了那份文件。

e.en: She {inadvertently} replied-all to a private message.
e.zh: 她不小心对一条私信点了全部回复。

inadvisable.t: adj. 不明智的；不可取的

e.en: It's {inadvisable} to share your password with anyone.
e.zh: 将密码告诉任何人都是不明智的。

e.en: Driving in this storm would be highly {inadvisable}.
e.zh: 在这场暴风雨中开车非常不明智。

inalienable.t: adj. 不可剥夺的；不可让与的

e.en: Free speech is considered an {inalienable} human right.
e.zh: 言论自由被视为不可剥夺的人权。

e.en: The constitution protects several {inalienable} rights of citizens.
e.zh: 宪法保护公民的若干不可剥夺的权利。

e.en: Stop posting {inane} comments on every social media thread.
e.zh: 别再在每条社交媒体帖子下发无聊的评论了。

e.en: The TV show was full of {inane} jokes and shallow plots.
e.zh: 那个电视节目充满了无聊的笑话和肤浅的情节。

e.en: He grinned {inanely} at the camera during the interview.
e.zh: 采访时他对着镜头傻乎乎地笑着。

e.en: She kept chattering {inanely} throughout the whole movie.
e.zh: 整部电影她都在喋喋不休地说着无聊的话。

inanimate.t: adj. 无生命的；无生气的

e.en: Children often talk to {inanimate} objects like stuffed toys.
e.zh: 孩子们经常对毛绒玩具等无生命的物体说话。

e.en: Rocks and chairs are {inanimate}, unlike plants and animals.
e.zh: 岩石和椅子是无生命的,与植物和动物不同。

e.en: The {inanity} of daytime television amazes me sometimes.
e.zh: 白天电视节目的无聊有时让我惊讶。

e.en: He laughed at the {inanity} of the office gossip.
e.zh: 他对办公室八卦的无聊嗤笑不已。

e.en: That rule is {inapplicable} to part-time employees.
e.zh: 该规定不适用于兼职员工。

e.en: The old tax law is now {inapplicable} to digital services.
e.zh: 旧税法现在不适用于数字服务。

inappreciable.t: adj. 微不足道的；难以察觉的

e.en: The price difference between the two phones is {inappreciable}.
e.zh: 这两部手机的价差微不足道。

e.en: Adding sugar made an {inappreciable} change to the flavor.
e.zh: 加糖对味道带来微乎其微的改变。

inappropriate.t: adj. 不恰当的；不合适的

e.en: That joke was completely {inappropriate} for a work meeting.
e.zh: 那个笑话在工作会议上完全不合适。

e.en: The website filters out {inappropriate} content for children.
e.zh: 该网站过滤掉不适合儿童的内容。

e.en: He {inappropriately} touched her shoulder during the meeting.
e.zh: 他在会议中不当地触碰了她的肩膀。

e.en: The kids were dressed {inappropriately} for the cold weather.
e.zh: 孩子们的穿着不适合这种寒冷天气。

e.en: The {inappropriateness} of his comment shocked everyone.
e.zh: 他评论的不恰当让所有人都感到震惊。

e.en: She apologized for the {inappropriateness} of her outfit.
e.zh: 她为自己服装不得体而道歉。

inapt.t: adj. 不合适的；不擅长的

e.en: His comparison was {inapt} and confused the audience.
e.zh: 他的比喻不恰当,让听众感到困惑。

e.en: That metaphor seems {inapt} for this technical discussion.
e.zh: 那个比喻不太适合这种技术讨论。

e.en: Climate change is now an {inarguable} scientific fact.
e.zh: 气候变化如今已是无可争议的科学事实。

e.en: Her talent as a pianist is simply {inarguable}.
e.zh: 她作为钢琴家的才华是无可辩驳的。

inarticulate.t: adj. 口齿不清的；表达不清的

e.en: He became {inarticulate} when asked about his feelings.
e.zh: 被问到自己的感受时,他变得语无伦次。

e.en: The witness was too {inarticulate} to describe the suspect.
e.zh: 那位证人无法清楚地描述嫌疑人。

inarticulateness.t: n. 表达不清；口齿不清

e.en: His {inarticulateness} on stage cost him the debate.
e.zh: 他在台上表达不清,输掉了辩论。

e.en: Anger reduced the manager to complete {inarticulateness}.
e.zh: 愤怒让那位经理完全说不出话来。

e.en: The renovation looked cheap and {inartistic}.
e.zh: 那次翻修看起来廉价且毫无艺术感。

e.en: Critics called the film visually {inartistic} and dull.
e.zh: 评论家称这部电影视觉上毫无艺术性又乏味。

e.en: {Inasmuch} as you helped me, I'll return the favor.
e.zh: 既然你帮过我,我会回报你。

e.en: The rule applies {inasmuch} as the contract is valid.
e.zh: 该规则在合同有效的范围内适用。

e.en: His {inattention} during class led to failing grades.
e.zh: 他上课不专心导致成绩不及格。

e.en: Driver {inattention} causes thousands of accidents each year.
e.zh: 司机分心每年造成数千起事故。

inattentive.t: adj. 不专心的；漫不经心的

e.en: The waiter was {inattentive} and forgot our drinks.
e.zh: 那位服务员不够细心,忘了我们点的饮料。

e.en: Students grow {inattentive} after sitting still too long.
e.zh: 学生坐久了就会变得心不在焉。

inattentiveness.t: n. 不专心；注意力不集中

e.en: Her {inattentiveness} in meetings frustrated the entire team.
e.zh: 她开会时心不在焉让整个团队很沮丧。

e.en: Driver {inattentiveness} is a leading cause of crashes.
e.zh: 司机不专心是车祸的主要原因之一。

e.en: His whisper was {inaudible} over the loud music.
e.zh: 在嘈杂的音乐中,他的低语完全听不见。

e.en: The bat's calls are {inaudible} to human ears.
e.zh: 蝙蝠的叫声人耳无法听到。

e.en: She muttered {inaudibly} under her breath.
e.zh: 她低声嘟囔,几乎听不清。

e.en: The old fan hummed almost {inaudibly} in the corner.
e.zh: 那台旧风扇在角落里几乎无声地嗡嗡作响。

e.en: The president's {inaugural} address drew a massive crowd.
e.zh: 总统的就职演说吸引了大批民众。

e.en: This is the {inaugural} season of our podcast.
e.zh: 这是我们播客的首播季。

inaugurate.t: v. 为…举行就职典礼；开创

e.en: The mayor will {inaugurate} the new library tomorrow.
e.zh: 市长明天将为新图书馆揭幕。

e.en: They plan to {inaugurate} a scholarship in her name.
e.zh: 他们计划以她的名字设立奖学金。

inauguration.t: n. 就职典礼；开幕仪式

e.en: Millions watched the president's {inauguration} on television.
e.zh: 数百万人通过电视观看了总统的就职典礼。

e.en: The {inauguration} of the bridge attracted huge crowds.
e.zh: 大桥的启用仪式吸引了大批民众。

incoherently.t: adv. 语无伦次地；不连贯地

e.en: He mumbled {incoherently} in his sleep.
e.zh: 他在睡梦中含糊不清地嘟囔着。

e.en: She spoke {incoherently}, jumping from topic to topic.
e.zh: 她说话颠三倒四,话题跳来跳去。

e.en: Her monthly {income} barely covers the rent.
e.zh: 她每月的收入勉强够付房租。

e.en: Passive {income} from investments has grown nicely.
e.zh: 投资带来的被动收入增长得不错。

e.en: The village welcomed every {incomer} with a small gift.
e.zh: 村里给每位新来者都送上一份小礼物。

e.en: As an {incomer}, she took time to learn local customs.
e.zh: 作为外来者,她花了些时间学习当地习俗。

e.en: Households with low {incomes} qualify for the subsidy.
e.zh: 低收入家庭符合该补贴的申请条件。

e.en: Rising rents are eating into people's {incomes}.
e.zh: 不断上涨的房租正在吞噬人们的收入。

incoming.t:
adj. 传入的；即将上任的
n. 进入

e.en: Please silence your phone to avoid {incoming} call alerts.
e.zh: 请把手机静音以免来电提示打扰。

e.en: The {incoming} CEO will start next Monday.
e.zh: 新任首席执行官将于下周一上任。

incommensurability.t: n. 不可通约性；无法比较

e.en: Philosophers debate the {incommensurability} of different scientific paradigms.
e.zh: 哲学家们在讨论不同科学范式之间的不可通约性。

e.en: The {incommensurability} of these two cultures makes comparison difficult.
e.zh: 这两种文化的不可比性让对比变得很困难。

incommensurable.t: adj. 不可通约的；无法相比的

e.en: Happiness and money are essentially {incommensurable} values.
e.zh: 幸福与金钱本质上是无法相提并论的价值。

e.en: The two theories rest on {incommensurable} assumptions about reality.
e.zh: 这两种理论建立在对现实彼此无法通约的假设之上。

incommensurate.t: adj. 不相称的；不成比例的

e.en: His salary is {incommensurate} with his level of responsibility.
e.zh: 他的薪水与他承担的责任不相称。

e.en: The punishment seemed {incommensurate} with the minor offense.
e.zh: 惩罚似乎与这种轻微违规不相称。

incommunicado.t: adj./adv. 与外界隔绝地（被单独监禁）

e.en: He went {incommunicado} for a week while writing the novel.
e.zh: 他写小说期间足足一周与外界断绝了联系。

e.en: The journalist was held {incommunicado} for three days.
e.zh: 那名记者被隔离关押了三天,无法与外界联系。

incomparable.t: adj. 无与伦比的；无法比较的

e.en: The view from the summit is simply {incomparable}.
e.zh: 山顶的景色简直无与伦比。

e.en: Her talent for storytelling is {incomparable} among her peers.
e.zh: 她讲故事的天赋在同辈中无人能及。

incomparably.t: adv. 无比地；无可比拟地

e.en: This phone is {incomparably} faster than my old one.
e.zh: 这部手机比我旧手机快得不是一点半点。

e.en: She sings {incomparably} better after the lessons.
e.zh: 上完课后她唱得好太多了,简直无法相比。

e.en: The update fixed an {incompatibility} with older browsers.
e.zh: 该更新修复了与旧浏览器的不兼容问题。

e.en: Their divorce was attributed to personal {incompatibility}.
e.zh: 他们离婚的原因被归结为性格不合。

incompatible.t: adj. 不兼容的；不相容的

e.en: This charger is {incompatible} with the new model.
e.zh: 这款充电器与新机型不兼容。

e.en: Their work styles turned out to be totally {incompatible}.
e.zh: 他们的工作风格事实证明完全合不来。

e.en: The project failed due to sheer managerial {incompetence}.
e.zh: 项目失败完全是因为管理层无能。

e.en: Voters were furious at the government's {incompetence}.
e.zh: 选民对政府的无能感到非常愤怒。

e.en: The court ruled on his {incompetency} to stand trial.
e.zh: 法院裁定他无受审能力。

e.en: Repeated mistakes revealed the team's {incompetency}.
e.zh: 屡次出错暴露出团队的无能。

e.en: The contractor turned out to be completely {incompetent}.
e.zh: 那个承包商结果完全是个外行。

e.en: Don't blame the tools when the worker is {incompetent}.
e.zh: 工人不行时别怪工具。

e.en: The case was handled so {incompetently} that it was dismissed.
e.zh: 案子处理得太外行,结果被驳回了。

e.en: He played the piece {incompetently}, missing many notes.
e.zh: 他演奏这首曲子很糟糕,漏掉了不少音符。

incomplete.t: adj. 不完整的；未完成的

e.en: Your application is {incomplete} without a passport photo.
e.zh: 没有护照照片你的申请就是不完整的。

e.en: The novel was left {incomplete} when the author died.
e.zh: 作者去世时这部小说尚未完成。

incompletely.t: adv. 不完全地；未完成地

e.en: The form was filled out {incompletely}, so it was rejected.
e.zh: 表格填得不完整,所以被退回了。

e.en: The medication is only {incompletely} absorbed by the body.
e.zh: 这种药物只能被人体部分吸收。

e.en: The {incompleteness} of the data makes analysis difficult.
e.zh: 数据的不完整使分析变得困难。

e.en: Gödel proved the {incompleteness} of formal mathematical systems.
e.zh: 哥德尔证明了形式数学系统的不完备性。

e.en: The professor marked the assignment with an {incompletion}.
e.zh: 教授给那份作业打了个未完成。

e.en: The {incompletion} of the bridge has frustrated commuters for years.
e.zh: 大桥迟迟未完工让通勤者抱怨了好几年。

incomprehensibility.t: n. 难以理解；不可思议

e.en: The {incomprehensibility} of the legal jargon frustrated readers.
e.zh: 那些法律术语晦涩难懂,让读者很恼火。

e.en: Many people are struck by the {incomprehensibility} of quantum mechanics.
e.zh: 许多人都被量子力学的难以理解所震撼。

incomprehensible.t: adj. 难以理解的；费解的

e.en: The instructions were {incomprehensible} without a diagram.
e.zh: 没有图示,这些说明根本看不懂。

e.en: His thick accent made him almost {incomprehensible} to me.
e.zh: 他口音很重,我几乎听不懂他在说什么。

incomprehensibly.t: adv. 难以理解地；费解地

e.en: The teacher spoke {incomprehensibly} fast for beginners.
e.zh: 老师讲得快得让初学者完全听不懂。

e.en: {Incomprehensibly}, the company fired its best engineer.
e.zh: 令人费解的是,公司居然解雇了最优秀的工程师。

e.en: She stared at the equation in complete {incomprehension}.
e.zh: 她盯着那道方程式,完全摸不着头脑。

e.en: His face showed {incomprehension} when he read the message.
e.zh: 他读到那条消息时一脸茫然。

e.en: Water is treated as {incompressible} in most engineering calculations.
e.zh: 在大多数工程计算中,水被视作不可压缩的。

e.en: The data turned out to be largely {incompressible}.
e.zh: 这份数据基本上无法再被压缩。

inconceivable.t: adj. 不可思议的；难以想象的

e.en: It seems {inconceivable} that anyone would refuse the offer.
e.zh: 竟然有人会拒绝这个提议,真是难以想象。

e.en: A smartphone was {inconceivable} just fifty years ago.
e.zh: 在五十年前,智能手机简直无法想象。

inconceivably.t: adv. 难以想象地；不可思议地

e.en: The universe is {inconceivably} vast.
e.zh: 宇宙浩瀚得令人无法想象。

e.en: He grew {inconceivably} rich in only three years.
e.zh: 他短短三年就变得难以想象地富有。

inconclusive.t: adj. 无定论的；非决定性的

e.en: The test results were {inconclusive}, so they ran it again.
e.zh: 测试结果不明确,于是他们又做了一次。

e.en: The meeting ended on an {inconclusive} note.
e.zh: 会议在没有定论的情况下结束。

inconclusively.t: adv. 非决定性地；无结论地

e.en: The trial ended {inconclusively}, with no clear verdict.
e.zh: 庭审在没有明确判决的情况下结束。

e.en: They debated {inconclusively} for hours about the new design.
e.zh: 他们就新设计争论了几个小时,毫无结论。
