e.en: There's a clear {incongruence} between his words and actions.
e.zh: 他的言行之间存在明显的不一致。

e.en: The {incongruence} in the data raised questions about the study.
e.zh: 数据中的不一致引发了对研究的质疑。

incongruent.t: adj. 不一致的；不协调的

e.en: Her cheerful tone seemed {incongruent} with the sad news.
e.zh: 她欢快的语气与那则悲伤的消息显得很不协调。

e.en: The bright pink walls felt {incongruent} with the office's serious vibe.
e.zh: 亮粉色的墙面与办公室严肃的氛围很不搭。

incongruities.t: n. 不协调之处（incongruity 的复数）

e.en: Auditors flagged several {incongruities} in the financial report.
e.zh: 审计员在财务报告中标出了几处不一致之处。

e.en: The novel is full of charming {incongruities} and surreal moments.
e.zh: 小说中充满了迷人的违和感和超现实的瞬间。

e.en: There was an obvious {incongruity} between his suit and sneakers.
e.zh: 他西装配球鞋,看起来明显不搭。

e.en: Comedy often relies on {incongruity} to make people laugh.
e.zh: 喜剧常常靠反差感来逗人发笑。

incongruous.t: adj. 不协调的；不合时宜的

e.en: The modern sculpture looked {incongruous} in the old church.
e.zh: 那座现代雕塑放在古老教堂里显得格格不入。

e.en: His casual jokes seemed {incongruous} at the funeral.
e.zh: 他在葬礼上开的玩笑显得很不合时宜。

incongruously.t: adv. 不协调地；不合时宜地

e.en: A grand piano sat {incongruously} in the tiny kitchen.
e.zh: 一架大钢琴不协调地摆在那间小厨房里。

e.en: He laughed {incongruously} during the somber funeral.
e.zh: 他在肃穆的葬礼上不合时宜地笑了出来。

inconsequential.t: adj. 无关紧要的；微不足道的

e.en: The typo was {inconsequential} and easy to overlook.
e.zh: 这个错字无关紧要,很容易忽略。

e.en: Most of the meeting covered {inconsequential} details.
e.zh: 会议大部分时间都在讨论无关紧要的细节。

e.en: He chatted {inconsequentially} about the weather all afternoon.
e.zh: 他整个下午都在闲扯天气这种无关紧要的事。

e.en: The bug affected the output only {inconsequentially}.
e.zh: 这个漏洞对输出的影响微不足道。

inconsiderable.t: adj. 微不足道的；不值一提的

e.en: She earned a not {inconsiderable} sum from her startup.
e.zh: 她从自己的创业公司赚到了一笔不算少的钱。

e.en: The damage to the roof was {inconsiderable}.
e.zh: 屋顶的损坏程度并不严重。

inconsiderate.t: adj. 不体谅的；不顾他人的

e.en: It was {inconsiderate} to play loud music at midnight.
e.zh: 半夜大声放音乐真是不为别人着想。

e.en: Leaving the dishes for roommates is pretty {inconsiderate}.
e.zh: 把碗丢给室友洗实在很没公德心。

e.en: The detective spotted an {inconsistency} in his alibi.
e.zh: 侦探在他的不在场证明里发现了一个矛盾之处。

e.en: There's a clear {inconsistency} between the report and the data.
e.zh: 报告和数据之间存在明显的不一致。

inconsistent.t: adj. 不一致的；前后矛盾的

e.en: His test scores have been {inconsistent} this semester.
e.zh: 他这学期的考试成绩起伏不定。

e.en: The witness gave {inconsistent} accounts of the accident.
e.zh: 目击者对事故的描述前后不一致。

inconsistently.t: adv. 不一致地；前后矛盾地

e.en: The app crashes {inconsistently}, making bugs hard to reproduce.
e.zh: 这个应用崩溃毫无规律,导致漏洞很难复现。

e.en: She trains {inconsistently} and her progress shows it.
e.zh: 她训练不规律,进步也明显跟不上。

inconsolable.t: adj. 无法安慰的；悲痛欲绝的

e.en: The child was {inconsolable} after losing his puppy.
e.zh: 那个孩子弄丢了小狗后伤心得无法安慰。

e.en: Fans were {inconsolable} when the band broke up.
e.zh: 乐队解散时,粉丝们悲痛欲绝。

inconsolably.t: adv. 无法安慰地；悲痛欲绝地

e.en: She wept {inconsolably} at her grandmother's funeral.
e.zh: 她在外婆的葬礼上哭得无法自抑。

e.en: The toddler sobbed {inconsolably} when his balloon popped.
e.zh: 气球破了,小家伙哭得怎么哄都没用。

inconspicuous.t: adj. 不显眼的；不引人注意的

e.en: The spy wore plain clothes to stay {inconspicuous}.
e.zh: 那名间谍穿着便装以免引人注意。

e.en: The settings menu is in an {inconspicuous} corner.
e.zh: 设置菜单在一个不显眼的角落里。

e.en: He slipped out of the meeting {inconspicuously}.
e.zh: 他不动声色地溜出了会议室。

e.en: The camera was mounted {inconspicuously} above the door.
e.zh: 摄像头不显眼地装在门的上方。

e.en: The poem laments the {inconstancy} of human affection.
e.zh: 这首诗哀叹人类感情的反复无常。

e.en: Investors worry about the {inconstancy} of the new market.
e.zh: 投资者担心这个新市场变化无常。

inconstant.t: adj. 易变的；反复无常的

e.en: The weather here is famously {inconstant} in spring.
e.zh: 这里春天的天气出了名地变化无常。

e.en: He proved an {inconstant} friend during the crisis.
e.zh: 危机时刻,他被证明是个靠不住的朋友。

incontestable.t: adj. 无可争辩的；不容置疑的

e.en: The DNA evidence was {incontestable} in court.
e.zh: DNA证据在法庭上无可争议。

e.en: Her talent for design is {incontestable}.
e.zh: 她的设计天赋无可置疑。

incontinence.t:
n. 失禁（大小便不能自控）
n. 不节制

e.en: Adult diapers help manage urinary {incontinence} discreetly.
e.zh: 成人纸尿裤能不动声色地应对尿失禁问题。

e.en: The medication caused temporary {incontinence} as a side effect.
e.zh: 这种药物引起了暂时性的失禁副作用。

incontinent.t:
adj. 失禁的
adj. 无节制的

e.en: Elderly patients may become {incontinent} after a stroke.
e.zh: 年长的病人在中风后可能会出现失禁。

e.en: The vet said the old dog is now {incontinent}.
e.zh: 兽医说这只老狗现在已经无法控制大小便了。

incontrovertible.t: adj. 无可辩驳的，确凿的

e.en: The video provided {incontrovertible} proof of the crime.
e.zh: 这段视频为这起罪行提供了无可辩驳的证据。

e.en: Climate scientists cite {incontrovertible} data on warming.
e.zh: 气候科学家引用了关于气候变暖的确凿数据。

incontrovertibly.t: adv. 无可辩驳地，确凿无疑地

e.en: The lab results {incontrovertibly} confirmed the diagnosis.
e.zh: 化验结果毫无争议地确认了诊断。

e.en: She is {incontrovertibly} the best player on the team.
e.zh: 她无可争辩地是队里最强的球员。

inconvenience.t:
n. 不便，麻烦
v. 给…带来不便

e.en: We apologize for any {inconvenience} caused by the outage.
e.zh: 对停电造成的不便我们深表歉意。

e.en: Taking the detour was a minor {inconvenience}.
e.zh: 绕道而行只是个小小的麻烦。

inconvenient.t: adj. 不方便的，造成麻烦的

e.en: Sorry, is now an {inconvenient} time to talk?
e.zh: 抱歉,现在聊天是不是不太方便?

e.en: The store's location is {inconvenient} for most customers.
e.zh: 这家店的位置对大多数顾客来说很不方便。

e.en: The bus stop is {inconveniently} located far from town.
e.zh: 公交站位置很不方便,离镇上挺远。

e.en: My phone died {inconveniently} right before the meeting.
e.zh: 我的手机偏偏在会议前没电了,真不凑巧。

incorporate.t:
v. 纳入，整合
v. 组建公司

e.en: We'll {incorporate} your feedback into the next release.
e.zh: 我们会把你的反馈纳入下一个版本中。

e.en: Try to {incorporate} more vegetables into your meals.
e.zh: 试着在饮食中加入更多蔬菜。

incorporated.t:
adj. 股份有限（Inc.）
v. 已整合的

e.en: The new design {incorporated} ideas from several teams.
e.zh: 新设计融合了几个团队的想法。

e.en: She {incorporated} her business in Delaware last year.
e.zh: 她去年在特拉华州把自己的公司注册成了法人。

incorporates.t: v. 纳入，包含（第三人称单数）

e.en: The latest model {incorporates} a faster neural engine.
e.zh: 最新款机型搭载了更快的神经引擎。

e.en: Her dance routine {incorporates} both ballet and hip-hop.
e.zh: 她的舞蹈编排融合了芭蕾和街舞。

incorporating.t: v. 正在纳入、整合（现在分词）

e.en: They redesigned the app, {incorporating} dark mode by default.
e.zh: 他们重新设计了应用,默认加入了深色模式。

e.en: The chef created a dish {incorporating} local seasonal produce.
e.zh: 主厨做了一道融入当地时令食材的菜。

incorporation.t:
n. 合并，整合
n. 公司注册成立

e.en: The {incorporation} of AI features boosted user engagement.
e.zh: 加入AI功能后,用户的活跃度大幅提升。

e.en: Filing for {incorporation} took only a few days online.
e.zh: 在网上申请公司注册只花了几天时间。

incorporeal.t: adj. 无形体的，非物质的

e.en: Ghosts are usually depicted as {incorporeal} beings.
e.zh: 鬼魂通常被描绘成没有实体的存在。

e.en: Ideas are {incorporeal}, yet they shape the world.
e.zh: 思想没有形体,却塑造着这个世界。

e.en: Your password is {incorrect}; please try again.
e.zh: 密码错误,请重新输入。

e.en: The textbook contains several {incorrect} historical dates.
e.zh: 教科书里有几个历史日期是错误的。

e.en: The package was {incorrectly} addressed and returned to sender.
e.zh: 包裹地址写错了,被退回给寄件人。

e.en: He {incorrectly} assumed the meeting was canceled.
e.zh: 他误以为会议取消了。

e.en: The audit revealed the {incorrectness} of last quarter's report.
e.zh: 审计揭示出上季度报告的错误。

e.en: She gently pointed out the {incorrectness} of his claim.
e.zh: 她委婉地指出了他说法的不正确。

incorrigibility.t: n. 不可救药，积习难改

e.en: His {incorrigibility} frustrated even the most patient teachers.
e.zh: 他屡教不改,连最有耐心的老师都束手无策。

e.en: The judge cited the teen's {incorrigibility} in her ruling.
e.zh: 法官在判决中提到了这名少年的难以管教。

incorrigible.t: adj. 不可救药的，屡教不改的

e.en: He's an {incorrigible} flirt at every office party.
e.zh: 每次公司派对上他都是个无可救药的调情高手。

e.en: Her {incorrigible} optimism kept the team going.
e.zh: 她那改不掉的乐观让团队一直撑了下来。

e.en: He is {incorrigibly} late to every single meeting.
e.zh: 每次会议他都死性不改地迟到。

e.en: She remained {incorrigibly} cheerful despite the bad news.
e.zh: 尽管消息不好,她依然顽固地保持开朗。

incorruptibility.t: n. 廉洁正直，不可腐蚀

e.en: The judge was respected for her absolute {incorruptibility}.
e.zh: 那位法官因绝对的廉洁正直而备受尊敬。

e.en: Voters value {incorruptibility} above charisma in officials.
e.zh: 选民看重官员的廉洁,远胜于其个人魅力。

incorruptible.t:
adj. 廉洁的，不受贿的
adj. 不腐坏的

e.en: The city needs {incorruptible} officials to restore trust.
e.zh: 这座城市需要廉洁的官员来重建信任。

e.en: Blockchain records are designed to be {incorruptible}.
e.zh: 区块链记录的设计目标就是不可篡改。

increase.t:
v. 增加，增长
n. 增长，增幅

e.en: Sales {increase} sharply during the holiday season.
e.zh: 假日季销售额大幅上涨。

e.en: The company announced a 5% pay {increase}.
e.zh: 公司宣布加薪百分之五。

increased.t:
v. 已增加（过去式）
adj. 增加的

e.en: Rent has {increased} by twenty percent this year.
e.zh: 今年房租上涨了百分之二十。

e.en: The new policy brought {increased} attention to mental health.
e.zh: 新政策让心理健康问题得到了更多关注。

increases.t:
v. 增加（第三人称单数）
n. 增幅（复数）

e.en: Exercise {increases} blood flow to the brain.
e.zh: 运动能增加流向大脑的血液。

e.en: The chart shows steady {increases} in monthly users.
e.zh: 图表显示每月用户数稳步增长。

increasing.t:
adj. 日益增加的
v. 正在增加

e.en: There's {increasing} demand for remote work options.
e.zh: 对远程工作选项的需求正在不断增长。

e.en: She felt {increasing} pressure as the deadline approached.
e.zh: 随着截止日期临近,她感到压力越来越大。

e.en: Teens are {increasingly} turning to short-form video.
e.zh: 青少年越来越倾向于观看短视频。

e.en: The job market is {increasingly} competitive for new graduates.
e.zh: 对应届毕业生来说,就业市场竞争越来越激烈。

incredible.t:
adj. 难以置信的
adj. 极好的，惊人的

e.en: The view from the summit was absolutely {incredible}.
e.zh: 山顶上的景色简直令人惊叹。

e.en: She told an {incredible} story about meeting her idol.
e.zh: 她讲了一个关于见到偶像的不可思议的故事。

incredibly.t:
adv. 极其，非常
adv. 难以置信地

e.en: The new phone is {incredibly} thin and light.
e.zh: 这款新手机薄得不可思议,也非常轻。

e.en: He's {incredibly} good at remembering people's names.
e.zh: 他记别人名字的本事强得离谱。

e.en: She stared at the bill in {incredulity}.
e.zh: 她难以置信地盯着那张账单。

e.en: His claims were met with widespread {incredulity} online.
e.zh: 他的说法在网上遭到普遍质疑。

e.en: He gave her an {incredulous} look when she said that.
e.zh: 听她那么说,他露出难以置信的表情。

e.en: Fans were {incredulous} at the surprise album drop.
e.zh: 歌迷对这张突然发布的专辑感到难以置信。

incredulously.t: adv. 怀疑地，难以置信地

e.en: "You did what?" he asked {incredulously}.
e.zh: “你做了什么?”他难以置信地问道。

e.en: She stared {incredulously} at the price tag.
e.zh: 她难以置信地盯着价格标签。

increment.t:
n. 增量，增幅
v. 递增（编程）

e.en: Salaries rise by a small {increment} each year.
e.zh: 工资每年都会有小幅度的递增。

e.en: The volume goes up by one {increment} per click.
e.zh: 每点击一次,音量就上升一格。

e.en: The update brings {incremental} improvements to battery life.
e.zh: 这次更新对电池续航做出了渐进式的改善。

e.en: We're seeing {incremental} progress on the project.
e.zh: 我们看到这个项目正在逐步推进。

incrementalism.t: n. 渐进主义，循序渐进

e.en: Critics argue {incrementalism} won't solve the climate crisis.
e.zh: 批评者认为渐进主义无法解决气候危机。

e.en: The reform favored {incrementalism} over radical change.
e.zh: 这项改革偏向渐进路线,而非激进变革。

e.en: We rolled out the feature {incrementally} to avoid bugs.
e.zh: 我们逐步上线这个功能,以避免出现漏洞。

e.en: Practice a few minutes daily and improve {incrementally}.
e.zh: 每天练几分钟,水平就能逐步提升。

e.en: The emails could {incriminate} several senior executives.
e.zh: 这些邮件可能会让多名高管陷入罪责。

e.en: He refused to {incriminate} his former business partner.
e.zh: 他拒绝指证他以前的生意伙伴。

incriminating.t: adj. 使人显得有罪的，定罪的

e.en: Police found {incriminating} evidence on his laptop.
e.zh: 警方在他的笔记本电脑上发现了犯罪证据。

e.en: She deleted the {incriminating} text messages immediately.
e.zh: 她立刻删除了那些有罪证的短信。

e.en: He stayed silent to avoid self-{incrimination}.
e.zh: 他保持沉默以避免自证其罪。

e.en: The lawyer warned against any {incrimination} of his client.
e.zh: 律师警告不得对其当事人进行任何指控。

e.en: A thick {incrustation} of salt covered the old pipes.
e.zh: 旧管道上覆盖着厚厚的一层盐垢。

e.en: The kettle has a hard {incrustation} of limescale inside.
e.zh: 水壶内部结了一层硬硬的水垢。

incubate.t:
v. 孵化
v. 孕育（想法、项目）

e.en: Hens {incubate} their eggs for about three weeks.
e.zh: 母鸡孵蛋大约需要三周时间。

e.en: The startup will {incubate} new ideas for six months.
e.zh: 这家初创公司将用六个月孵化新想法。

incubation.t:
n. 孵化
n. 潜伏期

e.en: The virus has an {incubation} period of five days.
e.zh: 该病毒的潜伏期为五天。

e.en: The project is still in its {incubation} phase.
e.zh: 这个项目仍处于孵化阶段。

incubator.t: n. 孵化器（创业、保温箱）

e.en: The premature baby was placed in an {incubator}.
e.zh: 那个早产儿被放进了保温箱里。

e.en: Y Combinator is a famous startup {incubator} in California.
e.zh: Y Combinator 是加州著名的创业孵化器。

incubus.t:
n. 梦魇，压迫感
n. 男性梦淫妖

e.en: Debt became an {incubus} that haunted him every night.
e.zh: 债务成了每晚困扰他的梦魇。

e.en: Medieval legends often described an {incubus} visiting sleepers.
e.zh: 中世纪传说常描述梦魇恶魔造访睡梦中的人。

inculcate.t: v. 反复灌输（思想、观念）

e.en: Parents try to {inculcate} good habits in their children.
e.zh: 父母努力把好习惯灌输给孩子。

e.en: The school aims to {inculcate} discipline from an early age.
e.zh: 学校致力于从小培养学生的纪律观念。

e.en: The {inculcation} of values takes years of patient teaching.
e.zh: 价值观的灌输需要多年耐心的教导。

e.en: Military training relies heavily on the {inculcation} of obedience.
e.zh: 军事训练在很大程度上依赖于对服从的灌输。

e.en: His own diary served to {inculpate} him at trial.
e.zh: 他的日记在审判中反而成了指控他的证据。

e.en: The witness refused to {inculpate} her colleagues.
e.zh: 那名证人拒绝指控她的同事。

e.en: Missionaries discussed the {inculturation} of faith into local traditions.
e.zh: 传教士讨论了信仰与当地传统的本土化融合。

e.en: The church promotes {inculturation} rather than cultural replacement.
e.zh: 教会推动文化融合而非文化取代。

incumbency.t:
n. 任期，在任
n. 职责

e.en: His {incumbency} as mayor lasted nearly a decade.
e.zh: 他担任市长的任期持续了将近十年。

e.en: Voters often favor candidates with {incumbency} advantages.
e.zh: 选民往往倾向于拥有现任优势的候选人。

incumbent.t:
adj. 现任的
n. 在任者

e.en: The {incumbent} senator is running for reelection this fall.
e.zh: 现任参议员将在今年秋天竞选连任。

e.en: It is {incumbent} on managers to support their teams.
e.zh: 管理者有责任支持自己的团队。

incumbents.t: n. 现任者，在职者（复数）

e.en: Most {incumbents} won their seats in the recent election.
e.zh: 大多数现任议员在最近的选举中保住了席位。

e.en: Tech startups are challenging traditional {incumbents} in finance.
e.zh: 科技初创公司正在挑战金融业的老牌巨头。

incur.t: v. 招致、引起（后果、费用）

e.en: You may {incur} extra fees for late payment.
e.zh: 逾期付款可能会产生额外费用。

e.en: The company will {incur} losses this quarter.
e.zh: 公司本季度将出现亏损。

incurable.t: adj. 无法治愈的；无可救药的

e.en: She was diagnosed with an {incurable} but manageable disease.
e.zh: 她被诊断出患有无法治愈但可控制的疾病。

e.en: He's an {incurable} romantic who believes in love at first sight.
e.zh: 他是个无可救药的浪漫主义者,相信一见钟情。

incurably.t: adv. 无法治愈地；无可救药地

e.en: My grandfather is {incurably} optimistic about the future.
e.zh: 我祖父对未来有着无可救药的乐观。

e.en: The patient is {incurably} ill but in good spirits.
e.zh: 病人病情无法治愈,但精神状态不错。

incurious.t: adj. 不感兴趣的；缺乏好奇心的

e.en: He gave the painting an {incurious} glance and walked on.
e.zh: 他漫不经心地瞥了一眼那幅画就走开了。

e.en: The students seemed {incurious} about the world beyond their phones.
e.zh: 这些学生似乎对手机以外的世界毫无好奇心。

incurred.t: v. incur 的过去式/过去分词

e.en: She {incurred} huge debts during her time at university.
e.zh: 她在大学期间欠下了巨额债务。

e.en: The repairs {incurred} costs we hadn't budgeted for.
e.zh: 维修产生了我们没有预算到的费用。

e.en: He apologized for {incurring} the boss's anger.
e.zh: 他为招致老板的愤怒而道歉。

e.en: They expanded carefully, avoiding {incurring} unnecessary debt.
e.zh: 他们谨慎扩张,避免背上不必要的债务。

incurs.t: v. incur 的第三人称单数

e.en: Each international transfer {incurs} a small bank fee.
e.zh: 每笔国际汇款都会产生一笔小额银行手续费。

e.en: Skipping class {incurs} a penalty under school rules.
e.zh: 按校规,旷课会受到处罚。

e.en: The {incursion} into enemy territory lasted only a few hours.
e.zh: 对敌方领土的入侵只持续了几个小时。

e.en: Streaming services made a major {incursion} into traditional TV.
e.zh: 流媒体服务大举进军传统电视行业。

incus.t: n. 砧骨（中耳的听小骨）

e.en: The {incus} is one of three tiny bones in the middle ear.
e.zh: 砧骨是中耳三块小骨之一。

e.en: Damage to the {incus} can lead to hearing loss.
e.zh: 砧骨受损可能导致听力丧失。

ind.t: n. 印度（India 的旧缩写，罕用）

e.en: The abbreviation {ind}. on the form means "individual."
e.zh: 表格上的缩写 ind. 表示"个人"。

e.en: Old maps sometimes label India simply as {Ind}.
e.zh: 旧地图有时仅将印度标注为 Ind。

e.en: I'm deeply {indebted} to my mentor for her guidance.
e.zh: 我非常感激导师对我的指导。

e.en: Many graduates remain heavily {indebted} for years after school.
e.zh: 许多毕业生在毕业后多年仍背负沉重债务。

e.en: Household {indebtedness} has reached a record high.
e.zh: 家庭负债已经达到创纪录的高点。

e.en: She expressed her {indebtedness} to everyone who supported her.
e.zh: 她对所有支持过她的人表达了感激之情。

e.en: He was fined for public {indecency} downtown.
e.zh: 他因在市中心有伤风化的行为被罚款。

e.en: The film was banned for its {indecency} in several countries.
e.zh: 这部电影因内容不雅在多个国家被禁。

e.en: They left the party with {indecent} haste.
e.zh: 他们以失礼的速度匆忙离开了派对。

e.en: The post was removed for containing {indecent} images.
e.zh: 该帖子因含有不雅图片而被删除。

e.en: The CEO was paid {indecently} large bonuses last year.
e.zh: 那位 CEO 去年拿到了大得离谱的奖金。

e.en: He dressed {indecently} for such a formal occasion.
e.zh: 在如此正式的场合,他穿得很不得体。

indecipherable.t: adj. 无法辨认的、难以破译的

e.en: His handwriting is completely {indecipherable} to me.
e.zh: 他的字迹我完全无法辨认。

e.en: The ancient inscription remained {indecipherable} for centuries.
e.zh: 那段古代铭文几个世纪以来一直无法破译。

e.en: Her {indecision} cost the team valuable time.
e.zh: 她的犹豫不决让团队浪费了宝贵的时间。

e.en: Years of {indecision} kept him in the wrong job.
e.zh: 多年的优柔寡断让他困在不合适的工作中。

indecisive.t: adj. 优柔寡断的；无决定性的

e.en: He's too {indecisive} to choose a restaurant for dinner.
e.zh: 他太优柔寡断,连晚餐去哪家餐厅都拿不定主意。

e.en: The election results were {indecisive}, requiring a runoff.
e.zh: 选举结果未分胜负,需要进行决选。

e.en: She shrugged {indecisively} when asked about her plans.
e.zh: 被问到她的打算时,她犹豫地耸了耸肩。

e.en: He hovered {indecisively} between the two job offers.
e.zh: 他在两份工作邀约之间犹豫不决。

e.en: His {indecisiveness} frustrated the entire project team.
e.zh: 他的优柔寡断让整个项目组都很沮丧。

e.en: Leadership requires action, not chronic {indecisiveness}.
e.zh: 领导力需要行动,而不是长期的犹豫不决。

e.en: Laughing at the funeral was considered highly {indecorous}.
e.zh: 在葬礼上大笑被认为是非常失礼的。

e.en: He apologized for his {indecorous} remarks at dinner.
e.zh: 他为自己晚餐时不得体的言论道歉。

e.en: The new phone is fast, and very expensive {indeed}.
e.zh: 这款新手机速度很快,而且确实非常昂贵。

e.en: "Are you tired?" "{Indeed} I am."
e.zh: "你累了吗?""我确实累了。"

indefatigable.t: adj. 不知疲倦的、坚持不懈的

e.en: She is an {indefatigable} advocate for children's rights.
e.zh: 她是一位不知疲倦的儿童权益倡导者。

e.en: His {indefatigable} energy kept the team going past midnight.
e.zh: 他不知疲倦的精力让团队一直工作到午夜之后。

e.en: She works {indefatigably} to clean up the local river.
e.zh: 她不知疲倦地致力于清理当地河流。

e.en: The volunteers campaigned {indefatigably} through the cold winter.
e.zh: 志愿者们在寒冬里坚持不懈地开展活动。

indefensible.t: adj. 无法辩解的；难以防守的

e.en: His behavior at the meeting was simply {indefensible}.
e.zh: 他在会上的行为根本无法辩解。

e.en: The old fortress proved {indefensible} against modern weapons.
e.zh: 这座古老的要塞在现代武器面前不堪一击。

indefinable.t: adj. 难以描述的、无法定义的

e.en: There's an {indefinable} charm about this little café.
e.zh: 这家小咖啡馆有一种难以言喻的魅力。

e.en: She felt an {indefinable} sadness as she left.
e.zh: 离开时她感到一种说不清的伤感。

e.en: The room felt {indefinably} different after the renovation.
e.zh: 装修后,房间给人一种说不出的不同感觉。

e.en: He was {indefinably} changed by his year abroad.
e.zh: 在国外的那一年让他发生了难以形容的变化。

indefinite.t: adj. 不确定的、无限期的

e.en: The project has been postponed for an {indefinite} period.
e.zh: 该项目已被无限期推迟。

e.en: "A" and "an" are {indefinite} articles in English.
e.zh: "a" 和 "an" 是英语中的不定冠词。

indefinitely.t: adv. 无限期地、不确定地

e.en: The meeting has been postponed {indefinitely} due to weather.
e.zh: 会议因天气原因被无限期推迟。

e.en: You can't store fresh milk {indefinitely} in the fridge.
e.zh: 鲜奶不能在冰箱里无限期保存。

e.en: That trip left an {indelible} impression on me.
e.zh: 那次旅行给我留下了难以磨灭的印象。

e.en: Use an {indelible} marker to label your luggage.
e.zh: 用不褪色的记号笔在行李上做标记。

e.en: That summer is {indelibly} etched in my memory.
e.zh: 那个夏天深深地刻在我的记忆里。

e.en: The scandal {indelibly} stained his political reputation.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻给他的政治声誉留下了无法抹去的污点。

e.en: It was {indelicate} of him to ask about her salary.
e.zh: 他询问她的薪水实在是不太得体。

e.en: She made an {indelicate} joke that embarrassed the guests.
e.zh: 她开了一个让客人尴尬的不得体玩笑。

e.en: The contract includes {indemnification} for any legal damages.
e.zh: 合同包含针对任何法律损失的赔偿条款。

e.en: They sought {indemnification} from the insurer after the fire.
e.zh: 火灾后他们向保险公司寻求赔偿。

e.en: The company agreed to {indemnify} customers for the data breach.
e.zh: 公司同意就数据泄露事件赔偿客户。

e.en: This clause will {indemnify} the contractor against third-party claims.
e.zh: 此条款将保障承包商免受第三方索赔。

e.en: The airline paid {indemnity} for the lost luggage.
e.zh: 航空公司就丢失的行李支付了赔偿金。

e.en: Most professionals carry an {indemnity} insurance policy.
e.zh: 大多数专业人士都会购买职业责任保险。

indent.t:
v. 缩进（文本）
n. 凹口、订单

e.en: Please {indent} the first line of every paragraph.
e.zh: 请将每段的第一行缩进。

e.en: The code won't run if you forget to {indent} the loop.
e.zh: 如果忘了给循环缩进，代码就跑不起来。

e.en: Python relies on {indentation} to define code blocks.
e.zh: Python 依靠缩进来划分代码块。

e.en: The editor automatically fixes inconsistent {indentation}.
e.zh: 编辑器会自动修正不一致的缩进。

e.en: Each bullet point should be {indented} two spaces.
e.zh: 每个项目符号应缩进两个空格。

e.en: The quoted paragraph is {indented} from the main text.
e.zh: 引用的段落从正文中缩进显示。

e.en: He spent an hour {indenting} the messy JSON file.
e.zh: 他花了一小时给混乱的 JSON 文件缩进。

e.en: {Indenting} nested lists makes them easier to read.
e.zh: 给嵌套列表缩进可以让它们更易读。

e.en: The IDE includes a built-in {indentor} for Python files.
e.zh: 该 IDE 内置了一个用于 Python 文件的缩进工具。

e.en: He wrote a small {indentor} script to clean up logs.
e.zh: 他写了一个小缩进脚本来整理日志。

indents.t: v./n. indent 的复数或第三人称单数

e.en: The formatter removed all extra {indents} from the file.
e.zh: 格式化工具移除了文件中所有多余的缩进。

e.en: Her essay {indents} every new paragraph by half an inch.
e.zh: 她的论文每个新段落缩进半英寸。

indenture.t:
n. 契约、合同
v. 以契约约束

e.en: The apprentice signed an {indenture} with the master craftsman.
e.zh: 学徒与师傅签订了一份契约。

e.en: The bond {indenture} spells out the issuer's obligations.
e.zh: 该债券契约详细说明了发行人的义务。

indentured.t: adj. 受契约束缚的（劳工）

e.en: Many workers came as {indentured} laborers in the colonies.
e.zh: 许多工人作为契约劳工来到殖民地。

e.en: She felt {indentured} to her employer because of the contract.
e.zh: 由于合同，她觉得自己像是被雇主束缚的契约工。

e.en: India gained {independence} from Britain in 1947.
e.zh: 印度于 1947 年从英国获得独立。

e.en: Working from home gave her a real sense of {independence}.
e.zh: 在家工作让她有了真正的独立感。

e.en: The textbook compares the {independences} of several African nations.
e.zh: 教科书比较了几个非洲国家的独立历程。

e.en: Statisticians test the {independences} between paired variables.
e.zh: 统计学家会检验配对变量之间的独立性。

e.en: She became financially {independent} right after college.
e.zh: 她大学一毕业就实现了经济独立。

e.en: An {independent} review confirmed the lab's results.
e.zh: 一项独立的评审证实了实验室的结果。

e.en: Two teams arrived at the same conclusion {independently}.
e.zh: 两个团队各自独立地得出了相同的结论。

e.en: The kids learned to dress {independently} by age four.
e.zh: 孩子们四岁前就学会了自己穿衣服。

e.en: The chemist Leonid {Inder} contributed to early thermodynamics research.
e.zh: 化学家列昂尼德·因德对早期热力学研究做出了贡献。

e.en: The village of {Inder} sits beside a salty lake in Kazakhstan.
e.zh: 因德尔村坐落在哈萨克斯坦一个咸水湖旁。

indescribable.t: adj. 难以形容的、无法描述的

e.en: The view from the summit was simply {indescribable}.
e.zh: 山顶的景色简直无法形容。

e.en: She felt an {indescribable} joy when her son was born.
e.zh: 儿子出生时，她感到一种难以言表的喜悦。

e.en: The dessert was {indescribably} delicious.
e.zh: 那道甜点美味得无法形容。

e.en: He was {indescribably} sad after losing his dog.
e.zh: 失去爱犬后，他难过得无以言表。

indiscernible.t: adj. 难以辨别的；无法区分的

e.en: The difference between the two paint colors is nearly {indiscernible}.
e.zh: 这两种颜料的差别几乎察觉不出来。

e.en: His whisper was {indiscernible} over the loud music.
e.zh: 在嘈杂的音乐声中他的耳语完全听不清。

e.en: The coach blamed the loss on team {indiscipline}.
e.zh: 教练把失利归咎于球队纪律涣散。

e.en: Repeated {indiscipline} in class led to his suspension.
e.zh: 屡次在课堂上违纪导致他被停学。

e.en: It was {indiscreet} of him to share private emails publicly.
e.zh: 他公开分享私人邮件实在太轻率了。

e.en: She regretted her {indiscreet} comments about her boss.
e.zh: 她对自己关于老板的轻率言论感到后悔。

e.en: He {indiscreetly} mentioned the surprise party to the host.
e.zh: 他不慎向主人提起了那个惊喜派对。

e.en: She {indiscreetly} forwarded the confidential email to a friend.
e.zh: 她轻率地把机密邮件转发给了朋友。

indiscrete.t: adj. 未分开的；浑然一体的

e.en: The mass appeared as one {indiscrete} blob under the microscope.
e.zh: 在显微镜下,这团东西看上去是不可分的一块。

e.en: The data formed an {indiscrete} continuum rather than separate groups.
e.zh: 这些数据形成连续体,而非分立的组别。

indiscretion.t: n. 不慎重的言行；轻率之举

e.en: A youthful {indiscretion} cost him the job offer.
e.zh: 年轻时的一次轻率之举让他丢了那份工作机会。

e.en: The senator apologized for his moment of {indiscretion}.
e.zh: 那位参议员为自己一时的失言道歉。

e.en: The tabloids kept digging up the actor's past {indiscretions}.
e.zh: 小报不断翻出那位演员过去的不检点行为。

e.en: He paid dearly for his financial {indiscretions}.
e.zh: 他为自己在财务上的轻率付出了沉重代价。

indiscriminate.t: adj. 不加选择的；一视同仁的

e.en: The bombing caused {indiscriminate} harm to civilians.
e.zh: 那次轰炸对平民造成了不分对象的伤害。

e.en: Her {indiscriminate} spending quickly drained the savings account.
e.zh: 她毫无节制的花销很快掏空了储蓄账户。

indiscriminately.t: adv. 不加选择地；任意地

e.en: The virus spreads {indiscriminately} across age groups.
e.zh: 这种病毒在各年龄段不加区分地传播。

e.en: He hands out compliments {indiscriminately} at parties.
e.zh: 他在派对上毫无分别地恭维每个人。

indiscrimination.t: n. 不加区别；无差别对待

e.en: The judge criticized the {indiscrimination} shown in the arrests.
e.zh: 法官批评了逮捕中表现出的不加区分。

e.en: Her {indiscrimination} in choosing friends often led to trouble.
e.zh: 她选朋友不加区别,常常因此惹麻烦。

indispensability.t: n. 不可或缺性；必不可少

e.en: The pandemic proved the {indispensability} of healthcare workers.
e.zh: 疫情证明了医护人员不可或缺的重要性。

e.en: No one should overestimate their own {indispensability} at work.
e.zh: 没人应该高估自己在工作中的不可替代性。

indispensable.t: adj. 不可或缺的；必需的

e.en: A good search engine has become {indispensable} for students.
e.zh: 一个好用的搜索引擎已成为学生不可或缺的工具。

e.en: She quickly made herself {indispensable} to the team.
e.zh: 她很快让自己成为团队中不可或缺的一员。

e.en: His advice proved {indispensible} during the negotiations.
e.zh: 他的建议在谈判中显得不可或缺。

e.en: A reliable laptop is {indispensible} for remote workers.
e.zh: 一台可靠的笔记本电脑对远程工作者必不可少。

indisposed.t: adj. 略感不适的；不愿意的

e.en: The singer canceled the show because she was {indisposed}.
e.zh: 那位歌手因身体不适取消了演出。

e.en: He felt {indisposed} after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后他感觉身体不太舒服。

e.en: A sudden {indisposition} kept her from attending the meeting.
e.zh: 突如其来的身体不适让她无法参加会议。

e.en: The minister cited an {indisposition} as reason for his absence.
e.zh: 那位部长以身体不适为由解释了缺席。

indisputable.t: adj. 无可争辩的；确凿的

e.en: The DNA evidence provides {indisputable} proof of his innocence.
e.zh: DNA证据为他的清白提供了无可争辩的证明。

e.en: Her talent as a pianist is {indisputable}.
e.zh: 她作为钢琴家的才华毋庸置疑。

indisputably.t: adv. 无可争辩地；确凿地

e.en: The new model is {indisputably} faster than its predecessor.
e.zh: 新款无可争议地比上一代更快。

e.en: He is {indisputably} the best player on the team.
e.zh: 他无疑是队里最优秀的球员。

indissoluble.t: adj. 不可分解的；牢不可破的

e.en: They formed an {indissoluble} bond during the long voyage.
e.zh: 他们在漫长的航程中结下了牢不可破的情谊。

e.en: Marriage was once seen as an {indissoluble} contract.
e.zh: 婚姻曾被视为不可解除的契约。

indissolubly.t: adv. 不可分解地；牢固地

e.en: The two families are {indissolubly} linked through marriage.
e.zh: 这两个家族通过联姻紧密相连,密不可分。

e.en: His name is {indissolubly} associated with the scandal.
e.zh: 他的名字与那场丑闻永远地联系在了一起。

indistinct.t: adj. 模糊不清的；朦胧的

e.en: The voices on the recording were faint and {indistinct}.
e.zh: 录音里的声音微弱而模糊不清。

e.en: In the fog, the mountains looked {indistinct} and distant.
e.zh: 在雾中,群山看起来模糊而遥远。

e.en: He muttered {indistinctly} into the microphone.
e.zh: 他对着麦克风含糊地嘟囔着。

e.en: She remembered the dream only {indistinctly} the next morning.
e.zh: 第二天早上她只能模糊地记起那个梦。

indistinguishable.t: adj. 难以分辨的；无差别的

e.en: The twins are virtually {indistinguishable} from one another.
e.zh: 那对双胞胎几乎完全分不出来。

e.en: AI-generated images are becoming {indistinguishable} from real photos.
e.zh: AI生成的图像越来越难与真实照片区分。

e.en: The two wines blended {indistinguishably} on the palate.
e.zh: 两种葡萄酒在口感上融合得难以分辨。

e.en: His handwriting and his brother's are {indistinguishably} similar.
e.zh: 他和他哥哥的笔迹相似到无法区分。

e.en: The poet would {indite} verses by candlelight each evening.
e.zh: 诗人每晚都会在烛光下创作诗篇。

e.en: She sat down to {indite} a long letter to her friend.
e.zh: 她坐下来给朋友写一封长信。

indium.t: n. 铟（化学元素，符号 In）

e.en: Touchscreens rely on a thin coating of {indium} tin oxide.
e.zh: 触摸屏依赖一层薄薄的氧化铟锡涂层。

e.en: {Indium} is a soft metal used in many electronic devices.
e.zh: 铟是一种柔软的金属,广泛用于电子设备中。

individual.t:
n. 个人；个体
adj. 单独的；个别的

e.en: Each {individual} on the team brings unique skills.
e.zh: 团队里的每个人都带来了独特的技能。

e.en: The teacher gives {individual} attention to every student.
e.zh: 老师对每个学生都给予单独的关注。

individualise.t: v. 使个性化（英式拼写）

e.en: Teachers try to {individualise} lessons for each student's needs.
e.zh: 老师努力根据每个学生的需要个性化教学。

e.en: You can {individualise} the app's interface with custom themes.
e.zh: 你可以用自定义主题来个性化这款应用的界面。

individualised.t: adj. 个性化的（英式拼写）

e.en: The clinic offers {individualised} treatment plans for every patient.
e.zh: 该诊所为每位病人提供个性化的治疗方案。

e.en: Her tutor created an {individualised} study schedule for the exam.
e.zh: 她的导师为考试制定了一份个性化的学习计划。

individualism.t: n. 个人主义；利己主义

e.en: American culture places strong emphasis on {individualism}.
e.zh: 美国文化非常强调个人主义。

e.en: Her bold fashion choices reflect a fierce {individualism}.
e.zh: 她大胆的穿搭体现出强烈的个人主义。

e.en: The book contrasts the {individualisms} of different Western societies.
e.zh: 这本书对比了不同西方社会中的各种个人主义形态。

e.en: Various {individualisms} shaped twentieth-century political thought.
e.zh: 各种形式的个人主义塑造了二十世纪的政治思想。

individualist.t: n. 个人主义者；独立自主者

e.en: He's a true {individualist} who refuses to follow trends.
e.zh: 他是个真正的个人主义者,不愿随波逐流。

e.en: As an {individualist}, she prefers working alone on projects.
e.zh: 作为一个个人主义者,她更喜欢独自做项目。

individualistic.t: adj. 个人主义的；追求个性的

e.en: Her style is highly {individualistic} and instantly recognizable.
e.zh: 她的风格极具个人特色,一眼就能认出。

e.en: Startup culture often rewards {individualistic} thinkers.
e.zh: 创业文化通常奖励有独立思想的人。

e.en: The teacher celebrates the {individualities} of each child in class.
e.zh: 这位老师珍视班里每个孩子的独特个性。

e.en: Their distinct {individualities} made the band's sound unique.
e.zh: 他们各自鲜明的个性造就了乐队独特的声音。

e.en: School uniforms shouldn't suppress a student's {individuality}.
e.zh: 校服不应该压抑学生的个性。

e.en: Her artwork shows remarkable {individuality} and creativity.
e.zh: 她的作品展现出非凡的个性和创造力。

individualization.t: n. 个性化；个人化定制

e.en: Modern marketing relies on the {individualization} of customer experiences.
e.zh: 现代营销依赖于客户体验的个性化。

e.en: The {individualization} of medicine has improved patient outcomes.
e.zh: 医疗的个性化改善了病人的治疗效果。

individualize.t: v. 使个性化；因人而异处理

e.en: Good teachers {individualize} their feedback for each student.
e.zh: 优秀的老师会针对每个学生给出个性化的反馈。

e.en: You can {individualize} your phone with custom wallpapers and ringtones.
e.zh: 你可以用自定义壁纸和铃声来个性化你的手机。

individualized.t: adj. 个性化的；量身定制的

e.en: The app offers an {individualized} learning plan for each student.
e.zh: 这款应用为每位学生提供个性化的学习计划。

e.en: She wanted an {individualized} approach instead of a generic template.
e.zh: 她想要个性化的方案，而不是千篇一律的模板。

e.en: Each cookie is wrapped {individually} for freshness.
e.zh: 每块饼干都单独包装以保持新鲜。

e.en: The teacher spoke to the students {individually} after class.
e.zh: 老师在课后逐一与学生谈话。

e.en: A few {individuals} donated most of the campaign funds.
e.zh: 少数几个人捐出了大部分竞选资金。

e.en: The policy affects high-income {individuals} more than companies.
e.zh: 该政策对高收入个人的影响大于对公司的影响。

individuate.t: v. 使个别化；区分个体

e.en: Twins often struggle to {individuate} themselves from each other.
e.zh: 双胞胎常常努力让自己与对方区分开来。

e.en: Branding helps small shops {individuate} their products from competitors.
e.zh: 品牌设计帮助小店让产品从同行中脱颖而出。

individuated.t: adj. 已个别化的；有独立个性的

e.en: Each character in the novel feels fully {individuated} and alive.
e.zh: 小说中每个角色都个性鲜明、栩栩如生。

e.en: By her teens she had {individuated} from her parents' beliefs.
e.zh: 到了十几岁，她已形成了与父母不同的独立信念。

e.en: Adolescence is a key stage of {individuation} from one's family.
e.zh: 青春期是脱离家庭、形成自我个体化的关键阶段。

e.en: The brand's success rests on careful product {individuation}.
e.zh: 该品牌的成功依赖于产品的精心差异化。

e.en: The constitution affirms the {indivisibility} of the republic.
e.zh: 宪法确认了共和国不可分割的整体性。

e.en: Physicists once believed in the {indivisibility} of the atom.
e.zh: 物理学家曾相信原子是不可分割的。

indivisible.t: adj. 不可分割的；除不尽的

e.en: Freedom and responsibility are {indivisible} in a healthy democracy.
e.zh: 在健康的民主中，自由与责任是不可分割的。

e.en: Seven is an {indivisible} number except by one and itself.
e.zh: 七是一个除了一和自身之外不可整除的数字。

indochina.t: n. 中南半岛；印度支那

e.en: France colonized much of {Indochina} in the nineteenth century.
e.zh: 法国在十九世纪殖民了印度支那的大部分地区。

e.en: The war in {Indochina} reshaped Southeast Asian politics for decades.
e.zh: 印度支那战争重塑了东南亚数十年的政治格局。

indochinese.t:
adj. 中南半岛的
n. 中南半岛人

e.en: The museum exhibits ancient {Indochinese} bronze drums.
e.zh: 博物馆展出古代印度支那的铜鼓。

e.en: Many {Indochinese} refugees settled in Paris after the war.
e.zh: 战后许多印度支那难民在巴黎定居。

e.en: Critics say the program tries to {indoctrinate} young viewers.
e.zh: 批评者认为该节目试图给年轻观众灌输思想。

e.en: Cults often {indoctrinate} new members through sleep deprivation.
e.zh: 邪教常通过剥夺睡眠来给新成员洗脑。

e.en: The textbook was criticized as political {indoctrination}.
e.zh: 这本教科书被批评为政治灌输。

e.en: Recruits undergo months of {indoctrination} before active duty.
e.zh: 新兵在服役前要经历数月的思想灌输。

e.en: His {indolence} cost him several promotions at work.
e.zh: 他的懒散让他错失了几次升职机会。

e.en: Hot afternoons invited a pleasant {indolence} by the pool.
e.zh: 炎热的下午让人想在泳池边惬意地懒散度日。

e.en: The poet wrote about the small daily {indolences} of summer.
e.zh: 诗人描写了夏日里那些小小的慵懒时光。

e.en: Her diary recorded the guilty {indolences} of the holiday week.
e.zh: 她的日记记下了假期里那些带着内疚的懒散瞬间。

indestructible.t: adj. 坚不可摧的；不可毁灭的

e.en: The phone case is marketed as virtually {indestructible}.
e.zh: 这款手机壳被宣传为几乎坚不可摧。

e.en: Their friendship proved {indestructible} despite the distance.
e.zh: 尽管相隔遥远，他们的友谊依然牢不可破。

e.en: Quantum physics is famous for its inherent {indeterminacy}.
e.zh: 量子物理以其固有的不确定性而闻名。

e.en: The contract's {indeterminacy} led to a lengthy court dispute.
e.zh: 合同条款的不确定性导致了漫长的法律纠纷。

e.en: The painting was from an {indeterminate} period in the 1800s.
e.zh: 这幅画来自 19 世纪某个不确定的时期。

e.en: His prison sentence was {indeterminate} pending good behavior.
e.zh: 他的刑期未定，视表现而决定。

index.t:
n. 索引；指数
v. 编入索引

e.en: Use the {index} at the back of the book to find topics.
e.zh: 使用书后的索引来查找主题。

e.en: The stock {index} closed up two percent today.
e.zh: 股票指数今日收盘上涨百分之二。

indexation.t: n. 指数化（与物价等挂钩）

e.en: Pension {indexation} protects retirees from inflation.
e.zh: 养老金指数化保护退休人员免受通货膨胀影响。

e.en: The government linked salaries to {indexation} of consumer prices.
e.zh: 政府将工资与消费者价格指数化挂钩。

indexed.t: adj. 已建立索引的；按指数调整的

e.en: Google has {indexed} billions of pages on the web.
e.zh: 谷歌已经索引了网络上数十亿个页面。

e.en: His salary is {indexed} to the cost of living.
e.zh: 他的薪水与生活成本挂钩。

indexer.t: n. 索引器；编制索引的人

e.en: The search {indexer} runs every night to update results.
e.zh: 搜索索引器每晚都会运行以更新结果。

e.en: She works as a professional book {indexer} from home.
e.zh: 她在家做一名专业的书籍索引编制员。

indexes.t:
n. 索引（index 的复数）
v. 编入索引

e.en: The database {indexes} make queries lightning fast.
e.zh: 数据库索引让查询变得飞快。

e.en: Most major stock {indexes} fell sharply after the news.
e.zh: 消息发布后，大多数主要股指大幅下跌。

e.en: Words like "this" and "now" have {indexical} meaning.
e.zh: "这个"和"现在"这类词具有指示性含义。

e.en: Photographs are often called {indexical} signs of reality.
e.zh: 照片常被称作现实的指示性符号。

e.en: Search engines spend enormous resources on {indexing} the web.
e.zh: 搜索引擎在网页索引上投入了巨大的资源。

e.en: Array {indexing} in Python starts at zero.
e.zh: Python 中的数组索引从零开始。

e.en: {India} is the most populous country in the world.
e.zh: 印度是世界上人口最多的国家。

e.en: We're flying to {India} next month for a wedding.
e.zh: 我们下个月要飞去印度参加一场婚礼。

indian.t:
n. 印度人
adj. 印度的

e.en: My favorite restaurant serves authentic {Indian} food.
e.zh: 我最喜欢的餐厅供应正宗的印度菜。

e.en: The {Indian} cricket team won the tournament again.
e.zh: 印度板球队再次赢得了锦标赛。

e.en: She grew up on a corn farm in northern {Indiana}.
e.zh: 她在印第安纳州北部的一个玉米农场长大。

e.en: {Indiana} is famous for the Indy 500 race every May.
e.zh: 印第安纳州因每年五月的印第 500 大赛而闻名。

indianapolis.t: n. 印第安纳波利斯（美国城市）

e.en: {Indianapolis} hosts one of the most famous car races in America.
e.zh: 印第安纳波利斯举办着美国最著名的汽车比赛之一。

e.en: Our flight had a layover in {Indianapolis} for two hours.
e.zh: 我们的航班在印第安纳波利斯转机停留了两小时。

e.en: Recent studies {indicate} that exercise improves memory.
e.zh: 近期研究表明，运动能改善记忆力。

e.en: Please {indicate} your preferred meeting time on the form.
e.zh: 请在表格上注明您方便的会议时间。

indicated.t: v. 表明（indicate 的过去式）

e.en: The survey {indicated} strong support for the new policy.
e.zh: 调查显示人们对新政策有强烈支持。

e.en: He {indicated} the exit with a quick nod of his head.
e.zh: 他用快速点头示意了出口的方向。

indicates.t: v. 表明（indicate 第三人称单数）

e.en: The red light {indicates} that the device is charging.
e.zh: 红灯表示设备正在充电。

e.en: Her tone {indicates} she's not happy with the decision.
e.zh: 她的语气表明她对这个决定不满意。

indicating.t: v. 表明（indicate 现在分词）

e.en: He raised his hand, {indicating} he had a question.
e.zh: 他举起手，表示他有一个问题。

e.en: Sales data is {indicating} a slowdown in the housing market.
e.zh: 销售数据显示房地产市场正在放缓。

e.en: There's no {indication} that the package has arrived yet.
e.zh: 目前没有迹象表明包裹已经送达。

e.en: His silence was a clear {indication} of disapproval.
e.zh: 他的沉默清楚地表示了不赞成。

e.en: All {indications} suggest the economy is recovering steadily.
e.zh: 所有迹象都显示经济正在稳步复苏。

e.en: Early {indications} from voters point to a tight election.
e.zh: 选民早期的迹象显示选情十分胶着。

e.en: His messy desk is {indicative} of how busy he's been.
e.zh: 他凌乱的桌子表明他最近有多忙。

e.en: The poll results are {indicative} but not conclusive.
e.zh: 民调结果具有指示意义，但并非定论。

e.en: GDP growth is one key {indicator} of economic health.
e.zh: GDP 增长是经济健康的一个关键指标。

e.en: The dashboard {indicator} warned that the engine was overheating.
e.zh: 仪表盘的指示灯警告发动机过热了。

e.en: Doctors monitor several {indicators} to assess heart health.
e.zh: 医生会监测多项指标来评估心脏健康。

e.en: Leading economic {indicators} point to slower growth ahead.
e.zh: 领先经济指标显示未来增长将放缓。

indices.t: n. 指数；索引（index 复数）

e.en: All three major stock {indices} hit record highs today.
e.zh: 今天三大股指均创下历史新高。

e.en: Loop through the array using these {indices}.
e.zh: 使用这些索引遍历数组。

e.en: The grand jury voted to {indict} the former CEO on fraud charges.
e.zh: 大陪审团投票决定以欺诈罪起诉这位前 CEO。

e.en: Critics {indict} the policy as harmful to small businesses.
e.zh: 批评者指责这项政策对小企业有害。

indictable.t: adj. 可起诉的；可控告的

e.en: Tax evasion at this scale is an {indictable} offense.
e.zh: 如此规模的逃税属于可起诉的罪行。

e.en: Prosecutors said his actions were clearly {indictable}.
e.zh: 检察官表示他的行为明显构成可起诉的罪行。

indicted.t: v. 起诉（indict 过去式/过去分词）

e.en: The senator was {indicted} on charges of bribery last week.
e.zh: 上周这位参议员被指控收受贿赂。

e.en: Several executives were {indicted} after the long investigation.
e.zh: 经过长期调查，多名高管遭到起诉。

e.en: The {indictment} accuses him of laundering millions of dollars.
e.zh: 起诉书指控他洗钱数百万美元。

e.en: The film is a sharp {indictment} of corporate greed.
e.zh: 这部电影是对企业贪婪的尖锐控诉。

e.en: Federal prosecutors filed {indictments} against five suspects.
e.zh: 联邦检察官对五名嫌疑人提起了诉讼。

e.en: The book offers harsh {indictments} of modern social media.
e.zh: 这本书对现代社交媒体提出了尖锐的批判。

indie.t:
adj. 独立的（音乐、电影等）
n. 独立厂牌

e.en: She loves listening to {indie} rock bands from Brooklyn.
e.zh: 她喜欢听来自布鲁克林的独立摇滚乐队。

e.en: The {indie} game won several awards at the festival.
e.zh: 这款独立游戏在节展上赢得了多个奖项。

indies.t: n. 独立厂牌；西印度群岛

e.en: Steam features many {indies} on its homepage every week.
e.zh: Steam 每周都在首页推荐许多独立游戏。

e.en: The label signed several promising {indies} this year.
e.zh: 该厂牌今年签下了几支有潜力的独立乐队。

e.en: Her cold {indifference} hurt him more than anger would have.
e.zh: 她冷漠的态度比愤怒更让他伤心。

e.en: Public {indifference} is the biggest threat to the campaign.
e.zh: 公众的冷漠是这场运动面临的最大威胁。

indifferent.t: adj. 冷漠的；不感兴趣的

e.en: Most teenagers seem {indifferent} to traditional news media.
e.zh: 大多数青少年似乎对传统新闻媒体漠不关心。

e.en: The food at that diner is honestly pretty {indifferent}.
e.zh: 那家小餐馆的食物说实话相当一般。

e.en: He shrugged {indifferently} when asked about the results.
e.zh: 被问到结果时，他漠然地耸了耸肩。

e.en: The waiter served us {indifferently} and never smiled once.
e.zh: 服务员漫不经心地招待我们，从未露出一丝笑容。

e.en: The novel portrays the {indigence} of factory workers in the 1900s.
e.zh: 小说描绘了 1900 年代工厂工人的贫困生活。

e.en: Charities try to ease the {indigence} of the city's homeless.
e.zh: 慈善机构努力缓解城市无家可归者的贫困。

e.en: The government promoted the {indigenization} of the local film industry.
e.zh: 政府推动本地电影产业的本土化。

e.en: Critics debated the {indigenization} of foreign management practices.
e.zh: 评论家们讨论了外国管理方式的本土化问题。

e.en: The forest is home to many {indigenous} plant species.
e.zh: 这片森林是许多本土植物物种的家园。

e.en: The museum showcases art by {indigenous} communities.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了原住民社区的艺术作品。

e.en: The clinic offers free care to {indigent} patients.
e.zh: 该诊所为贫困病人提供免费治疗。

e.en: She volunteers to provide legal aid for {indigent} defendants.
e.zh: 她做志愿者为贫困被告提供法律援助。

indigestible.t: adj. 难消化的；难理解的

e.en: Raw beans can be tough and {indigestible} for most people.
e.zh: 生豆子对大多数人来说很难消化。

e.en: The report was full of {indigestible} jargon and statistics.
e.zh: 那份报告满是难懂的术语和数据。

e.en: Eating too quickly often gives me {indigestion}.
e.zh: 吃得太快经常让我消化不良。

e.en: He took an antacid to relieve his {indigestion}.
e.zh: 他吃了片胃药来缓解消化不良。

e.en: She was {indignant} when accused of cheating on the exam.
e.zh: 被指控考试作弊时,她感到非常愤慨。

e.en: The customer grew {indignant} over the rude service.
e.zh: 那位顾客因服务态度恶劣而大为光火。

e.en: He {indignantly} denied stealing the documents.
e.zh: 他愤慨地否认偷了那些文件。

e.en: She slammed the door {indignantly} and walked away.
e.zh: 她愤怒地摔上门走开了。

e.en: The new policy sparked widespread public {indignation}.
e.zh: 新政策引发了广泛的公众愤慨。

e.en: Her voice trembled with {indignation} during the speech.
e.zh: 她演讲时声音因愤慨而颤抖。

e.en: Refugees often suffer countless {indignities} at border crossings.
e.zh: 难民在过境时常常遭受种种屈辱。

e.en: He endured the {indignities} of the prison without complaint.
e.zh: 他默默忍受了监狱里的种种侮辱。

e.en: Being searched in public felt like a deep {indignity}.
e.zh: 在公共场合被搜身让人感到深深的屈辱。

e.en: She refused to suffer the {indignity} of begging for help.
e.zh: 她拒绝忍受乞求帮助的屈辱。

e.en: She painted the bedroom walls a deep {indigo} blue.
e.zh: 她把卧室的墙刷成了深靛蓝色。

e.en: Farmers once grew {indigo} to make natural dye.
e.zh: 农民们曾种植靛蓝来制作天然染料。

e.en: The company faced {indirect} pressure from its investors.
e.zh: 该公司受到投资者的间接压力。

e.en: He gave an {indirect} answer to avoid the question.
e.zh: 他给出了一个间接的回答来回避问题。

e.en: The pointer adds another layer of {indirection} in the code.
e.zh: 指针在代码中增加了一层间接引用。

e.en: She used polite {indirection} to decline the invitation.
e.zh: 她用委婉的方式婉拒了邀请。

e.en: His comments {indirectly} criticized the company's leadership.
e.zh: 他的评论间接批评了公司的领导层。

e.en: The ad campaign {indirectly} boosted sales of related products.
e.zh: 这次广告活动间接带动了相关产品的销量。

e.en: China's {industrialization} lifted millions out of poverty.
e.zh: 中国的工业化使数以百万计的人摆脱了贫困。

e.en: Heavy {industrialization} reshaped the city's skyline overnight.
e.zh: 大规模工业化几乎一夜之间重塑了这座城市的天际线。

e.en: Leaders pledged to {industrialize} the southern provinces by 2030.
e.zh: 领导人承诺到2030年使南部省份实现工业化。

e.en: Small towns rarely {industrialize} without major investment.
e.zh: 没有大量投资，小城镇很难实现工业化。

industrialized.t:
adj. 已工业化的
v. industrialize 的过去式

e.en: Japan {industrialized} dramatically after the Meiji Restoration.
e.zh: 明治维新后日本迅速实现了工业化。

e.en: Most {industrialized} countries import raw materials cheaply.
e.zh: 大多数工业化国家都能廉价进口原材料。

industrializes.t: v. industrialize 的第三人称单数

e.en: As a society {industrializes}, traditional crafts often disappear.
e.zh: 社会工业化时，传统手工艺往往会消失。

e.en: The bill {industrializes} agriculture through massive subsidies.
e.zh: 这项法案通过大额补贴推动农业工业化。

industrializing.t: v. 正在工业化（industrialize 的现在分词）

e.en: Quickly {industrializing} cities suffer from severe air pollution.
e.zh: 快速工业化的城市往往饱受严重空气污染之苦。

e.en: The country is {industrializing} faster than its infrastructure allows.
e.zh: 该国工业化的速度已超出基础设施的承载力。

industrially.t: adv. 在工业方面；产业上

e.en: These chemicals are {industrially} produced in huge quantities.
e.zh: 这些化学品是工业化大批量生产的。

e.en: The bread is {industrially} baked and shipped nationwide.
e.zh: 这种面包是工业化烘烤后销往全国的。

industrie.t: n. 工业（法/德语拼写，= industry）

e.en: The French word "{industrie}" simply means industry in English.
e.zh: 法语单词"industrie"在英语中就是industry的意思。

e.en: The poster used "{industrie}" to evoke a European feel.
e.zh: 海报用"industrie"一词营造出欧洲风情。

industries.t: n. 行业；产业（industry 的复数）

e.en: Tech and finance are the city's two leading {industries}.
e.zh: 科技和金融是这座城市最重要的两大产业。

e.en: Many {industries} are racing to adopt AI tools.
e.zh: 许多行业都在争相采用人工智能工具。

e.en: She's an {industrious} student who never misses a deadline.
e.zh: 她是个勤奋的学生，从不错过任何截止日期。

e.en: {Industrious} workers built the bridge in just six months.
e.zh: 勤劳的工人们仅用六个月就建好了这座桥。

e.en: The bees worked {industriously} all through the summer.
e.zh: 蜜蜂们整个夏天都在勤奋地工作。

e.en: He typed {industriously} until well past midnight.
e.zh: 他勤奋地打字，一直敲到深夜过后。

e.en: Her {industriousness} earned her a quick promotion.
e.zh: 她的勤奋让她很快获得了晋升。

e.en: The team's {industriousness} impressed every visiting client.
e.zh: 团队的勤勉让每一位来访客户都印象深刻。

industry.t:
n. 行业；产业
n. 勤奋

e.en: The film {industry} has changed completely since streaming.
e.zh: 自从有了流媒体，电影行业彻底变了样。

e.en: Her {industry} and talent took her straight to the top.
e.zh: 她的勤奋和才华让她一路登顶。

e.en: Believers say the spirit can {indwell} the human heart.
e.zh: 信徒们认为圣灵可以居于人心之中。

e.en: Old memories {indwell} every corner of this house.
e.zh: 陈年的记忆萦绕在这屋子的每个角落。

indwelling.t: adj. 内在的；留置的（如留置导管）

e.en: The patient has an {indwelling} catheter for daily medication.
e.zh: 病人体内留置着一根导管，用于每日用药。

e.en: She spoke of an {indwelling} sense of peace and purpose.
e.zh: 她谈到内心深处那种平静与笃定的感觉。

indy.t:
adj. 独立制作的（independent 的缩写）
n. 印第赛车

e.en: He drives in the {Indy} 500 every Memorial Day weekend.
e.zh: 每年阵亡将士纪念日他都会参加印地500大赛。

e.en: The band has a refreshingly {indy} sound and DIY vibe.
e.zh: 这支乐队有一种清新的独立音乐风格和DIY气质。

e.en: He won his first {IndyCar} championship at twenty-three.
e.zh: 他在二十三岁就赢得了人生第一个印地赛车冠军。

e.en: The {IndyCar} season opens with a street race in Florida.
e.zh: 印地赛车赛季以佛罗里达的街道赛揭开序幕。

e.en: The suffix "-{ine}" often appears in chemical names like chlorine.
e.zh: 后缀"-ine"常出现在像chlorine（氯）这样的化学名称中。

e.en: Many female names end in "-{ine}", such as Christine.
e.zh: 许多女性名字以"-ine"结尾，比如Christine。

inebriate.t:
v. 使喝醉
n. 醉汉

e.en: Two glasses of wine were enough to {inebriate} him.
e.zh: 两杯葡萄酒就足以让他醉倒。

e.en: A noisy {inebriate} stumbled out of the corner pub.
e.zh: 一个喧闹的醉汉踉跄着从街角酒吧走了出来。

e.en: The {inebriated} guests were politely asked to leave.
e.zh: 那几位喝醉的客人被礼貌地请了出去。

e.en: He became loudly {inebriated} after the third round.
e.zh: 喝到第三轮后他就大声喧哗地醉了。

e.en: His {inebriation} was obvious from across the room.
e.zh: 隔着整间屋子也能看出他喝醉了。

e.en: The driver was charged with public {inebriation} last night.
e.zh: 昨晚那名司机被指控公开酗酒。

e.en: The cake was burnt and completely {inedible}.
e.zh: 蛋糕烤焦了，完全没法吃。

e.en: These mushrooms look pretty but are highly {inedible}.
e.zh: 这些蘑菇看着漂亮，却根本不能食用。

ineffable.t: adj. 无法形容的；妙不可言的

e.en: The view from the summit had an {ineffable} beauty.
e.zh: 山顶上的景色有一种难以言表的美。

e.en: She felt an {ineffable} sadness watching the old film.
e.zh: 看着那部老电影，她感到一种说不出的悲伤。

e.en: The garden in spring is {ineffably} lovely.
e.zh: 春天里的花园美得难以形容。

e.en: He smiled {ineffably}, as if hiding a private joke.
e.zh: 他笑得让人捉摸不透，像是藏着什么心事。

e.en: That night left an {ineffaceable} mark on her memory.
e.zh: 那一夜在她的记忆里留下了无法磨灭的烙印。

e.en: The scandal caused {ineffaceable} damage to his reputation.
e.zh: 那场丑闻给他的名誉造成了无法抹去的损害。

ineffective.t: adj. 无效果的；不起作用的

e.en: The new policy proved totally {ineffective} against fraud.
e.zh: 事实证明这项新政策对打击欺诈毫无效果。

e.en: Antibiotics are {ineffective} against viral infections like colds.
e.zh: 抗生素对感冒等病毒感染是无效的。

e.en: The team communicated {ineffectively} during the crisis.
e.zh: 危机期间团队的沟通毫无成效。

e.en: He argued {ineffectively} and lost the debate badly.
e.zh: 他辩得软弱无力，结果大输一场。

e.en: Critics highlighted the {ineffectiveness} of the security measures.
e.zh: 批评人士强调了那些安保措施的无效性。

e.en: Her {ineffectiveness} as a manager became impossible to ignore.
e.zh: 她作为管理者的无能已经无法被忽视。

e.en: His protests were polite but ultimately {ineffectual}.
e.zh: 他的抗议虽然礼貌，但最终毫无作用。

e.en: The mayor was widely seen as a weak, {ineffectual} leader.
e.zh: 市长被普遍认为是个软弱无能的领导者。

e.en: He waved {ineffectually} at the buzzing wasp.
e.zh: 他朝那只嗡嗡叫的黄蜂徒劳地挥着手。

e.en: The committee debated {ineffectually} for three more hours.
e.zh: 委员会又毫无结果地讨论了三个小时。

inefficacy.t: n. (尤指药物/方法) 无效

e.en: Studies revealed the {inefficacy} of the experimental drug.
e.zh: 研究揭示了那种实验性药物的无效。

e.en: The {inefficacy} of the old method forced a redesign.
e.zh: 旧方法的无效迫使团队重新设计。

e.en: Bureaucratic {inefficiency} delayed the project for months.
e.zh: 官僚作风导致项目延误了好几个月。

e.en: We're hiring consultants to identify {inefficiency} in our workflow.
e.zh: 我们正聘请顾问来找出工作流程中的低效环节。

e.en: This old engine is noisy and {inefficient}.
e.zh: 这台老引擎既吵又费油。

e.en: Reading every email twice is an {inefficient} habit.
e.zh: 每封邮件都看两遍是个低效的习惯。

e.en: The office uses energy {inefficiently} despite the new lights.
e.zh: 尽管换了新灯，办公室的用电仍然很浪费。

e.en: He works {inefficiently}, jumping between tasks all day.
e.zh: 他工作效率很低，整天在不同任务间来回切换。

inegalitarian.t: adj. 反平等主义的；不平等的

e.en: Critics call the tax code deeply {inegalitarian}.
e.zh: 批评者称这套税法极度不平等。

e.en: The country has an {inegalitarian} system favoring large landowners.
e.zh: 这个国家有一个偏袒大地主的不平等制度。

inelastic.t: adj. 无弹性的；(需求) 缺乏弹性的

e.en: Demand for insulin is highly {inelastic} regardless of price.
e.zh: 无论价格如何，对胰岛素的需求都极缺乏弹性。

e.en: The waistband is too {inelastic} to be comfortable.
e.zh: 腰带弹性太差，穿起来不舒服。

inelasticity.t: n. 无弹性；(经济) 缺乏弹性

e.en: Price {inelasticity} explains why gasoline sales barely change.
e.zh: 价格弹性低解释了汽油销量为何几乎不变。

e.en: The {inelasticity} of the rope made knot-tying difficult.
e.zh: 这根绳子缺乏弹性，打结很困难。

e.en: His {inelegant} solution worked but embarrassed the senior engineers.
e.zh: 他那个不够优雅的解决方案能用，却让资深工程师颇感尴尬。

e.en: She made an {inelegant} exit by tripping on the rug.
e.zh: 她被地毯绊倒，退场时显得十分狼狈。

e.en: The code was written {inelegantly} but shipped on time.
e.zh: 代码写得不够漂亮，但按时上线了。

e.en: He {inelegantly} stuffed the shirt into his backpack.
e.zh: 他粗鲁地把衬衫塞进了背包里。

e.en: The committee confirmed her {ineligibility} due to residency rules.
e.zh: 委员会因居住地规定确认了她不符合资格。

e.en: His {ineligibility} for the scholarship surprised everyone.
e.zh: 他无法申请该奖学金一事让大家感到意外。

e.en: Part-time staff are {ineligible} for the year-end bonus.
e.zh: 兼职员工没有资格获得年终奖金。

e.en: She was {ineligible} to vote because of her age.
e.zh: 她因年龄不够而没有投票资格。

ineluctable.t: adj. 无法逃避的；必然的

e.en: Aging is an {ineluctable} part of being human.
e.zh: 衰老是为人无法回避的一部分。

e.en: The conclusion of the report was {ineluctable} given the data.
e.zh: 考虑到数据，报告的结论无可避免。

e.en: The argument {ineluctably} leads to a single conclusion.
e.zh: 这一论证不可避免地导向唯一的结论。

e.en: Costs rose {ineluctably} as the project expanded.
e.zh: 随着项目扩张，成本也无可避免地上升。

e.en: The new manager was completely {inept} at handling conflict.
e.zh: 这位新经理在处理冲突方面完全不在行。

e.en: His {inept} attempt to apologize made things worse.
e.zh: 他笨拙的道歉反倒让事情更糟。

e.en: The investigation revealed shocking {ineptitude} in the safety team.
e.zh: 调查揭示了安全团队令人震惊的无能。

e.en: Her {ineptitude} with spreadsheets cost the company hours.
e.zh: 她不会用电子表格，让公司浪费了好几个小时。

e.en: The film {ineptly} handles its most emotional scenes.
e.zh: 这部电影在处理最动人的场景时显得很笨拙。

e.en: He {ineptly} tried to fix the leaking pipe himself.
e.zh: 他笨手笨脚地想自己修那根漏水的管道。

e.en: Her {ineptness} on social media became a running joke.
e.zh: 她在社交媒体上的笨拙成了大家长期的笑谈。

e.en: The team's {ineptness} in defense cost them the match.
e.zh: 球队防守上的笨拙让他们输掉了比赛。

inequalities.t:
n. 不平等（复数）
n. (数学) 不等式

e.en: The report highlights stark {inequalities} in healthcare access.
e.zh: 该报告强调了医疗资源获取上的巨大不平等。

e.en: Students learn to solve {inequalities} in algebra class.
e.zh: 学生们在代数课上学习如何求解不等式。

inequality.t:
n. 不平等；差距
n. (数学) 不等式

e.en: Income {inequality} has widened over the past decade.
e.zh: 过去十年里，收入不平等的差距越来越大。

e.en: Solve the {inequality} and graph the solution set.
e.zh: 解出这个不等式，并画出解集的图像。

e.en: The new tax rules are clearly {inequitable} to renters.
e.zh: 新的税收规则对租房者明显不公平。

e.en: Critics called the funding split {inequitable} and rushed.
e.zh: 批评者认为这种资金分配既不公平又太仓促。

e.en: Resources were distributed {inequitably} across the districts.
e.zh: 资源在各区之间分配得很不公平。

e.en: The bonus was shared {inequitably} among the team members.
e.zh: 奖金在团队成员之间分配得很不公平。

e.en: He spent an {indolent} Sunday reading on the couch.
e.zh: 他在沙发上读书，度过了一个懒散的周日。

e.en: Doctors describe this tumor as {indolent} and slow-growing.
e.zh: 医生形容这种肿瘤是惰性的，生长缓慢。

e.en: The cat stretched {indolently} in the afternoon sun.
e.zh: 那只猫在午后的阳光里懒洋洋地伸了个懒腰。

e.en: He waved {indolently} from the hammock without getting up.
e.zh: 他懒散地从吊床上挥了挥手，没有起身。

indomethacin.t: n. 吲哚美辛（一种消炎止痛药）

e.en: The doctor prescribed {indomethacin} for his gout flare-up.
e.zh: 医生为他的痛风发作开了吲哚美辛。

e.en: {Indomethacin} can irritate the stomach if taken without food.
e.zh: 吲哚美辛若空腹服用可能刺激胃部。

indomitable.t: adj. 不屈不挠的；无法征服的

e.en: Her {indomitable} spirit carried the team through the playoffs.
e.zh: 她不屈的精神带领球队闯过了季后赛。

e.en: The climber showed an {indomitable} will to reach the summit.
e.zh: 那位登山者展现出登顶的不屈意志。

e.en: {Indonesia} is the world's largest archipelago, with thousands of islands.
e.zh: 印度尼西亚是世界上最大的群岛国家，拥有数千座岛屿。

e.en: We flew to {Indonesia} for a diving trip in Bali.
e.zh: 我们飞往印度尼西亚，去巴厘岛潜水度假。

indonesian.t:
adj. 印度尼西亚的
n. 印尼人；印尼语

e.en: She is learning {Indonesian} to prepare for her move to Jakarta.
e.zh: 她正在学印尼语，为搬去雅加达做准备。

e.en: The restaurant serves authentic {Indonesian} satay and rendang.
e.zh: 这家餐厅供应正宗的印尼沙嗲和仁当牛肉。

e.en: The hotel has an {indoor} pool open year-round.
e.zh: 这家酒店有一个全年开放的室内泳池。

e.en: Cats living {indoor} lives tend to be safer and healthier.
e.zh: 室内饲养的猫往往更安全也更健康。

e.en: It started raining, so we moved the party {indoors}.
e.zh: 开始下雨了，所以我们把派对移到了室内。

e.en: Kids today spend too much time {indoors} on their phones.
e.zh: 如今的孩子在室内玩手机的时间太多了。

indrawn.t: adj. 吸入的；（性格）内向的

e.en: She gave a sharp, {indrawn} breath at the bad news.
e.zh: 听到坏消息，她猛地倒吸了一口气。

e.en: His {indrawn} cheeks made him look gaunt and tired.
e.zh: 他凹陷的双颊让他显得憔悴疲惫。

indubitable.t: adj. 毋庸置疑的；确凿的

e.en: Her talent for piano is {indubitable}, even at age six.
e.zh: 即便才六岁，她的钢琴天赋也是毋庸置疑的。

e.en: The DNA evidence offered {indubitable} proof of his innocence.
e.zh: DNA证据为他的清白提供了无可置疑的证明。

e.en: This is {indubitably} the best ramen in the city.
e.zh: 这毫无疑问是全城最好吃的拉面。

e.en: He is {indubitably} the most experienced engineer on the team.
e.zh: 他无疑是团队里最有经验的工程师。

e.en: Bright screens at night can {induce} insomnia.
e.zh: 夜里看亮屏幕可能会引发失眠。

e.en: Doctors decided to {induce} labor a week early.
e.zh: 医生决定提前一周诱导分娩。

induced.t:
adj. 诱发的
v. 诱导（过去式）

e.en: The medication {induced} drowsiness within twenty minutes.
e.zh: 这种药在二十分钟内就让人犯困。

e.en: Stress {induced} her migraines during the busy season.
e.zh: 忙碌季节里压力诱发了她的偏头痛。

e.en: A signing bonus is a common {inducement} for new hires.
e.zh: 签字奖金是吸引新员工常见的激励手段。

e.en: Free shipping is a strong {inducement} to complete the purchase.
e.zh: 免运费是促成下单的强力诱因。

e.en: The company offered cash {inducements} to early retirees.
e.zh: 公司向提前退休者提供了现金奖励。

e.en: Tax breaks are typical {inducements} for foreign investment.
e.zh: 税收优惠是吸引外资的常见激励措施。

e.en: Caffeine acts as a mild {inducer} of alertness.
e.zh: 咖啡因可作为温和的提神诱导剂。

e.en: Certain drugs are an {inducer} of liver enzymes.
e.zh: 某些药物是肝酶的诱导剂。

induces.t: v. 诱导；引起（第三人称单数）

e.en: Lavender tea {induces} a calm, sleepy feeling.
e.zh: 薰衣草茶能让人产生平静困倦的感觉。

e.en: This perfume {induces} a sneezing fit every time.
e.zh: 这款香水每次都会让我打喷嚏不止。

e.en: The gene is {inducible} only when sugar levels drop.
e.zh: 该基因仅在糖水平下降时才会被诱导表达。

e.en: Researchers prefer {inducible} systems for precise experimental control.
e.zh: 研究人员更喜欢可诱导系统，以便精准控制实验。

inducing.t: v. 诱导；引起（现在分词）

e.en: The doctor avoided {inducing} labor unless absolutely necessary.
e.zh: 除非必要，医生不会贸然诱导分娩。

e.en: The film has a strangely sleep-{inducing} pace.
e.zh: 这部电影的节奏出奇地催人入睡。

induct.t: v. 使正式就职；引入；征召入伍

e.en: They will {induct} her into the Hall of Fame next year.
e.zh: 明年他们将把她列入名人堂。

e.en: The army plans to {induct} new recruits next Monday.
e.zh: 军队计划在下周一让新兵入伍。

e.en: The coil's {inductance} determines how the circuit filters signals.
e.zh: 线圈的电感决定了电路如何过滤信号。

e.en: Engineers measured the {inductance} with a precision LCR meter.
e.zh: 工程师用精密LCR仪表测量了电感。

inducted.t: v. 使就职（过去式）；已征召入伍

e.en: She was {inducted} into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
e.zh: 她被正式列入摇滚名人堂。

e.en: All freshmen were {inducted} into the honor society last week.
e.zh: 所有新生上周都被吸纳进了荣誉学会。

inductee.t: n. 新入职者；应征入伍者

e.en: Each {inductee} gave a short speech at the ceremony.
e.zh: 每位入会者都在仪式上发表了简短致辞。

e.en: The youngest {inductee} this year is just nineteen.
e.zh: 今年最年轻的入选者只有十九岁。

e.en: The committee is {inducting} five new members tonight.
e.zh: 委员会今晚将吸纳五位新成员。

e.en: They are {inducting} her for her contributions to medicine.
e.zh: 他们因她对医学的贡献而授予她正式会员身份。

induction.t: n. 归纳（推理）；就职；电磁感应

e.en: New hires must complete a two-day {induction} program.
e.zh: 新员工必须完成为期两天的入职培训。

e.en: The {induction} cooktop heats pots without warming the surface.
e.zh: 电磁炉能加热锅具而不加热炉面。

inductions.t: n. 归纳；就职仪式（复数）

e.en: The Hall of Fame holds its {inductions} every August.
e.zh: 名人堂每年八月举行入选仪式。

e.en: Hospitals saw fewer labor {inductions} during the pandemic.
e.zh: 疫情期间医院的引产手术数量有所减少。

e.en: Scientists rely on {inductive} reasoning to form new hypotheses.
e.zh: 科学家依靠归纳推理来形成新的假设。

e.en: The phone supports {inductive} charging on any Qi pad.
e.zh: 这款手机支持在任何Qi充电板上进行无线感应充电。

e.en: He argued {inductively} from a handful of case studies.
e.zh: 他根据少量案例进行了归纳式论证。

e.en: The wireless earbuds charge {inductively} inside their case.
e.zh: 这款无线耳机在收纳盒内通过感应充电。

e.en: The {inductivist} approach builds theories from observed patterns.
e.zh: 归纳主义方法是从观察到的规律中构建理论。

e.en: Popper rejected the {inductivist} view of how science progresses.
e.zh: 波普尔反对关于科学进步的归纳主义观点。

e.en: The circuit needs a small {inductor} to filter the noise.
e.zh: 这个电路需要一个小电感来过滤噪声。

e.en: He soldered the {inductor} carefully onto the circuit board.
e.zh: 他小心地把电感焊到了电路板上。

inducts.t: v. 使就职（第三人称单数）

e.en: The league {inducts} three legendary players every spring.
e.zh: 该联盟每年春天会让三位传奇球员入选名人堂。

e.en: The school formally {inducts} its prefects in a Friday assembly.
e.zh: 学校在周五的集会上正式任命级长。

e.en: On weekends I {indulge} in a slice of chocolate cake.
e.zh: 周末我会放纵自己吃一块巧克力蛋糕。

e.en: Parents shouldn't {indulge} every tantrum their child throws.
e.zh: 父母不应纵容孩子每次发脾气。

e.en: She {indulged} herself with a long bubble bath.
e.zh: 她任由自己泡了个长长的泡泡浴。

e.en: The grandparents always {indulged} the kids with extra dessert.
e.zh: 祖父母总是纵容孩子们多吃甜点。

e.en: A spa weekend is my favorite kind of {indulgence}.
e.zh: 周末水疗是我最喜欢的一种放纵享受。

e.en: The teacher asked for the audience's {indulgence} during the delay.
e.zh: 老师在延误期间请观众多多包涵。

e.en: Designer handbags are her main {indulgences}.
e.zh: 设计师手袋是她最大的奢侈嗜好。

e.en: He cut back on small daily {indulgences} to save money.
e.zh: 他减少了日常的小享受以省钱。

e.en: My grandmother was always {indulgent} with weekend sweets.
e.zh: 我奶奶在周末吃糖这事上总是很纵容。

e.en: The chocolate dessert was rich and almost too {indulgent}.
e.zh: 那道巧克力甜点浓郁得几乎让人罪恶。

e.en: She smiled {indulgently} as her toddler made a mess.
e.zh: 看着小孩弄得一团糟，她宠溺地笑了。

e.en: The teacher nodded {indulgently} at the silly question.
e.zh: 老师对那个傻问题宽容地点了点头。

indulges.t: v. 放纵；沉溺（第三人称单数）

e.en: He {indulges} in chocolate every Friday night.
e.zh: 他每周五晚上都会放纵地吃巧克力。

e.en: She rarely {indulges} her kids with expensive toys.
e.zh: 她很少用昂贵的玩具来娇惯孩子。

indulging.t: v. 放纵；沉溺（现在分词）

e.en: I'm {indulging} in a long bath after work.
e.zh: 下班后我正享受一个长长的泡澡。

e.en: Stop {indulging} him; he needs to learn responsibility.
e.zh: 别再纵容他了，他需要学会承担责任。

indurate.t:
v. 使变硬；使麻木
adj. 坚硬的

e.en: Years of hardship had {indurate} his heart against pity.
e.zh: 多年的苦难使他的心变得冷硬，毫无怜悯。

e.en: The clay will {indurate} when fired in the kiln.
e.zh: 这种黏土在窑里烧制后会变硬。

e.en: The doctor noticed an {induration} on the patient's arm.
e.zh: 医生发现病人手臂上有一处硬结。

e.en: Soil {induration} makes farming nearly impossible here.
e.zh: 土壤板结使这里几乎无法耕作。

e.en: The {Indus} river flows through Pakistan and northwest India.
e.zh: 印度河流经巴基斯坦和印度西北部。

e.en: Ancient cities thrived along the {Indus} thousands of years ago.
e.zh: 几千年前印度河沿岸就有繁荣的古城。

e.en: The {industrial} park houses dozens of small factories.
e.zh: 这个工业园区聚集了几十家小工厂。

e.en: She loves the {industrial} look of exposed brick walls.
e.zh: 她喜欢裸露砖墙那种工业风的感觉。

e.en: Rapid {industrialisation} transformed the country in two decades.
e.zh: 快速的工业化在二十年里改变了这个国家。

e.en: {Industrialisation} brought pollution along with economic growth.
e.zh: 工业化带来经济增长的同时也带来了污染。

industrialise.t: v. 使工业化（英式拼写）

e.en: The government plans to {industrialise} rural regions next.
e.zh: 政府计划下一步对农村地区推行工业化。

e.en: It took Britain a century to fully {industrialise}.
e.zh: 英国花了一个世纪才完全实现工业化。

industrialised.t:
adj. 已工业化的
v. 工业化（过去式）

e.en: Most {industrialised} nations face aging population issues.
e.zh: 大多数工业化国家都面临人口老龄化问题。

e.en: The region {industrialised} faster than anyone predicted.
e.zh: 这个地区工业化的速度超出了所有人的预期。

industrialises.t: v. 使工业化（第三人称单数）

e.en: As a country {industrialises}, its energy demand soars.
e.zh: 一个国家工业化时，能源需求会急剧上升。

e.en: The plan {industrialises} farming through automation.
e.zh: 该计划通过自动化使农业实现工业化。

industrialising.t: v. 使工业化（现在分词）

e.en: Vietnam is rapidly {industrialising} its coastal provinces.
e.zh: 越南正在快速推进沿海省份的工业化。

e.en: {Industrialising} economies often struggle with worker safety.
e.zh: 工业化中的经济体往往在劳工安全问题上举步维艰。

industrialism.t: n. 工业主义；产业主义

e.en: Critics argued {industrialism} alienated workers from their craft.
e.zh: 批评者认为工业主义让工人与自己的手艺脱节。

e.en: The novel attacks the dehumanizing effects of {industrialism}.
e.zh: 这部小说抨击了工业主义对人性的扭曲。

e.en: The wealthy {industrialist} donated millions to local hospitals.
e.zh: 那位富有的实业家向当地医院捐了数百万。

e.en: She married a German {industrialist} in the 1920s.
e.zh: 她在二十年代嫁给了一位德国实业家。

e.en: The lawsuit aims to address pay {inequity} at the firm.
e.zh: 这起诉讼旨在解决公司内部的薪酬不公问题。

e.en: She spoke openly about the {inequity} she faced at work.
e.zh: 她坦率地谈到了自己在工作中遭遇的不公。

ineradicable.t: adj. 无法根除的；根深蒂固的

e.en: The stain on his reputation seemed {ineradicable}.
e.zh: 他名誉上的污点看起来无法洗清。

e.en: Childhood memories left an {ineradicable} mark on her writing.
e.zh: 童年记忆在她的写作中留下了无法抹去的印记。

e.en: The pastor preached the {inerrancy} of scripture.
e.zh: 那位牧师宣讲圣经无误的教义。

e.en: Few scholars now defend the absolute {inerrancy} of these texts.
e.zh: 如今很少有学者还坚持这些文本绝对无误。

inert.t: adj. 惰性的；迟钝的；无活力的

e.en: Helium is an {inert} gas often used in balloons.
e.zh: 氦气是一种惰性气体，常用于充气球。

e.en: He lay {inert} on the couch all afternoon.
e.zh: 他整个下午都一动不动地躺在沙发上。

e.en: Bureaucratic {inertia} slowed the reform to a crawl.
e.zh: 官僚机构的惰性把改革拖得举步维艰。

e.en: Newton's first law describes the {inertia} of moving objects.
e.zh: 牛顿第一定律描述的是运动物体的惯性。

e.en: The phone uses an {inertial} sensor to detect motion.
e.zh: 这款手机用惯性传感器来检测运动。

e.en: Spacecraft rely on {inertial} navigation when GPS is unavailable.
e.zh: 在没有 GPS 时，航天器依赖惯性导航。

inescapable.t: adj. 不可避免的；无法逃脱的

e.en: The conclusion is {inescapable}: we have to refactor the code.
e.zh: 结论无可回避：我们必须重构这段代码。

e.en: Climate change has become an {inescapable} topic in the news.
e.zh: 气候变化已经成为新闻中无法回避的话题。

inescapably.t: adv. 不可避免地；无法逃脱地

e.en: The two issues are {inescapably} linked to each other.
e.zh: 这两个问题彼此之间无法分开。

e.en: Her work is {inescapably} shaped by her upbringing.
e.zh: 她的作品不可避免地受到她成长经历的影响。

inessential.t:
adj. 非必要的
n. 非必需品

e.en: Strip out all the {inessential} features before launch.
e.zh: 在上线之前去掉所有不必要的功能。

e.en: He treats sleep as if it were {inessential}.
e.zh: 他似乎把睡觉当成可有可无的事。

inestimable.t: adj. 难以估量的；无价的

e.en: Her mentor's advice has been of {inestimable} value.
e.zh: 导师的建议对她而言价值无可估量。

e.en: The library holds books of {inestimable} historical importance.
e.zh: 这座图书馆收藏着具有无可估量历史价值的书籍。

e.en: He gradually accepted the {inevitability} of the layoffs.
e.zh: 他渐渐接受了裁员无法避免的事实。

e.en: There is a sense of {inevitability} about the merger.
e.zh: 这桩合并案给人一种势在必行的感觉。

inevitable.t: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的

e.en: A confrontation with management seems {inevitable} now.
e.zh: 现在和管理层的正面冲突看来已不可避免。

e.en: Some delays are {inevitable} when launching a new product.
e.zh: 发布新产品时出现一些延误是难免的。

inevitably.t: adv. 不可避免地；必然地

e.en: Big rewrites {inevitably} introduce new bugs.
e.zh: 大规模重写不可避免地会引入新的 bug。

e.en: Conversations about politics {inevitably} get heated.
e.zh: 关于政治的讨论难免会变得激烈。

inexact.t: adj. 不精确的；不准确的

e.en: The translation is {inexact} but captures the general meaning.
e.zh: 这个翻译并不精确，但抓住了大致意思。

e.en: Weather forecasting remains an {inexact} science.
e.zh: 天气预报至今仍是一门并不精确的科学。

inexcusable.t: adj. 不可原谅的；无法辩解的

e.en: Showing up two hours late is simply {inexcusable}.
e.zh: 迟到两个小时实在让人无法原谅。

e.en: The data leak was an {inexcusable} security failure.
e.zh: 这次数据泄露是不可原谅的安全失误。

e.en: The customer service was {inexcusably} rude on the phone.
e.zh: 客服在电话里粗鲁得让人无法接受。

e.en: He was {inexcusably} late to his own wedding.
e.zh: 他在自己的婚礼上迟到了，简直无法原谅。

inexhaustible.t: adj. 用之不尽的；不知疲倦的

e.en: Toddlers seem to have an {inexhaustible} supply of energy.
e.zh: 幼儿似乎拥有用之不竭的精力。

e.en: The internet is an {inexhaustible} source of cat videos.
e.zh: 互联网是源源不绝的猫咪视频宝库。

inexorabilities.t: n. 无情；不可阻挡（inexorability 的复数）

e.en: The novel explores the {inexorabilities} of fate and time.
e.zh: 这部小说探讨命运与时间那种无可阻挡的力量。

e.en: She wrote about the {inexorabilities} of grief and loss.
e.zh: 她写下了悲伤与失去那种无可逃避的力量。

e.en: The {inexorability} of climate change frightens many scientists.
e.zh: 气候变化的不可阻挡性让许多科学家感到恐惧。

e.en: He marveled at the {inexorability} of the tide rising.
e.zh: 他惊叹于潮水涨起时那种无可阻挡的气势。

inexorable.t: adj. 不可阻挡的；无情的

e.en: The {inexorable} rise of streaming has reshaped television.
e.zh: 流媒体不可阻挡的崛起重塑了电视行业。

e.en: There was an {inexorable} logic to her argument.
e.zh: 她的论证有一种无可辩驳的逻辑。

inexorably.t: adv. 不可阻挡地；无情地

e.en: Housing prices have risen {inexorably} for a decade.
e.zh: 房价在过去十年里持续不断地上涨。

e.en: The story moves {inexorably} toward a tragic ending.
e.zh: 故事不可阻挡地走向了悲剧的结局。

inexpedient.t: adj. 不合时宜的；不妥的

e.en: Raising taxes now would be politically {inexpedient}.
e.zh: 此时加税在政治上并不明智。

e.en: The CEO called the merger {inexpedient} given market conditions.
e.zh: 鉴于市场状况，CEO 认为这次合并并不合时宜。

e.en: This laptop is surprisingly {inexpensive} for its specs.
e.zh: 这款笔记本以它的配置来说便宜得出奇。

e.en: They serve {inexpensive} but delicious noodles near the office.
e.zh: 办公室附近有家店卖便宜又好吃的面条。

inexpensively.t: adv. 便宜地；花费不多地

e.en: You can travel through Southeast Asia quite {inexpensively}.
e.zh: 在东南亚旅行其实可以非常省钱。

e.en: The startup operates {inexpensively} from a small co-working space.
e.zh: 这家初创公司在一个小型共享办公空间里低成本运营。

e.en: Her {inexperience} showed during the first client meeting.
e.zh: 她在第一次客户会议上暴露了自己的经验不足。

e.en: The team's {inexperience} actually led to fresh ideas.
e.zh: 团队缺乏经验反倒带来了新颖的想法。

inexperienced.t: adj. 没经验的；不熟练的

e.en: Even {inexperienced} developers can contribute to open source.
e.zh: 即使是没有经验的开发者也能为开源项目做贡献。

e.en: The hike is too tough for {inexperienced} climbers.
e.zh: 对于没经验的登山者来说，这条徒步路线太难了。

e.en: His {inexpert} editing left the video full of jump cuts.
e.zh: 他外行的剪辑让视频里到处都是跳切。

e.en: The repair was {inexpert} but at least the door closed.
e.zh: 修得不太专业，但至少门能关上了。

e.en: He {inexpertly} chopped the onions, making everyone laugh.
e.zh: 他切洋葱的样子很外行，把大家都逗笑了。

e.en: The article was {inexpertly} translated and full of errors.
e.zh: 这篇文章翻译得很不专业，错漏百出。

inexpiable.t: adj. 不可饶恕的；无法弥补的

e.en: In her eyes, his betrayal was an {inexpiable} sin.
e.zh: 在她看来，他的背叛是无法弥补的罪过。

e.en: The general carried the {inexpiable} guilt of that order.
e.zh: 将军背负着那道命令带来的无法赎清的罪疚。

inexplicable.t: adj. 无法解释的；费解的

e.en: For some {inexplicable} reason, the app crashes only on Tuesdays.
e.zh: 出于某种莫名其妙的原因，这款应用只在周二崩溃。

e.en: Her sudden resignation remains {inexplicable} to her colleagues.
e.zh: 她突然辞职的原因让同事们至今都想不明白。

inexplicably.t: adv. 无法解释地；莫名其妙地

e.en: The server {inexplicably} reboots every Sunday at 3 a.m.
e.zh: 服务器每周日凌晨三点都会莫名其妙地重启。

e.en: He {inexplicably} stopped replying to her texts.
e.zh: 他莫名其妙地不再回她的短信了。

inexpressible.t: adj. 难以表达的；无法形容的

e.en: She felt an {inexpressible} relief when the test results came back.
e.zh: 当检查结果出来时，她感到一种难以言喻的轻松。

e.en: There is an {inexpressible} joy in seeing your child smile.
e.zh: 看到自己的孩子微笑，那种喜悦无法用言语形容。

e.en: The view from the summit was {inexpressibly} beautiful.
e.zh: 山顶上的景色美得难以形容。

e.en: Losing the dog was {inexpressibly} sad for the whole family.
e.zh: 失去那只狗让全家人难过得无法形容。

inexpressive.t: adj. 缺乏表情的；呆板的

e.en: His face stayed {inexpressive} throughout the verdict.
e.zh: 在宣读判决的整个过程中，他的脸上毫无表情。

e.en: The robot's {inexpressive} eyes made it feel uncanny.
e.zh: 机器人那双毫无表情的眼睛让人觉得很诡异。

inextinguishable.t: adj. 扑不灭的；无法抑制的

e.en: She has an {inextinguishable} curiosity about how things work.
e.zh: 她对事物的运作方式有一种永不熄灭的好奇心。

e.en: The candle was advertised as nearly {inextinguishable} in the wind.
e.zh: 这种蜡烛号称在风中几乎吹不灭。

inextricable.t: adj. 密不可分的；无法摆脱的

e.en: There is an {inextricable} link between sleep and mental health.
e.zh: 睡眠与心理健康之间有着无法分割的联系。

e.en: The two stories are {inextricable} from one another.
e.zh: 这两个故事彼此交织，无法分开。

inextricably.t: adv. 密不可分地；无法分开地

e.en: Their careers are {inextricably} linked through years of collaboration.
e.zh: 他们的事业因多年合作而密不可分。

e.en: Privacy and security are {inextricably} tied in modern apps.
e.zh: 在现代应用中，隐私与安全密不可分。

inf.t: n. 无穷大（infinity 的缩写）；信息（info 的缩写）

e.en: The function returned {inf} when we divided by zero.
e.zh: 当我们除以零时，函数返回了无穷大。

e.en: Set the timeout to {inf} to disable it entirely.
e.zh: 将超时设为无穷大即可完全禁用它。

infallibilities.t: n. 绝对可靠；永无错误（infallibility 的复数）

e.en: The book mocks the supposed {infallibilities} of various ancient oracles.
e.zh: 这本书嘲讽了各种古代神谕所谓的绝对正确性。

e.en: Critics question the {infallibilities} claimed by competing religious traditions.
e.zh: 评论家质疑各宗教传统所宣称的绝对无误性。

infallibility.t: n. 绝对可靠；永无错误

e.en: No engineer believes in the {infallibility} of automated tests.
e.zh: 没有工程师会相信自动化测试是绝对无误的。

e.en: The doctrine asserts the pope's {infallibility} on matters of faith.
e.zh: 该教义主张教宗在信仰问题上绝对无误。

infallible.t: adj. 绝对可靠的；不会出错的

e.en: Even the best spam filter is not {infallible}.
e.zh: 即便是最好的垃圾邮件过滤器也并非万无一失。

e.en: She has an almost {infallible} memory for names.
e.zh: 她对名字的记忆几乎从不出错。

infallibly.t: adv. 绝对可靠地；必定地

e.en: The dog {infallibly} senses when a storm is coming.
e.zh: 那只狗总能准确无误地察觉暴风雨即将来临。

e.en: His advice {infallibly} pointed us toward the cheapest option.
e.zh: 他的建议总能准确无误地指向最便宜的选项。

infamous.t: adj. 臭名昭著的；声名狼藉的

e.en: The startup became {infamous} for its toxic work culture.
e.zh: 这家初创公司因恶劣的工作文化而声名狼藉。

e.en: That bug is {infamous} among backend engineers everywhere.
e.zh: 那个 bug 在各地后端工程师中臭名昭著。

e.en: The CEO {infamously} fired half the staff over email.
e.zh: 那位 CEO 因通过邮件解雇半数员工而臭名昭著。

e.en: Cryptocurrency markets are {infamously} volatile and hard to predict.
e.zh: 加密货币市场因波动剧烈、难以预测而臭名远扬。

e.en: The scandal earned the company lasting {infamy} online.
e.zh: 这场丑闻让公司在网上留下了长久的恶名。

e.en: Pearl Harbor lives in {infamy} as a day of attack.
e.zh: 珍珠港作为受袭之日永远留在耻辱史中。

e.en: Quantum computing is still in its {infancy} commercially.
e.zh: 量子计算在商业上仍处于初期阶段。

e.en: She spent her {infancy} in a small village abroad.
e.zh: 她的婴儿时期是在国外一个小村庄度过的。

infant.t:
n. 婴儿；幼儿
adj. 婴儿的；初期的

e.en: The new car seat is rated for any {infant} under 20 pounds.
e.zh: 这款新儿童座椅适用于二十磅以下的婴儿。

e.en: This feature is still in its {infant} stage of development.
e.zh: 该功能仍处于开发的初期阶段。

e.en: The painting depicts the Spanish {infanta} in royal attire.
e.zh: 这幅画描绘了身着皇家盛装的西班牙公主。

e.en: The {infanta} was betrothed to a foreign prince at twelve.
e.zh: 那位公主十二岁时便已与一位外国王子订婚。

e.en: Historians documented {infanticide} as a tragic outcome of extreme poverty.
e.zh: 历史学家记录了杀婴行为作为极端贫困的悲惨后果。

e.en: The law treats {infanticide} as a distinct serious crime.
e.zh: 法律将杀婴行为视为一项独立的重罪。

e.en: His {infantile} response to criticism embarrassed the whole team.
e.zh: 他对批评的幼稚反应让整个团队难堪。

e.en: The clinic specializes in treating {infantile} respiratory conditions.
e.zh: 该诊所专门治疗婴幼儿呼吸系统疾病。

e.en: The {infantry} advanced slowly through the muddy fields.
e.zh: 步兵部队缓慢地穿过泥泞的田野推进。

e.en: He served two years in the {infantry} before college.
e.zh: 他在上大学前在步兵部队服役了两年。

e.en: Every {infantryman} carried over forty pounds of gear.
e.zh: 每名步兵都背着超过四十磅的装备。

e.en: The veteran spoke proudly about his years as an {infantryman}.
e.zh: 那位老兵自豪地谈起他当步兵的岁月。

e.en: Pediatricians recommend back-sleeping for healthy {infants} under one year.
e.zh: 儿科医生建议一岁以下健康婴儿仰卧睡觉。

e.en: The app blocks loud notifications when {infants} are nearby.
e.zh: 当婴儿在附近时，该应用会屏蔽响亮的通知。

e.en: The MRI scan revealed a small {infarct} in his brain.
e.zh: 核磁共振扫描显示他脑部有一个小的梗死灶。

e.en: Doctors monitored the {infarct} closely after his stroke.
e.zh: 医生在他中风后密切监测梗死区域。

e.en: He survived a myocardial {infarction} thanks to quick treatment.
e.zh: 由于救治及时，他从心肌梗塞中幸存下来。

e.en: Smoking dramatically increases the risk of {infarction}.
e.zh: 吸烟会显著增加梗塞的风险。

infatuate.t: v. 使迷恋；使冲昏头脑

e.en: Sleek demos can {infatuate} investors before due diligence begins.
e.zh: 精致的演示在尽职调查前就能让投资者着迷。

e.en: Pop stars often {infatuate} young fans with their charm.
e.zh: 流行明星常以魅力让年轻粉丝痴迷不已。

infatuated.t: adj. 热恋的；盲目迷恋的

e.en: He was completely {infatuated} with his new coworker.
e.zh: 他对新同事完全是一见倾心。

e.en: Tech bros got {infatuated} with the AI hype overnight.
e.zh: 科技圈一夜之间就对 AI 热潮痴迷起来。

e.en: My {infatuation} with that startup faded after the layoffs.
e.zh: 裁员之后我对那家初创公司的迷恋就消退了。

e.en: Teenage {infatuation} rarely survives the first real argument.
e.zh: 青春期的痴情很少能挺过第一次真正的争吵。

infeasible.t: adj. 不可行的；行不通的

e.en: Shipping the feature this quarter is simply {infeasible}.
e.zh: 本季度上线该功能根本不可行。

e.en: The proposed budget made the project {infeasible} from the start.
e.zh: 提出的预算从一开始就让该项目无法实现。

e.en: One careless click can {infect} the entire company network.
e.zh: 一次粗心的点击就可能感染整个公司网络。

e.en: Her enthusiasm seemed to {infect} everyone in the room.
e.zh: 她的热情似乎感染了房间里的每一个人。

infected.t:
adj. 被感染的
v. 感染（过去式）

e.en: The laptop got {infected} after he opened a sketchy attachment.
e.zh: 他打开了一个可疑附件后，笔记本就被感染了。

e.en: Doctors quarantined every patient {infected} during the outbreak.
e.zh: 医生隔离了疫情期间每一位被感染的病人。

e.en: The malware kept {infecting} new machines through a shared drive.
e.zh: 恶意软件持续通过共享盘感染新机器。

e.en: His pessimism was {infecting} the rest of the team.
e.zh: 他的悲观情绪正在感染团队其他成员。

e.en: She stayed home to avoid spreading the {infection} at work.
e.zh: 她留在家中，以免把感染传到公司。

e.en: Antivirus software detected an {infection} in the download folder.
e.zh: 杀毒软件在下载文件夹中检测到了一处感染。

e.en: Hand washing prevents most common {infections} during flu season.
e.zh: 勤洗手可以预防流感季大多数常见感染。

e.en: The hospital reported a sharp drop in postoperative {infections}.
e.zh: 医院报告称术后感染人数大幅下降。

infectious.t: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的

e.en: Her laughter is so {infectious} the whole office joins in.
e.zh: 她的笑声极具感染力，整个办公室都跟着笑。

e.en: Measles is highly {infectious} and spreads through the air.
e.zh: 麻疹传染性极强，会通过空气传播。

infectiously.t: adv. 具传染性地；富感染力地

e.en: The toddler giggled {infectiously} at every silly face.
e.zh: 那个小孩看到每个鬼脸都咯咯笑得让人忍不住跟着笑。

e.en: He spoke {infectiously} about his passion for open source.
e.zh: 他谈起对开源的热情时，感染力十足。

e.en: Researchers measured how {infective} the new variant really was.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了新变种实际的传染力有多强。

e.en: The {infective} dose for this virus is surprisingly small.
e.zh: 这种病毒的感染剂量小得惊人。

infects.t: v. 感染（第三人称单数）

e.en: This worm {infects} any USB drive plugged into the host.
e.zh: 这种蠕虫会感染插入主机的任何 U 盘。

e.en: His cynicism slowly {infects} every new hire on the team.
e.zh: 他的愤世嫉俗渐渐影响着团队里每个新人。

infelicitous.t: adj. 不恰当的；不得体的

e.en: His {infelicitous} joke at the funeral made everyone uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他在葬礼上不合时宜的玩笑让所有人都很尴尬。

e.en: The translation contained several {infelicitous} word choices.
e.zh: 译文中有几处用词不太得当。

e.en: The essay had only one minor {infelicity} in its phrasing.
e.zh: 这篇文章措辞上仅有一处小小的不妥。

e.en: Editors flagged the {infelicity} of using slang in formal reports.
e.zh: 编辑指出在正式报告中使用俚语并不恰当。

e.en: From the silence, I could only {infer} that something went wrong.
e.zh: 从这片沉默中，我只能推断出一定出了什么差错。

e.en: The model tries to {infer} user intent from short queries.
e.zh: 模型会尝试从简短的查询中推断用户意图。

e.en: Running model {inference} on the GPU was ten times faster.
e.zh: 在 GPU 上运行模型推理速度快了十倍。

e.en: Her {inference} from the data turned out to be correct.
e.zh: 她从数据中得出的推论后来证明是正确的。

e.en: The detective drew careful {inferences} from a few small clues.
e.zh: 侦探从几条小线索中作出了谨慎的推断。

e.en: Statistical {inferences} require enough samples to be reliable.
e.zh: 统计推断需要足够的样本才能可靠。

inferential.t: adj. 推理的；基于推论的

e.en: The case relied entirely on {inferential} evidence and witness memory.
e.zh: 该案件完全依赖于推断性证据和证人记忆。

e.en: Modern chips are optimized for {inferential} workloads in AI.
e.zh: 现代芯片专为人工智能中的推理类工作负载进行了优化。

e.en: We could only conclude {inferentially} that the server had crashed.
e.zh: 我们只能通过推断得出服务器已经崩溃的结论。

e.en: The article argues {inferentially} for tighter privacy regulation.
e.zh: 文章通过推论的方式主张加强隐私监管。

inferior.t:
adj. 较差的；下级的
n. 下级

e.en: The cheaper cable is clearly {inferior} in build quality.
e.zh: 那根便宜的线在做工上明显更差。

e.en: Don't let trolls make you feel {inferior} online.
e.zh: 别让网上的喷子让你觉得自己不如别人。

e.en: Constant comparisons online can fuel a sense of {inferiority}.
e.zh: 在网上不断攀比会助长一种自卑感。

e.en: He hides his {inferiority} complex behind loud opinions.
e.zh: 他用大声发表观点来掩饰自己的自卑情结。

e.en: That {infernal} printer jams every single morning at the office.
e.zh: 办公室那台讨厌的打印机每天早上都卡纸。

e.en: The poem describes an {infernal} landscape of fire and smoke.
e.zh: 这首诗描绘了一片烈火与浓烟的地狱般景象。

e.en: This new bug is {infernally} hard to reproduce locally.
e.zh: 这个新 bug 在本地极难复现，烦人得要命。

e.en: The summit was {infernally} hot even at sunrise.
e.zh: 即便是日出时分，山顶也热得令人难以忍受。

inferno.t: n. 熊熊烈火；人间地狱

e.en: Firefighters battled the {inferno} for nearly twelve hours.
e.zh: 消防员与那场大火搏斗了将近十二个小时。

e.en: The kitchen turned into a brief {inferno} after the grease fire.
e.zh: 油着火后，厨房瞬间变成了一片火海。

e.en: The compiler {inferred} the type from the assigned value.
e.zh: 编译器从赋值推断出了变量的类型。

e.en: From his tone, she {inferred} that he was upset.
e.zh: 从他的语气中，她推断出他不开心。

e.en: TypeScript is good at {inferring} return types automatically.
e.zh: TypeScript 很擅长自动推断返回类型。

e.en: He kept {inferring} motives that nobody actually had.
e.zh: 他不断揣测一些其实并不存在的动机。

infers.t: v. 推断（第三人称单数）

e.en: The algorithm {infers} your preferences from past clicks.
e.zh: 该算法会根据你过去的点击推断你的偏好。

e.en: A good reader {infers} tone even from short text messages.
e.zh: 优秀的读者即使从简短短信中也能读出语气。

e.en: Years of overfarming left the soil {infertile} and cracked.
e.zh: 多年的过度耕种让土壤变得贫瘠龟裂。

e.en: The clinic helps couples who fear they may be {infertile}.
e.zh: 该诊所帮助那些担心自己不孕不育的夫妇。

infertility.t: n. 不孕不育；土地贫瘠

e.en: New treatments offer hope to couples struggling with {infertility}.
e.zh: 新疗法为饱受不孕不育困扰的夫妇带来了希望。

e.en: Soil {infertility} forced the village to import most vegetables.
e.zh: 土壤贫瘠迫使村子大部分蔬菜都得依赖进口。

infest.t: v. (害虫等) 大量出没；成灾

e.en: Termites can {infest} a wooden house within a single season.
e.zh: 白蚁可以在一个季节内就侵扰一栋木房子。

e.en: Bots {infest} the comment section of every viral video.
e.zh: 机器人充斥着每一条爆款视频的评论区。

e.en: The kitchen had a serious cockroach {infestation} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天厨房里蟑螂横行,问题严重。

e.en: Farmers sprayed crops to control the locust {infestation}.
e.zh: 农民喷洒农药以控制蝗虫泛滥。

e.en: The old mattress was {infested} with bedbugs.
e.zh: 那张旧床垫里满是臭虫。

e.en: These waters are {infested} with sharks year-round.
e.zh: 这片水域常年有鲨鱼出没。

e.en: Medieval crusaders branded their enemies as {infidel} forces.
e.zh: 中世纪的十字军把敌人称作异教徒势力。

e.en: The extremist group labeled outsiders as {infidel} threats.
e.zh: 该极端组织将外人视为异教徒威胁。

e.en: She filed for divorce after discovering his {infidelity}.
e.zh: 发现丈夫不忠后,她提出了离婚。

e.en: Marital {infidelity} is a common theme in classic novels.
e.zh: 婚姻中的不忠是经典小说常见的主题。

e.en: The shortstop covered the {infield} with impressive range.
e.zh: 那名游击手在内场的防守范围令人惊叹。

e.en: Rain soaked the {infield} before the game started.
e.zh: 比赛开始前,大雨浇湿了整个内场。

e.en: He's the most reliable {infielder} on the team.
e.zh: 他是队里最可靠的内野手。
